News.title: Celebrity Traitors prize money: What does the winner get and how much are stars paid?
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The second season of Celebrity Traitors is in full flow, with a huge prize pot up for grabs.

The star-studded cast, which includes Michael Sheen, Maya Jama, Ross Kemp and Miranda Hart, are all being paid for their participation – and according to reports, the celebrities are paid a flat fee of £40,000 for appearing in the series.

On The Rest Is Entertainment podcast in July 2025, host Marina Hyde said: “Look at the calibre of the people they got. They were able to pay everybody a blanket 40k fee, right? They’re paying them a 40k fee.”

open image in gallery Claudia Winkleman is back for more 'Celebrity Traitors' ( BBC )

However, rugby player Joe Marler said this varies from star to star as he was paid £30,000 to appear on last year’s series.

The BBC declined to comment on the fee when asked by The Independent.

As for the prize money, the celebrities will be competing for up to £100,000, with the exact figure depending on how well the celebrities perform in each challenge.

Unlike the regular version, where the contestants keep the jackpot, the celebrities will give their prize winnings to a charity of their choice.

In the civilian version of the game of deception, a slightly higher total prize of £120,000 can be won by the contestants.

Much like the civilian version, Claudia Winkleman is also the host of the celebrity series.

Also appearing on the series this year are comedians Joe Lycett, Rob Beckett, Romesh Ranganathan, Joanne McNally and James Acaster, the latter of whom is convinced that last year’s winner Alan Carr has ruined comedians’ chances of reigning supreme.

“I think we’re going to be the first ones under the magnifying glass being looked at – particularly at the beginning when you have absolutely nothing to go on,” he told the BBC before filming the series earlier this year, calling it a real “concern”.

Elsewhere, the series has a contestant unlike any before, with mathematician Professor Hannah Fry bringing her statistical expertise to the game in a bid to sniff out the suspicious contestants.

The full list of celebrities taking part in the series can be found here.

News.title: Pensioners ‘spending their children’s inheritance to go on more holidays’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Older people are spending their money to go on more holidays rather than leaving it to their children or losing it to inheritance tax, a senior figure in the travel industry has said.

Recently-released data from Abta, the UK’s largest travel trade association shows that 82 per cent of over-65s had been on holiday in the past 12 months, a rise of five percentage points from two years ago.

The number of over-65s holidaying abroad has risen to 55 per cent, which represents a percentage point increase from two years ago.

Mark Tanzer, Abta’s chief executive, told The Times that the spike could be attributed to a willingness to spend money which could have become inheritance for their children.

“I think that generation is probably fitter than it used to be; your mortgage is paid off, you are starting your pension, you are actually quite cash rich compared to a young family starting out,” he told the newspaper.

“I think they have got more disposable income and they want to have experiences, there may be a bit of them thinking, ‘I just don’t want to leave this to my kids’, but they certainly don’t want to leave it to the taxman. I think there’s that sense of ‘well if I don’t spend it, it will just go to inheritance tax’.”

According to The Times, this idea is known as ski-ing, meaning “spending the kids’ inheritance”.

Spain was the most popular overseas destination for the age group with 43 per cent visiting the country. The US and Turkey were also popular, with city breaks and beach holidays regular choices among over-65s.

open image in gallery Benidorm is one of the most popular Spanish destinations with Britons ( AFP/Getty )

However, Abta’s report, called Holiday Habits, found that holidays remain a spending priority among the British people and fewer people are looking to cut back on them over other non-essentials such as dining out, buying clothes or other leisure activities.

Its data suggested that there was a bit more caution when it came to holiday spending due to the increased cost of living.

Holidays remain far down the list in terms of what people are willing to cut back on, but the gap between them and other areas of spending has tightened.

Abta’s polling showed 23 per cent of people would cut back spending on UK holidays, while 32 per cent would look to cut back on holidays abroad.

In his forward to the report on the data, Mr Tanzer wrote: “Behind the headline figures, it has been a tough year for the travel industry.

“The conflict in the Middle East shook the sector, not just in terms of the initial disruption to travel, but also the ripple effects of changes to fuel supply and prices.

“How we travel to and through the Middle East has changed and there does not appear to be an immediate resolution of the disruption on the horizon.

He added: “Perhaps, though, it is the cost of living – more than anything – that has been the constant challenge shaping customer behaviour. While people do continue to spend on travel, they are leaving it much later to departure before committing to their holiday. It is a pattern that is becoming regular for travel businesses, adding increased pressure and unpredictability.”

News.title: Astronomers find the first ever green star
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Astronomers have found the first ever green star, in a study that shows white dwarves can actually come in a wide array of different colours.

The colour of most stars is decided by their colour: when they are cooler, they are orange, whereas our own warmer Sun is white, and the very hottest are a pale blue. Previously, researchers had thought that white dwarves – the remains that are left behind after stars like our Sun die, would work in the same way.

But new research suggests that, despite their name, white dwarves can actually come in a wide array of colours. If we were able to get up close with them, they would come in pink, cyan, yellow, purple – and even green, according to the authors of the study, who found the first such example ever seen.

“Most stars, including most white dwarfs, behave like ‘perfect radiators,’ so their colour is set almost entirely by temperature. But nobody had really looked into what else might be possible for white dwarfs,” said Mark Hollands, from the University of Warwick, who led the work. “It turns out these incredibly dense stars can produce colours nobody expected, and some of them genuinely surprised me."

White dwarves are unusual because they are so dense, the researchers say: they are millions of times denser than the outer shell of the Sun, roughly the same as water. That density means that any elements that might be around are able to interact with the plasma in the white dwarf, absorbing light across many more colours.

As such, those white dwarves are not those perfect radiators. Instead, they will reflect the chemical makeup of the material that are around them.

There is not a white dwarf near enough for us to see its colour. Instead, researchers int he new study calculated it, using data about its spectrum, the “fingerprint” that can be found by splitting starlight apart into its different wavelengths.

Scientists were then able to run that data through a model that simulates how the light would look to a human who was looking at them. As such, they were able to calculate the stars’ true colour.

It showed that the colour is decided by the material in the star’s atmosphere, putting them in different groups. Those with lots of carbon will appear pink or purple, others that are surrounded by pieces of old planetary systems will look yellow, and cooler ones with hydrogen and helium atmospheres will be blue.

But researchers were most excited by WD J1330+6435, a white dwarf that is about 4,000 degrees Celsius and has taken on rocky material from the planetary system for which it was once the Sun. That material has added calcium, lithium, and sodium to the atmosphere, making it glow with a chartreuse green.

It is the first star of that colour ever found, the researchers say.

“The traces of sodium in the atmosphere of this white dwarf absorb the orange part of the spectrum, leaving behind a ghostly green glow,” said Dr Hollands.

Imagine standing on a planet and looking up at a green star. It feels like something out of science fiction."

They also found what they believe to be the reddest star ever seen. WD J1011+2845 is relatively nearby – just 48 light years away – and carbon is being lifted up to its surface which then distorts the light so that almost all of the light is squeezed into particular wavelengths that make it glow a deep salmon-pink.

Most of the white dwarves that are nearby are still white. Of the 151 examples in the study, which are all within about 65 light years of Earth, five of them were unusually coloured, with two yellow and three pink.

The remaining 146 averaged out to be a cool white. But even that helps adjust our understanding of their colour: astronomers previously believed that white dwarves are generally blue, but that is because those examples are brighter and so can be seen from further away.

The work is reported in a new paper, ‘Any colour you like: The diverse chromaticities of white dwarfs’, published in the journal RAS Techniques and Instruments.

News.title: Former DUP leader Jeffrey Donaldson jailed for 15 years over historical sex offences
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Former DUP leader Jeffrey Donaldson has been given a 15-year jail sentence for a series of historical sex offences against two women when they were children.

Judge Paul Ramsey told Newry Crown Court that Donaldson, 63, had shown no “regret, apology or shame” after he was convicted of 18 offences, including one count of rape, earlier this year.

The judge told Donaldson he had “doubled down on his denials” since his conviction for the offences committed between 1985 and 2008.

“There has not been, and doubtless will not be, one word of regret, apology or shame from this man to at least provide his victims with some crumb of comfort,” he said.

He said Donaldson had achieved many things in his political career but had now experienced a “catastrophic descent into disgrace”.

open image in gallery A prison van transporting former DUP Leader Sir Jeffrey Donaldson arrives at Newry court house ( Getty )

Telling the former MP to stand before passing sentence, the judge told Donaldson: “You are now 63 years of age. It is well known that you in the course of your political career have reached the very heights of public office, and this is, on any view, a catastrophic descent into disgrace.

“It is only through the courage, resourcefulness, and determination of two young women that you’ve been brought to justice in respect of the crimes you committed against them when they were children.

“You persistently denied these offences and continued to do so, but you’ve been found guilty by a jury, and it’s now my duty to sentence you for these crimes.”

The former Lagan Valley MP has been in Maghaberry Prison in Co Antrim awaiting sentencing since the end of the trial in June.

The two victims gave evidence against him during the trial.

Complainant A gave evidence of inappropriate touching and kissing by Donaldson and an incident where he used a light to examine her genitals.

Complainant B told the trial she had been raped as a child of primary school age by Donaldson and later sexually assaulted by him.

Donaldson had denied the offences but the jury convicted him of one count of rape, 13 counts of indecent assault and four counts of gross indecency.

Since his conviction, Jeffrey Donaldson has been stripped of his knighthood and removed from the Privy Council.

His solicitor has previously confirmed that papers have been lodged for an appeal.

His wife Eleanor Donaldson, 60, was found to have aided and abetted his crimes after a trial of the facts, which was granted on mental health grounds.

She cannot be given a prison sentence but could be given a treatment order or an absolute discharge.

The judge is due to decide on this at a later date.

She has also lodged an appeal against the outcome of her trial of the facts.

News.title: Expert explains what happens to your money if you die without a will
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Dying without a will is a dangerous business. You risk your money going to the wrong person, leaving dependants struggling and, in extreme cases, your assets going to the Crown.

Yet only 37 per cent of Brits have written a will, according to the National Wills Report, down from around 50 per cent in the past.

“Most people know they should write a will, but many never get round to it,” says Adam Vanstone, chartered financial planner at Chester Rose Financial Planning.

“Partly that’s because nobody likes confronting their own death, but mostly it’s because they don’t understand what happens if they don’t.”

So, here’s what could happen if you die without an up-to-date will in England and Wales.

Married, with or without children

There are different rules depending on if you have children or not, and even their age.

Without kids, for example, your spouse gets everything, free of inheritance tax (IHT). They can also use your unused tax-free allowance when they die, as long as they make a will themselves. The surprise here is that your parents and siblings get nothing.

If you have adult children, however, things can change.

“The spouse will not automatically inherit everything,” says Brett Dixon, vice president of the Law Society of England and Wales. “Instead, they receive a set amount and share the rest with their descendants. This continues to be the case even if they are an estranged spouse.”

Your husband, wife or civil partner gets your personal possessions and the first £322,000 of your estate. Half of anything above that goes to them and the other half is shared between your children.

That means your children could end up owning part of your home, drawing it into a child’s divorce or debts, or leaving them pushing for a sale.

Invest at least £100 in Stocks or ETFs of your choice. Get fractional shares worth £50! Terms and conditions apply. Go to website 

open image in gallery October is Free Wills Month - many solicitors offer the simple service ( Getty Images )

Much can depend on how you own the property: If you own it as joint tenants, your share passes automatically to your spouse, will or no will. If it’s in your sole name or you own it as tenants in common, your children could inherit part of it.

There could also be an IHT bill on the children’s share, which a will leaving everything to your spouse could have deferred.

If you have young children, there are again different considerations.

“Where children are under 18, they cannot inherit their entitlement outright,” says Andrea Jones, national head of private client advisory at Irwin Mitchell. “Instead, their share is held on a statutory trust until they reach adulthood.

“This can create ongoing administrative responsibilities and costs for the family and often requires additional trustees to act alongside the surviving parent, which many families wouldn’t have chosen had a will been in place.”

Cohabiting couples

If you die with no will and live with a partner you are not married to, your partner will inherit nothing with your estate going to your children, if you have any, or your parents and siblings if not.

“There is a ‘common law marriage’ myth, in which the law will treat you the same as a married couple if you act like one,” says Dixon.

“This is not the case. Cohabitants do not have any automatic rights on intestacy. Without a will, your cohabiting partner will not automatically inherit anything.”

Your partner can make a claim on the estate through the courts, but it’s slow, costly and uncertain. If you own your home as joint tenants, though, it passes to them automatically.

Second marriages

“Intestacy can produce particularly harsh outcomes for blended families,” says Jones. “A surviving spouse is prioritised under the intestacy rules, meaning children from a previous relationship may receive less than expected or, in some cases, nothing immediately.

“This can often create tension between family members and may be very different from what the deceased would have wanted.”

For example, Bob has two children, Robert and Roberta, from a first marriage and then marries Olive. If he dies with an estate worth less than £322,000, everything will go to Olive. If it’s worth more, Olive gets the first £322,000 and half the rest. Robert and Roberta share the other half.

In simple terms: If you remarry, write a new will. Marriage usually cancels an existing one.

open image in gallery Dying without a will can lead to unintended people benefiting and create administrative headaches too ( Getty Images )

Separations and living solo

If you separate from your partner, but are not divorced, writing a will or updating an existing one should be a priority.

Die without an up-to-date will and your estranged spouse will inherit, no matter how long you have been separated.

“The misconception that separation ends inheritance rights can lead to unintended outcomes, particularly where the deceased had formed a new relationship or intended their assets to pass elsewhere,” says Jones.

On the other hand, if you are single and without children when you die without a will, your estate will go to your parents, then your siblings (or their children), then grandparents, then aunts and uncles (or their children).

And if there are none of those, it goes to the Crown. Your friends, godchildren or anyone else will get nothing.

“Making a will ensures your estate passes how you intend - whether that is to family, friends or charities,” says Dixon.

Free Wills Month

October is Free Wills Month, when anyone aged 55 and over can have a simple will written or updated for free by a participating solicitor.

It’s a good deal if your affairs are straightforward. But if you have young children, a blended family or a large estate, it’s worth paying for proper advice.

A basic will from a solicitor costs around £150 - perhaps not a lot to pay, for the knowledge that you aren’t leaving a mess behind you when you die.

News.title: Julia Stiles brings Save the Last Dance co-star on stage for Dance with the Stars routine
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

It’s been a quarter of a century since Julia Stiles starred as ballet hopeful Sara in Save the Last Dance, but it seems she’s still got the moves after paying homage to the film on Dancing with the Stars.

Stiles, who is competing on the 2026 series of Strictly Come Dancing’s American cousin, recreated memorable moments from her character’s much-memed final dance routine – and even brought on co-star Sean Patrick Thomas for a cameo.

Paired with professional dancer Ezra Sosa, Stiles performed a Jazz routine to a remix of Jennifer Lopez’s “Jenny from the Block” as part of the show’s Super Bowl Night theme. The pair incorporated moves from the dance number that Stiles performs in Save the Last Dance, which sees her character perform ballet with a hip hop twist in her audition for the prestigious performing arts school Julliard.

Mid-way through the DWTS tribute on Tuesday (13 October), the cameras even cut to see Stiles’s Save the Last Dance co-star Thomas, recreating the often-parodied moment where his character Derek, Stiles’s love interest in the film, is seen nodding his head in approval of Sara’s audition.

Just like the shot from the film, Thomas stood in the wings of the theatre with his jacket over his shoulder at the side of the stage, nodding along to the music while Sosa copied him.

The routine earned the pair a score of 24 from the three judges, placing them second on the leaderboard behind ex-Love Island star Maura Higgins and her partner Mark Ballas, who also happens to be the son of Strictly head judge Shirley Ballas.

Fans were full of praise for the nostalgic dance routine, with one person writing in the video’s comments on YouTube: “Seeing Sean in the audience and giving a node to Save the Last Dance was absolutely EVERYTHING!! I can’t believe that it’s been 25 years since the movie came out i love that iconic movie so much.”

Another wrote: “She ate and left no crumbs,” while a third commented: “Aaahhhhhh Patrick Thomas there doing his signature move of approval.”

Sean Patrick Thomas and Ezra Sosa recreated the scene from 'Save the Last Dance' ( ABC )

Released in 2001, Save the Last Dance follows teenager Sara as she moves to a new school following the death of her mother, and falls back in love with dance with the help of new boyfriend Derek (Thomas).

While the dance film was originally panned by critics, it has become a cult classic over the last few decades thanks to Stiles’s final routine, which has gone on to become a meme. In 2023, the actor made a cameo as her film character on Saturday Night Live, joining then-cast member Chloe Fineman to recreate the dance live on air.

Next week’s episode of Dancing with the Stars will see Stiles perform a contemporary routine to Frankie Valli’s “Can’t Take My Eyes Off You” in honour of Heath Ledger, her co-star in 1999’s 10 Things I Hate About You. The Australian actor died in 2008 from an accidental drug overdose at the age of 28.

News.title: Republicans turn America’s love of meat into bizarre midterm election battleground
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Amid ongoing debates over inflation and conflict in Iran, an unexpected culinary battle line has been drawn in the midterm elections, turning dietary habits into a political testing ground. Candidates across the country are increasingly using meat consumption to signal their cultural and economic credentials.

The latest dispute flared up in Mississippi, where Democratic Senate candidate Scott Colom released a campaign  highlighting a broadcast clip of Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith. Responding to voters concerned about soaring beef prices, Hyde-Smith noted that "you know you have so many proteins to choose from."

The video cuts directly to a man at a backyard grill who responds: "Pick another protein? I'd rather pick another senator instead."

open image in gallery As Democrats and Republicans argue over high prices and the Iran war, they're also having a food fight over who's the most red-blooded carnivore ( M&S )

The Mississippi contest is unusual in that a Democrat is using beef prices to attack a Republican.

Across much of the rest of the country, Republicans have taken the offensive, labeling Democratic rivals as vegans or opponents of meat production in an effort to present them as culturally out of step, hostile to local farming interests, or lacking traditional masculinity.

In Texas, Republicans highlighted a past interview in which Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico described his campaign going vegan during a previous run for the statehouse. Talarico has since made a point of publicly consuming local barbecue to counter claims that his personal diet makes him unsuited to represent the state.

In Colorado, Republican attacks have targeted Democratic congressional candidate Manny Rutinel over his past involvement in animal welfare activism.

open image in gallery In Texas, Republicans highlighted a past interview in which Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico described his campaign going vegan during a previous run for the statehouse ( AFP/Getty )

While in college, Rutinel posed shirtless with a banner supporting People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals. In 2021, he founded Climate Refarm, an organization focused on reducing meat consumption that signed onto letters calling for higher taxes on meat and dairy products.

He also backed a failed 2024 ballot initiative intended to ban a Denver lamb slaughterhouse.

Rutinel, 31, is challenging Republican Rep. Gabe Evans in Colorado's 8th congressional district, an area containing extensive ranchland, dairy operations, and major meat processing plants, including the headquarters of beef giant JBS Swift.

GOP opponents have repeatedly criticized Rutinel over his plant-based stance, leading conservative media outlet Daily Wire to release undercover footage of a campaign staffer claiming Rutinel eats meat "as little as possible."

Rutinel has sought to dismiss the issue, frequently eating steak tacos while campaigning. "I don't think Coloradans care about what's on my plate, I think they care more about what's on theirs," Rutinel stated following a recent campaign event.

open image in gallery Democrats have also seized on meat, though primarily as an example of household essentials growing more expensive under Trump ( Getty )

Evans maintained that the controversy involves policy rather than personal choice. "I don't care what he eats personally," Evans said during an interview. "I care that he wants to use the power of the government to make everyone eat that way."

Republicans have leveled similar criticisms against Democratic House candidates in other states. In Iowa's 2nd district, a region dominated by swine farming, Lindsay James faced scrutiny for supporting "meatless May" in a 2020 Facebook post.

In Arizona's 1st district, Democratic candidate Amish Shah has been targeted over his long-standing vegetarianism and animal rights advocacy.

Elsewhere in Iowa, Republican Senate candidate and current Rep. Ashley Hinson criticized her Democratic opponent, state lawmaker Josh Turek, for opposing legislation to ban the sale of lab-grown meat in the state. "He’d rather have meat that comes from a lab than from our family farms," she told supporters at a campaign stop.

Democrats have also seized on meat, though primarily as an example of household essentials growing more expensive under Trump. To curb rising costs, Trump tried to lower market prices by expanding beef imports from foreign suppliers, particularly Argentina, whose government is led by a close ally.

However, those imports sparked backlash from domestic cattle producers while doing little to lower consumer prices, creating potential political vulnerabilities in agricultural states.

Bureau of Labor Statistics data shows the average price of ground beef reached $6.79 per pound last month, up from $5.55 in January 2025, when Trump returned to office.

This economic context framed Hyde-Smith's original comments, a cattle rancher and former state agriculture commissioner. Colom, the local prosecutor who delivers the final line in his campaign spot, faces a difficult race in Mississippi.

Responding to the , Hyde-Smith's campaign attributed the rising cost of living to Democratic policies. "It is Scott Colom who supports Biden-era policies that drove up inflation," said spokesman Nathan Calvert.

News.title: Coronation Street star warns fans over bombshell storyline
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Coronation Street star Bethany Fallon has warned fans her latest storyline is “not going to end well” after her character’s bombshell pregnancy news.

Tuesday (14 October) night’s episode ended with the revelation that Bethany Platt is pregnant after a one-night stand with her mum Sarah’s boyfriend, Kit Green (Jacob Roberts).

“It's not going to end well, because it's her mum's ex-boyfriend's baby!” she said. “I don't actually know what Bethany was thinking when she slept with Kit – I think they both were in quite a bad place at the time.”

The surprise pregnancy comes at an already difficult time for the Platt family, as Sarah (Tina O’Brien) is about to stand trial for murdering Theo Sliverton (James Cartwright), having been revealed as the killer after a murder mystery storyline earlier this year.

open image in gallery Fallon as Bethany Platt ( ITV )

Fallon, 30, also shared her shock at learning of the pregnancy storyline from the show’s producer Kate Brooks, adding that when she “was telling me what was happening and then she said that Bethany ends up being pregnant, my jaw was on the floor!”

The actor admitted she’s worried about how fans will feel towards Bethany too. “I think they're going to be annoyed at her and think that she's just really stupid, which she is for what she's done!” she explained. “But there were two people involved here, so I'm hoping she doesn't get all the blame…"

In the coming episodes, viewers will see Bethany – who is in a relationship with Ryan Connor (Ryan Prescott) – consider whether to get a termination, while Sarah’s murder trial continues.

“I feel like she’s in so much shock and she can’t imagine having this baby,” Fallon continued. “But then maybe there’ll be outside influences if people find out and maybe that will change things.”

What Fallon does know is that Bethany won’t be sharing the news with her mum anytime soon. “I think right now it’s deny, deny, deny,” she said. “Coming clean is not an option, especially if she wants to keep a relationship with her mum because her mum would have the right to never speak to either of them again. I mean the whole family would, it's not even just Sarah. So she’s stuck in an impossible position right now.”

open image in gallery Sarah is on trial for killing the abusive Theo ( ITV )

Kit is also at the centre of another huge storyline, having been diagnosed with stage three breast cancer.

Bethany Platt has been reintroduced to the cobbles multiple times since teenage mum Sarah gave birth on screen back in 2000.

Fallon began playing the character in 2015 and during her tenure, Bethany has been at the centre of several big storylines, including a grooming and sexual exploitation plot in 2016.

open image in gallery Kit is undergoing treatment for cancer ( ITV )

Elsewhere on the cobbles, a long-running dementia storyline will end next year. Debbie Webster, played by Sue Devaney, was diagnosed with the condition on the soap in 2025.

Devaney will leave the show as part of the hard-hitting plot – and it was previously reported that she felt “blindsided” by the exit news.

The actor first joined the soap in her teens in 1984 and her original stint lasted for just one year. She was brought back in 2019, aged 52, which made her think: “This is nice. I could end my career on Corrie, and I’d be very happy.”

Devaney added to The Sun: “I don’t know what I’m doing after I’ve done where I am. Nobody knows – we just have to make the best of every day, don’t we?”

News.title: Ukrainian Vampire drones drop food on town besieged by Russian army
News.content:
On Ukraine’s front lines, drones are the deadliest weapons in Kyiv’s arsenal, hunting Russian soldiers one by one with chilling precision.

But across the Dnipro River, the same machines have been given a very different mission: keeping trapped civilians from dying of starvation.

Since March, Ukrainian drones have been flying food and medicine into occupied Oleshky, on the river’s left bank, where residents are surviving on grass and weeds.

The town is less than three miles from Kherson, a city battered by Russian drones and shelling.

Since December, Oleshky has been under an effective blockade. Its roads are mined and shops have closed, with no food arriving by road since late May. Humanitarian agencies are blocked from entering, and the health system has all but collapsed.

Only around 2,000 of its 24,000 pre-war residents remain. For them, the drones are now their only lifeline.

“With the onset of winter, the situation is only getting worse,” said Elvina Osmanova of the Kherson regional military administration. “Food supplies are running out. People are facing a life-threatening choice: risk their lives trying to find food outside the city or remain without food.”

News.title: Man City dismantled by PSG in breathless Champions League battle
News.content:
When Manchester City play like this what a loss their football will be to the Premier League – and the Champions League – if they are heavily sanctioned later this season.

In what turned out to be a match for the ages, a night of brilliant, unbridled attack, we were treated to the ultimate game of two halves as the back-to-back European champions Paris St-Germain took City apart for 45 minutes. And then were left holding on.

City will hope this is a sign of what is to come in their Premier League fight. But with a different result. After suffering a resounding defeat at the hands of the Premier League’s independent commission, with 114 of the 115 charges against them proven, they maintain their innocence and are mounting an appeal.

Could they make a comeback? It would be incredible and highly improbable if they did so but, out on the pitch, and 3-0 down after a first half in which they were in danger of being humiliated by PSG, they created enough opportunities to save themselves.

The data backed that. City’s expected goals (xG) was 2.57 while PSG’s was 1.83. City had 27 shots to 15 and had more possession and more passes. Enzo Maresca made a triple substitution to devastating effect, especially with the introduction of new signings Ayyoub Bouaddi and Iliman Ndiaye.

In the end they clawed back two goals, both scored by Erling Haaland, who now has 61 in 60 games in this competition – seventh outright in the all-time list, before Ruud van Nistelrooy. And 37 of those for City, overtaking Sergio Agüero’s club record.

News.title: Barcola starts to justify £123m price tag with hat-trick as Liverpool hit LASK for six
News.content:
Of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season, Liverpool have the friendliest league-phase fixtures and they can secure back-to-back wins against Austrian side LASK in this evening’s early kick off.

Having already vanquished one of their pot one opponents by beating Atletico Madrid at Anfield, Andoni Iraola’s team really should be targeting one of the top spots.

They travel to Linz without some key players, though. Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai missed the defeat by Manchester City and remain sidelined, while Hugo Ekitike is a long-term absentee.

There were positive aspects to Liverpool’s performance against City, but they collapsed like a deck of cards after Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh second yellow card.

Tonight’s game is one they should dominate, and it is a presentable opportunity for Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola to kick-start their seasons and respond to the recent criticism of their performances. Iraola hopes to have a stronger squad to choose from at the weekend, when Liverpool face a stringent test at Brentford. This is the second of nine matches in 28 days for Liverpool.

“You don’t have a lot of time to train,” said Iraola. “You try to prepare the games now a lot of times just with the videos and the tactics boards, just a little bit outside. You have to prioritise the freshness of the players.

“Especially now we are playing four games in 10 days, it’s keeping all the legs, all the energy in the games.

LASK are currently third in the Austrian league, but booked their place in this season’s Champions League proper with a remarkable comeback from 4-0 down on aggregate against Celtic.

They have injury problems of their own to contend with George Bello and Moses Usor limping off in the weekend’s defeat by league leaders Rapid Wien and Ramiz Harakate tearing his anterior cruciate ligament in July.

They do play on a grass pitch at the Raiffeisen Arena though Kasper Schmeichel, the former Celtic goalkeeper who was working as a TV pundit for the game, was critical of the playing surface.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Second Ebola case confirmed in Kenya
News.content:
Kenya has recorded its second-ever case of Ebola after a relative of a patient who died last week tested positive for the virus, officials have said.

A 39-year-old man fell ill on Tuesday and has since been confirmed to be infected with Ebola, according to Kenyan health authorities.

The patient, who is now isolated, is a family member of Kenya’s first-ever Ebola case, who died in a hospital in Nairobi last Monday.

The index case, a 40-year old businessman, had travelled to Kenya from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the epicentre of the deadly outbreak of the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, which has so far killed more than 4,300 people.

Kenyan authorities have identified 128 of his contacts and have successfully tracked down 113 of them, who are having their temperatures checked daily for a period of three weeks, the country’s Director-General for Health, Dr Patrick Amoth, said in a statement.

“There is no evidence of spread in the wider community,” the statement, issued on Wednesday, added.

However, questions remain over whether more cases will crop up in the coming weeks.

News.title: I tried Apple’s new smart home hub – the brand faithful will love it
News.content:
HomeView can control smart lights, heating, security cameras and video doorbells via touch or voice, but devices must support Matter – the cross-brand smart home standard. That means you aren’t confined to Apple-approved gadgets, but you are still limited – Ring video doorbells, for example, aren’t Matter-compatible, so they won’t work with HomeView, which could be a deal-breaker for even the biggest Apple fan.

But for anyone put off by the complexity of setting up a smart home, Apple is trying to simplify things. It has partnered with LG on Home Collection – a range of devices, including security cameras and a video doorbell – that connect with a single tap, just as AirPods do with an iPhone. They won’t be available until later in the year, but they could mark a major step towards making smart home set-up less complicated.

My early verdict

HomeView is built for the Apple faithful: set-up requires an iPhone or iPad, personalised AI features need a recent Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone, and some apps work only when your phone is nearby. In a household split between iPhone and Android, Android users will get a much thinner experience, and Apple’s own services come first at every turn.

Still, HomeView is the most polished smart display I have seen. Face recognition makes it both a great shared and personalised device; the sound quality is excellent; and Siri AI is finally worth talking to, especially when it can draw on your personal context. I’ll need to live with it for a few weeks before giving a final verdict, but so far it’s a beautifully designed device I’d be happy to invite into my home.

News.title: Ed Miliband calls for ‘new deal on debt’ as developing countries face spiralling borrowing costs
News.content:
Ed Miliband, the foreign secretary, has called for a “new deal on debt” as spiralling borrowing costs force developing countries to spend more on interest payments than on education or health.

In a speech in Bangkok on Wednesday, Mr Miliband warned that the global financial system is failing emerging markets, and promised to use the UK’s diplomatic heft to push for urgent reform.

He said: “The short-term repayments are crippling, and while many are not defaulting on their payments they are being forced, if you like, to default on the lives and prospects of future generations.

“So we need a new deal on debt, a deal that supports countries to repay over longer time horizons and, crucially, refinancing with better rates to give developing countries precious fiscal space.”

Although public debt is not inherently problematic, servicing costs are at a 25-year-high – squeezing government coffers just as conflict, climate change and a ‘Godzilla’ El Niño push food and fuel prices ever higher.

Emerging economies in particular have little headroom: according to the Rockefeller Foundation, average interest payments now exceed 10 per cent of revenue in developing nations, while UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD) analysis found 3.7 billion people live in countries where debt servicing costs exceed spending on health or education.

At the same time, overseas development aid (ODA) spending from wealthy countries has plummeted – hitting social, infrastructure and humanitarian projects, and disaster response.

The mounting global debt pile has dominated discussions in Bangkok this week, where some 15,000 people have descended for the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank annual meetings.

This included the first meeting of the newly formed Borrowers’ Platform on Monday. A group of finance ministers and central bank governors from some 30 countries, it was formed to exchange ideas about how to deal with debt burdens – and how to avoid pitfalls.

News.title: Trump backs down in Zambia mineral and data-sharing row
News.content:
Zambia has signed a five-year health financing agreement with the US government after the US dropped demands for access to sensitive health data and separated the deal from negotiations over the country’s mineral resources.

The agreement follows months of negotiations over a $2.49 billion health aid package, with Zambia pushing back against US demands to share medical data and give preferential access to the country’s rich mineral reserves in exchange for money to provide lifesaving healthcare.

Under the final agreement, Zambia will not be required to hand over individual patient records or biological specimens, which the US had previously argued was important for global disease surveillance.

Data sharing will be restricted to monitoring and evaluating US-funded health programmes.

A separate agreement covering US access to Zambia’s critical minerals has also been decoupled from the health financing deal, it was confirmed last week.

“The government will not be sharing any specimens with the United States because we removed all those aspects that raised concern,” Zambian Health Minister Roma Chilengi said last week as the agreement was signed.

Zambia’s Foreign Minister Mulambo Haimbe also confirmed that the health and mineral agreements had been separated.

“There was this [memorandum of understanding] on health and another on critical minerals, and we were saying that these need to be decoupled, and this has been done,” he said.

News.title: Progress against HIV stalls in South Africa, research shows
News.content:
South Africa’s progress in tackling the Aids and HIV crisis has stalled in one of its most populous provinces, new research has found.

The number of new cases of the infection in KwaZulu-Natal province, centred around the eastern port of Durban, have stopped falling after years of steep declines.

Data from a long-running study following thousands of people also showed those with detectable levels of virus in their blood had risen slightly despite years of medics prescribing antiretroviral drugs.

Researchers said the peer-reviewed study published in The Lancet HIV medical journal “provides a stark warning on prevailing HIV trends in rural South Africa, where ground is being lost in the fight against the HIV epidemic”.

The researchers, led by scientists at Durban’s Africa Health Research Institute (AHRI) and Stellenbosch University’s South African Centre for Epidemiological Modelling and Analysis (SACEMA), used a 20-year study which has tested nearly 60,000 people.

Analysis showed that after steep reductions in HIV incidence from 2013 to 2018, incidence rates for both males and females showed little or no decrease from 2019 onwards.

Incidence rates had continued to fall for young people under 35, but that had been offset by a lack of progress for those in middle age.

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez makes incognito entrance to Man Utd training as Jason Wilcox arrives after star’s bombshell blast
Sports.content:

DISGRUNTLED Manchester United stars and chiefs arrived back at Carrington for training following their dismal defeat in Spain.

Conceding inside one minute, a red card and a player revolt summed up a horror trip to the Spanish capital as Atletico Madrid collected their first ever win over an English opponent in the group or league phase of the Champions League with a 2-0 win.



If another poor performance on the pitch wasn’t enough to dull supporters’ mood, then Lisandro Martinez’s explosive rant at Old Trafford bosses certainly was the icing on a pretty awful tasting cake.

SunSport exclusively revealed how United stars are divided over the defender’s comments, which saw him openly question technical director Jason Wilcox and slam the lack of backing for the manager and squad in the summer.



Martinez, 28, expressed how he expected more from the technical director and sensationally said they “don’t have the best squad compared to other top teams”.

While the fallout from those comments continues, inside the club it has to be back to business as usual as Michael Carrick and Co arrived back for training ahead of their Premier League clash against Leeds at the weekend.

The main culprit of the new frenzy around the club ironically made an incognito entrance as he ducked out of sight in the back of a Toyota Aygo.

Sports.title: Parents spending over £1,200 a year on fuel to take kids to play sport
Sports.content:
Next

Parents of sporty kids spend on average £1,216 a year on fuel getting their children to training and matches, racking up some 1,716 miles.

A study of 2,000 mums and dads who take their child to play sport found they spend an average of three hours, 22 minutes a week chauffeuring their amateur athletes.



Football was found to be the most common sport these parents drive their children to, with 61 per cent saying they regularly transport them to training sessions and matches, followed by swimming (40 per cent), and dance (18 per cent).

Meanwhile, 74 per cent claimed they have had to miss out on something important to them, such as a social event, birthday or work commitment, as they prioritise their children’s sporting endeavours.



For most, the Sunday morning drive is something they expect to look back on fondly rather than gladly leave behind, with 77 per cent saying they’ll miss it when they no longer have to do it.

While 72 per cent also believe the time spent driving has positively impacted their relationship with their children.



Farrell Hsu, managing director for Chery UK, the car company which commissioned the research, said: “Grassroots sport plays a hugely important role in young people’s lives.

“These findings show just how much dedication is required from parents behind the scenes, with parents logging an average of more than 1,700 miles a year behind the wheel to enable their children to take part.

“Football is by far the most popular activity these parents are driving to, and as the official automotive partner of AFC Bournemouth, we see just how sports bring families and local communities together.

“While managing work, personal commitments and travel costs is a constant balancing act, these car journeys have been shown to provide important bonding time for parents and their children, from early morning training sessions to weekend matches.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The research also found the biggest issues parents had with the driving were traffic congestion (28 per cent), fuel and travel costs (26 per cent) and balancing it with work (21 per cent).

In fact, 36 per cent have gone as far as skipping a meal or eating on the move to ensure their child makes it on time, while 34 per cent have had to leave work early.

Nevertheless, for most it’s a job worth doing, with 91 per cent agreeing their child taking part in grassroots sport has positively affected them beyond just their physical health.

Confidence (66 per cent), teamwork (63 per cent) and social skills (56 per cent) were the qualities most had seen improve in their children thanks to playing sports.



And for parents, the things they enjoy most about the role are seeing their child enjoy it (74 per cent), their child keeping active (71 per cent) and it supporting their mental wellbeing (55 per cent).

The biggest things which could make travelling to sporting events better would be lower fuel or charging costs (41 per cent), better parking (38 per cent) and more local training and competition venues (24 per cent).

Meanwhile, the most useful vehicle qualities and features for sporting commitments are good fuel economy (40 per cent), easy-to-clean seats and surfaces (31 per cent), comfortable seating (30 per cent), and plenty of boot space (28 per cent).

Overall, 78 per cent of parents cover up to 49 miles a week getting their children to and from training, matches and competitions, according to research carried out through OnePoll.com.

While, on average, parents of children who play sport drive typically 33 miles a week, implying most of this driving happens in shorter bursts rather than long journeys.



Chery spokesperson, Farrell Hsu, added: “With parents spending an average of more than £1,200 a year of fuel, and more than three hours a week sitting behind the wheel, running costs and travel time will inevitably take a real toll on busy families.

“What stands out in the data is how local this driving is.

“For most parents, a full week of training runs and weekend fixtures comes in under 50 miles.

“For anyone able to charge at home, that has the potential to take a real bite out of the annual fuel bill.”

Sports.title: From record flop to Wag attack and trying to join LIVERPOOL, Martinez is latest Argentine to ruffle Man Utd feathers
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED and Argentine players have a long and difficult history.

The Red Devils have signed eight in all, with many totally backfiring.



Lisandro Martinez kept that trend going with his bombshell outburst slamming the club’s transfer dealings.

United have certainly had more than a handful of players from Argentina who proved to be a handful.



Legendary former boss Sir Alex Ferguson claimed he “found working with Argentinian footballers quite difficult”.

He added: “There was deep patriotism towards Argentina. They always had the flag round them.

“I had no problem with that, but the ones I managed didn’t try particularly hard to speak English. With Veron it was just, ‘Mister’.”

“Although he made spectacular contributions, he simply couldn’t play in our teams. He played in every position. I could have coached him for a hundred years without knowing where to put him.”

SunSport has taken a look at the eight Argentines to play for United and how they got on.

Juan Sebastian Veron

There were big expectations on Veron when he arrived at Old Trafford from Parma for £28million – which was a British record fee – in 2001.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But he struggled to adapt to the Premier League and couldn’t quite figure out his best position – as Sir Alex admitted.

Veron played 82 times for the Red Devils across two seasons and won a Prem title in 2002-03.

While his versatility helped the team in parts, he didn’t fit into United’s system tactically, with the likes of Roy Keane and Paul Scholes much preferred.

He was eventually sold to Chelsea in August 2003 for around £15m.



Gabriel Heinze

Things started off great for Heinze, who won plaudits among fans for his tough-tackling displays and fighting spirit after joining from PSG in 2004.

He played 39 times in his first season as he became a key player – but a serious knee injury forced him to miss most of the 2005-06 season.

Heinze then lost his place at left-back to Patrice Evra, who was signed from Monaco midway through the season.

But he wasn’t happy to become second choice after returning to fitness and later ruffled some feathers by trying to force a move to United’s bitter rivals Liverpool.



United chief David Gill initially agreed to let him go if Liverpool met their £6.8m asking price – which they did.

But Sir Alex blocked the move and Heinze eventually left for Real Madrid the following season as his spell with United ended on a sour note.

Carlos Tevez

Another star who enjoyed such a great start before a bitter end.

Striker Tevez actually joined United on a two-year loan deal from West Ham.

He formed part of a lethal frontline at United alongside Wayne Rooney and Cristiano Ronaldo and became a real crowd favourite as he bagged 19 goals in his first season.



Tevez was clinical in front of goal and helped the Red Devils win two Prem titles and the Champions League.

His second season wasn’t quite as prolific as his first as he only managed five goals in the Prem, but he still finished with 15 strikes in all competitions.

Then came one of the most controversial moments in top flight history as Tevez opted to join cross-town rivals Man City in a £47m move.



And who could forget that infamous ‘Welcome to Manchester’ sign to mark his controversial arrival that infuriated United fans.

Angel Di Maria

The attacking midfielder was one of the most high-profile signings in the post-Fergie era when he was signed from Real Madrid for around £60m in 2014.

But he summed up United’s strategy under CEO Ed Woodward of splashing the cash on big-name players who didn’t always deliver.

And Di Maria was certainly one of those players as he only lasted just season at Old Trafford.

His quality definitely showed in parts as he registered three goals and 10 assists in the English top flight.



But it was clear he didn’t like his surroundings and found it hard to adapt to life in the UK. He had periods of inconsistency and off-the-pitch issues, including a shock break-in at his home in January 2015.

He ended up leaving for Paris Saint-Germain at the end of the season after failing to win silverware.

And his wife Jorgelina Cardoso later complained how their time in Manchester was a “nightmare”.

She slammed the “disgusting” food and told of how she initially refused to move to the city.



Marcos Rojo

The defender spent seven years at United after initially joining in 2014 from Sporting Lisbon after an impressive World Cup with Argentina.

On the face of it, his spell could be seen as a success as he won the FA Cup, Carabao Cup and Europa League.

But his time at Old Trafford was marred by constant injuries – summed up by the incredible stat that he played just 76 Prem games between 2014 and 2021.

There will be no questions about his attitude and tenacity when he did make it onto the pitch after finishing his United career with 122 appearances.

But he simply wasn’t someone United could depend on enough.



Sergio Romero

One of the few Argentine stars United will look back on with fondness.

Romero was signed to be the team’s back-up keeper in 2015 as he reunited with his old AZ Alkmaar boss Louis van Gaal.

The fact that pressure was taken off his shoulders from the get-go helped his case as he primarily worked as David de Gea‘s understudy.

But when he was called upon, he usually came up trumps as he kept 39 clean sheets in 61 appearances overall.



And supporters will recall how he was the team’s No 1 keeper throughout their successful Europa League campaign in 2016-17.

He started 12 matches in the tournament under Jose Mourinho and lifted the trophy after United’s 2-0 win over Ajax in the final.

Romero earned a reputation as one of the best back-up keepers in Europe before leaving the club in 2021.

Lisandro Martinez

Signed from Ajax by his old manager Erik ten Hag to bring a wave of new signings to Old Trafford.



There were initial worries that he wasn’t the right frame for the Premier league as Jamie Carragher once claimed he was “too short” to be effective in duels.

He did go on to prove him wrong with some impressive physical displays to continue his reputation as ‘The Butcher’.

Martinez has made 115 appearances so far in his United career that has seen him win two trophies.

But his time in Manchester has been blighted by injury issues, inconsistency and – more recently – outspoken behaviour.

Martinez’s time with the club threatens to end on a sour note after criticising the hierarchy over their failure to strengthen the squad.



And he risked alienating his team-mates by claiming the team were not good enough for top European competition.

United are now faced with a big decision on his future in the coming months.

Alejandro Garnacho

A once talented star who came through the youth ranks at Old Trafford and tipped to follow in Cristiano Ronaldo’s footsteps.



His breakout season in 2022-23 brought 34 appearances and five goals.

The following campaign saw him net a stunning overhead kick strike against Everton that put him on the map as he finished the season with 10 goals in all competitions.

But his final season with United was a difficult one as he fell out with manager Ruben Amorim after being accused of a poor attitude.

He irked his boss after storming down the tunnel having been subbed off at half time against Ipswich.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And the final straw appeared to be when he was benched for the Europa League final defeat to Tottenham.



After the game, he claimed their 2024-25 season had been “s*****” and he was sold to Chelsea for around £40m that summer.

Sports.title: Football legend renowned for iconic hair looks completely unrecognisable after shaving head
Sports.content:
Next

FORMER Colombian international Carlos Valderrama has parted ways with the trademark afro hair that made him one of the most instantly recognisable footballers in the world.

The 65-year-old retired attacking midfielder let his wife Elvira Redondo cut off the long locks that accompanied him throughout his playing career and after he hung up his boots.



He posted a video of the memorable moment on his Instagram, saying in a message accompanying the video: “My people. Today is the day.”

Valderrama, regarded as one of the best Colombian footballers of all time, appeared to have some doubts before his partner got to work, saying: “More or less” with a ‘so-so’ hand gesture as she asked him whether he was ready.





But he still had a smile on his face as Elvira finished up and said: “Imagine what the grandchildren are going to say when they see you with your hair shaved off.”

Valderrama looked more like fictional New York police detective Kojak than the man whose precise passing and technical skills made him one of South America’s most recognisable footballers in the late 1980s and early 1990s.

And his wife couldn’t resist a laugh as she presented him to his army of fans with his new look and joked: “Baldy Valderrama.”

It was not immediately clear today why the footballer, who revealed in April he had rejected an offer of DOLLARS two million dollars before the 1994 World Cup to cut his trademark hair, had opted for the transformation.



One fan, referencing the footballer by his nickname of El Pibe which in English would be ‘The Kid’, responded by saying: “When you’re good looking, you’re good looking. It really suits you.”

Another added: “Legend with or without the mane.”

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Valderrama’s wife also added her own comment on Carlos’ Instagram, saying affectionately: “My love, you look beautiful and I love you however you look.”

The former Colombian national team captain insisted when he revealed the six-figure haircut offer he wouldn’t have accepted it even if DOLLARS five million had been on the table.



He said: “I decide my life. I was always like this. I answer for my history. It is my history.”

Valderrama, named by Pele in the FIFA 100 list of the world’s greatest living players, was a member of the Colombia national team from 1985 to 1998.

He represented his country in 111 full internationals, making him the fourth most-capped player ever.

He played for Colombia in three FIFA World Cups and five Copa America tournaments.

After spending most of his career playing club football in South America and Europe, towards the end of his career Valderrama played in Major League Soccer, joining the league in its first season.

Sports.title: Jags QB Lawrence finally hitting lofty heights expected from No 1 pick
Sports.content:
When the Jacksonville Jaguars selected Trevor Lawrence with the first overall pick in the 2021 NFL Draft, they were looking for a franchise saviour.

The Jags were coming off a 1-15 season, and an astonishing 11 losing campaigns out of the previous 13. They are one of just four teams in the NFL to have never played in a Super Bowl.

Conversely, Lawrence arrived having won 34 of his 36 games in college and 52 of 54 in high school. He was supposed to bring those wins to Florida.

Safe to say, that did not happen. As a rookie, he was thrown right in and lost more games in five weeks than he had in five years.

The Urban Meyer head coaching experiment was a disaster and Jacksonville managed just three wins that year.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Jacksonville Jaguars beat the Philadelphia Eagles in London - and the last few minutes did not disappoint!

Lawrence and the Jags' campaigns in the subsequent three years under Meyer's replacement Doug Pederson were a mixed bag that included a playoff win, but ultimately a 4-13 season saw Pederson fired.

Enter Liam Coen, longtime NFL quarterback coach and offensive coordinator who was poached from Tampa Bay in January 2025. Coen's arrival, and Lawrence's development during his tenure, have put the 27-year-old in the mix for NFL MVP and the Jags up there as Super Bowl contenders.

What do the numbers say?

Since the start of last season, the Jaguars have won 17 games out of 22, tied for the best regular-season record in the league. Despite a heart-breaking final-minute defeat to Buffalo in the postseason, year one for Coen ended with the second-best record for the Jags in franchise history (13-4).

Lawrence's ascension was a large part of that, but he may be getting even better - and the 4-1 Jags have started out hot.

Last year, he offered the volume, but not the efficiency. He finished sixth in passing yards (4,007) and fifth in touchdowns (29), but only 28th in completion percentage (60.9), 20th in quarterback rating (91.0) and 16th in yards per attempt (7.2). He was an MVP finalist.

This season, he is playing at a higher level - and getting the ball downfield. After five games, Lawrence is fourth in quarterback rating (106.3), eighth in completion percentage (67.1), and fifth in yards per attempt (8.2) along with 1,174 yards (14th) and 10 TDs (tied fifth).

What has actually changed?

Image: Jacksonville Jaguars head coach Liam Coen is getting the best out of Lawrence

Sam Darnold. Jared Goff. Baker Mayfield. There are plenty of examples of high quarterback draft picks who struggled for large parts of their careers before finding success in the right situation. The expectation is that everything will click immediately, but that is simply not the reality for most QBs.

If you're the best in college, you're most likely joining the worst teams in the professional game, and it can take years for the stars to align.

Through the early period of Lawrence's NFL career, it would be no surprise for NFL RedZone's coverage to turn to Jacksonville and show a quarterback running for his life. You would see him scrambling around to avoid pressure, throwing from awkward positions... playing 'hero ball', essentially.

Now, watch Lawrence and you'll see cool, calm, composed and importantly, assured. He knows where his feet should be, where his eyes should look and where his teammates will be at any given time. Coen has been crucial in helping Lawrence find a rhythm.

Look no further than Lawrence's stunning fourth-down throw to Parker Washington against the Eagles on Sunday. Feet, eyes, timing... touchdown.

Lawrence was slicing and dicing, dinking and dunking his way to 331 yards against Philadelphia, and it's becoming a common occurrence.

The supporting cast

Lawrence has not been blessed with an 'alpha' receiver so far in his career. No disrespect to Marvin Jones, Christian Kirk, or Calvin Ridley but these aren't names you'd want to provide an elite quarterback. Brian Thomas Jr had an instant impact as a rookie in 2024 but has since dropped off, giving way to last season's top option: Washington.

Image: Parker Washington has developed into Lawrence's go-to target

In the 24-year-old, the Jaguars have found a gem. Sixth-round picks don't usually make too much of an impact, let alone develop into a team's top target by their fourth year.

Washington's one-handed grab in London showed the trust Lawrence has in him. According to ESPN, since Week 11 of last season, Washington has 17 catches for a league-best 381 yards on third and fourth downs. He was Lawrence's top target by a clear distance in that lone playoff game last year.

Lawrence is tremendous at spreading the ball around to multiple receivers, but Washington tops the team with 22 catches, 352 yards and four TDs so far this campaign after doing the same last year (58-847-5). Don't be surprised to see more games like last Sunday (6-124-2).

It would be an oversight not to mention Jacksonville's improved defense at this point. Since Coen took over and brought defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile with him, the Jaguars have only allowed 18.5 points per game, behind only Seattle and Minnesota. This year, that number is 14.0 with only the Vikings (12.8) performing better.

They will be crucial for the Jags to make a deep run this season.

What comes next?

The Jaguars continue their London visit this Sunday, facing the desperation-mode Houston Texans at Wembley, live on Sky Sports. Houston started 0-4 but won last week and need a victory to keep their season alive.

The game is one of four divisional games for Jacksonville in their next six. If we are talking about a serious contender, this is a chance for Lawrence and company to show their credentials.

If you ask someone who their Super Bowl favourite is this season, they are most likely to say the Buffalo Bills, San Francisco 49ers, Kansas City Chiefs or Seattle Seahawks. How long before the Jaguars are one of the first teams mentioned?

Sports.title: 'Top two - why not?' - Why Sangare turned down top clubs for Brentford
Sports.content:
Mamadou Sangare could have been playing Champions League football this week. After all, the signs point to him being an elite-level player.

Not only did the midfielder star for RC Lens last season - playing a key role as they finished as Ligue 1 runners-up and French Cup champions - but there were major European clubs eyeing up his signature over the summer.

And not just major clubs, the elite of the elite. Yet he turned those bigger clubs down for a Brentford team without European football this season.

"Yeah it's true," he tells Sky Sports from Brentford's training ground about that interest. "But I'm not going to give any names, out of respect.

"There were a lot of clubs. For me, the most important thing was to know where I could progress. And Brentford was the best place for my development.

"A coach who really wanted me was something that was important to me. That's why I chose Brentford."

It is fair to say Sangare had earned a big move. As well as his club success with Lens, he was also named in the Ligue 1 Team of the Year at the age of 24, pipping Paris Saint-Germain duo Joao Neves and Fabian Ruiz to a midfield spot.

So was it hard to say no to some of the major European clubs? "No, it wasn't difficult," he replies.

"Just because a big club comes calling, it doesn't mean you have to say yes to it. You have to see a lot of different aspects.

"I'm a little different from other players because I see things differently. For me, Brentford was the best option - as a young player, as a player who still has to prove himself at a high level.

"I think that choosing Brentford was the best option for me to progress and to reach my best potential."

'I'd never seen an approach like that' - Sangare on Brentford's pitch to him

If Sangare wasn't a coup for Brentford when he joined, he was definitely one after his Premier League debut. He got two assists as the Bees hammered Tottenham on the opening weekend, but the way he strutted around with ease in his first Premier League game made him a star for the future already.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Brentford and Tottenham Hotspur

"He can play for a top four club," said Jamie Redknapp after that display. And the big question everyone had was: how do Brentford keep on spotting then securing future gems in the making?

The key is in the preparation when it comes to Brentford, who pitch the club to incoming players via a very detailed presentation.

Bryan Mbeumo recently revealed how thorough Brentford's pitch can be. The Bees watched him 28 times for Ligue 2 side Troyes before approaching him in 2019, then presented him with all his strengths and weaknesses on a screen.

Because of this presentation, he had a clear idea of where he'd fit in, where he'd improve - and seven years later, he was sold to Manchester United for £71m. He had gone from a French second-division player to scoring 20 Premier League goals in a single season for the Bees.

And for Sangare? "It was exactly the same," he says about the presentation that Brentford gave him over the summer.

"It was incredible. It was the first time I've ever seen something like that. I've been at a few clubs, but I've never seen an approach like that.

"Brentford has a well-placed structure. It was something I've never seen before - it really pushed me to choose this club.

"I had a positive, detailed discussion with the coach. He showed me his style of play and what he expected from me.

"He also showed me the tools which could allow me to improve. He showed me my weaknesses and what I needed to work on. I'm a young player, I really liked that.

"When a coach speaks to you like that, it shows that he wants to see you improve. It was really important for me."

However, not all roads are straightforward in football. Despite being the new darling of Brentford, he has started the last two games against Chelsea and Aston Villa on the bench.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brentford fans have come up with a brilliant new chant for summer signing Mamadou Sangare

There is no injury. Instead, he is competing with the trustworthy pair of long-term servants Vitaly Janelt and Mathias Jensen for a midfield starting spot. Yehor Yarmoliuk is another up and coming option in that position and scored at Villa. Sangare has had to wait his turn after such a high-profile start.

"I haven't spoken much about that with the coach," Sangare says about his recent appearances on the bench. "He's the coach, he's the boss. I'm a player like so many others. It's not only about me here.

"The most important thing is the team. That's what counts. Whether I start or not, as long as they need me, I'll be there.

"It's up to me to work even harder to get my place back, even though I wouldn't say that I lost it. It's up to me to keep working and to do even more than the others. We'll see how it goes."

Despite his limited appearances in recent weeks, Sangare has still shown his worth. He averages the most tackles out of any Premier League player per 90 minutes, while only Man City's Elliot Anderson has won more duels on the ground than the Mali midfielder.

Image: Mamadou Sangare is still one of the standout defensive midfielders in the league this season

With the calibre of player like Sangare in the team, it makes Brentford such a hard team to beat. They are still unbeaten in the Premier League this season, having beaten Chelsea and Tottenham and drawn with Aston Villa.

Liverpool are up next at the Gtech Community Stadium on Saturday, having been stung by Keith Andrews' side in this fixture last season. Even though they have never played a European match before, Brentford are a continental club in the making.

'Why can't Brentford reach top four, or top two?'

Sangare managed to defy all the odds at Lens last season, taking them to Europe and winning them a cup. That would be the perfect tonic for Brentford fans this season - who have never won a major trophy in their history.

But with Brentford sitting fourth in the table after six games, Sangare's message is clear: Europe is not enough.

"The goal is to reach Europe and win as many games as possible," he says. "We know that Brentford has never played a European game before.

"Why can't we also reach the top four, or the top two? Why can't we cause a real surprise? Because we're a good team in the league. We have a very good team with very good players, with a great coach as well."

Those are the team's ambitions. What about his own? After his performances for Brentford already this season, many have branded him as the next player off the conveyer belt, after the Bees brought in nearly £200m for Mbeumo, Yoane Wissa, Ivan Toney and David Raya.

"I saw some comments about that," says Sangare about transfer rumours linking him with a move away already. "I don't think too much about it. I just want to work and help the team to reach their goals.

"They put a lot of money in me. They trusted me. It's up to me to do everything to make it happen - by winning games, by improving the team.
