Sports.title: Kiss vows Wallabies will 'return fire' vs All Blacks | Rennie: Quality win was coming
Sports.content:
New Zealand vs Australia: Les Kiss vows Wallabies will 'return fire' vs All Blacks in Bledisloe Cup Test | Dave Rennie: Quality was coming

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of New Zealand vs Australia in the first Bledisloe Cup Test at Eden Park Highlights of New Zealand vs Australia in the first Bledisloe Cup Test at Eden Park

Australia head coach Les Kiss has vowed the Wallabies will "return fire" against the All Blacks in Saturday's return Bledisloe Cup Test in Sydney, live on Sky Sports.

Last week, Australia's six-Test unbeaten run came to a shuddering halt when New Zealand ensured they will retain the Bledisloe Cup for a 24th year after powering to a 50-19 victory over the Wallabies at Eden Park.

A competitive first half, perhaps even edged by Australia, saw the All Blacks three points ahead at the break as the sides traded two tries each.

But the second half proved altogether different, as the All Blacks added five further tries in a display of clear dominance.

"It's like anything. You get a knockback, you find out more about yourself and that's what we'll do. We'll work hard on what we have to do," said Kiss.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player New Zealand performed their famous haka before facing Australia at Eden Park last Saturday New Zealand performed their famous haka before facing Australia at Eden Park last Saturday

"Belief is created and sustained by not just wins and losses, they're created by other things. These boys have a strong culture, a strong belief in themselves and a confidence about what they can do.

"But the lessons are there: if you can't get your strengths going and their strengths grow, it makes it a difficult game.

"We'll go back and we'll work on what we have to and try and turn the dial in the right areas that can go to Sydney and return fire."

⁠Australia face some injury issues and will be without ​key centre Len Ikitau, who ​left Saturday's game in the first half ⁠with a head knock, while Hunter Paisami has been suspended.

Jordan Petaia ⁠is also unavailable due to ​an ankle injury, with Corey Toole ​and Kadin Pritchard joining the camp.

Australia team for second Test Starting XV: 15. Tom Wright, 14. Max ⁠Jorgensen, 13. Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii, 12. Isaac Henry, 11. Harry Potter, 10. Declan ​Meredith, 9. Ryan Lonergan; 1. Aidan Ross, 2. Josh Nasser, 3. Allan Alaalatoa, 4. Jeremy Williams, 5. Lukhan Salakaia-Loto, 6. Rob Valetini, 7. Fraser McReight, 8. Harry Wilson (c)



Replacements: 16. Billy Pollard, 17. Angus Bell, 18. Massimo De Lutiis, 19. Josh Canham, 20. Carlo Tizzano, ‌21. Kalani Thomas, 22. Harry McLaughlin-Phillips, 23. Filipo ​Daugunu.

Joseph-Aukuso Sua'ali'i moves from the wing to outside center in place of Ikitau, with Harry Potter returning on the left wing.

Declan Meredith will start at No 10 in place of Ben Donaldson, who sustained a leg injury during the first Test in Auckland.

There are also two changes in the front row where former All Black Aidan Ross will start at loosehead and Josh Nasser, a tryscorer last weekend, is named at hooker.

The uncapped Harry McLaughlin-Phillips has been named on the bench.

"Over the last five Tests, we didn't lose the run of ourselves; the boys always said we've got work to do. It doesn't change now," Kiss said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Wallabies picked up a stunning victory over South Africa in Perth last month, finishing with just 11 players The Wallabies picked up a stunning victory over South Africa in Perth last month, finishing with just 11 players

"We'll have a good look at that game, like we have, get into the nuts and bolts of what we need to get right. How do we get our strengths into the game? How do we just nullify their strengths, and that's what we look at.

"We need to make sure we do the work that gets that done. It'll be making sure we get the things that we feel that can make a difference, that's for sure.

"Once they got their momentum, it was hard to wrestle back."

Rennie: Quality performance from All Blacks had been coming

For the All Blacks, four players have been ruled ‌out of Saturday's Test in ‌Sydney.

New Zealand will be without hooker Asafo Aumua and back-row Anton Segner after both failed ​their second head-injury assessments (HIAs).

Flanker Ethan ⁠Blackadder has picked ⁠up a calf injury, and wing Leroy Carter has been ‌ruled out due to a high ankle sprain, which he suffered while scoring a ‌try in the second half.

Prop George Bower comes in to start at loosehead, lock Fabian Holland will play next to Scott Barrett in the second row and Josh Moorby is named on the left wing. There are five further changes among the replacements.

All Blacks team for second Test Starting XV: 15. Beauden Barrett, 14. Will Jordan, 13. Quinn Tupaea, 12. Jordie Barrett, 11. Josh Moorby, 10. Damian McKenzie, 9. Cam Roigard; 1. George Bower, 2. Codie Taylor (c), 3. Fletcher Newell, 4. Scott Barrett, 5. Fabian Holland, 6. Tupou Vaa’i, 7. Peter Lakai, 8. Wallace Sititi, 9. Cam Roigard



Replacements: 16. Samisoni Taukei’aho, 17. Xavier Numia, 18. Pasilio Tosi, 19. Shannon Frizell, 20. Du’Plessis Kirifi, 21. Cortez Ratima, 22. Timoci Tavatavanawai, 23. Rieko Ioane

"I thought a quality performance was coming, but we're also playing a really good side," said New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie.

"So the arm wrestle in the first half [vs Australia at Eden Park], I thought we probably left a couple of opportunities out there, and then they scored late."

New Zealand's Leroy Carter is one of four players out through injury for this weekend's contest

Rennie, who coached the Wallabies for three seasons before being dismissed in favour of the ill-fated return of Eddie Jones in 2023, pinpointed a couple of specific areas he feel turned last week's Test in the All Blacks' favour.

"We did a good job looking after the ball, and we played in the right parts of the field. Created good momentum and pressure and benefited from that.

"We're happy. We talked about a number of areas that needed to be better coming out of South Africa, and we saw good shifts. We're confident in our ability, and we felt in Africa that we just lost key moments.

"We had a really good edge around training, and we were well aware of the importance of winning and also the Bledisloe Cup. So it was nice to nail that."

A tight first half was eventually blown open by the All Blacks at Eden Park

The All Blacks head coach admitted the 31-point defeat at Eden Park won't define this Wallabies side under Kiss, and he expects a stronger performance in Sydney.

"Yeah, look, it's a tough end for them, but it was nice to catch up with a number of those guys post-game. Oh, they'll be hurting.

"They've had a really good year, and I'm confident they'll bounce back next week. Look, I'm very happy with the mindset and the work ethic brutality, and it was spot on."

Sports.title: Martinez releases statement to clarify outburst - but does not apologise
Sports.content:
Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has clarified his outburst after Tuesday's Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid in a statement - but stopped short of an apology.

Martinez launched an extraordinary attack on the club's hierarchy after the 2-0 defeat in Madrid, as he criticised the lack of summer investment in the squad, said he expected more from "upstairs" and singled out technical director Jason Wilcox.

But 24 hours on from his astonishing post-match interview, the Argentina international released a statement on Instagram on Wednesday night to clear up his comments.

He said: "Following everything that has been said about my comments yesterday, I want to share some thoughts on what I said and how I feel.

"After the match, I spoke out of anger and frustration at not getting the result we all wanted.

"Those who know me know how I live football, with passion, commitment and a huge desire to win. And when things don't go our way, it hurts, especially when representing a club with the history and stature of Manchester United.

"My words reflect how I feel and how much I want to see this club competing for the biggest honours. Those high standards are part of how I see football and the responsibility that comes with wearing this shirt.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kaveh Solhekol and Rob Dorsett answered your questions about Martinez's post-match outburst

"When I talk about wanting more, I'm talking about the ambition we must all have as part of this club. To keep growing, to become stronger and to have everything we need to compete at the highest level. These are standards we must all hold ourselves to, starting with me.

"I know that, first and foremost, it's us, the players, who have to deliver, and I put myself at the front of that responsibility. We need to demand even more of ourselves and work together to take Manchester United back to the top.

"I believe in my team-mates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward. I'm convinced that the way forward is to keep working together, with ambition and commitment.

"My goal has been the same since day one, to win, to compete at the highest level and to give everything I have for this badge."

Sky Sports News' Football Correspondent Rob Dorsett:

There are real doubts about whether Martinez's contract will be extended when it expires in the summer.

United will focus on revamping their defence in the next transfer windows and have the formal option to prolong Martinez's stay for a further year.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie O'Hara criticised Martinez following comments made by the defender aimed at the Manchester United hierarchy

Sky Sports News has also been told United are looking at new centre-backs, as well as left-backs.

United's bosses have yet to decide whether to discipline Martinez for his comments, when he said: "I expect more from our technical director [meaning director of football, Jason Wilcox]. We expect more from the top, from upstairs, to bring in more players to compete."

Sky Sports News has been told there is anger and bemusement at what Martinez said, both in the United boardroom and in the changing room, with at least one other player challenging him over his comments as the squad got on board the plane to fly back to Manchester.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Soccer Special pundits react to Lisandro Martinez's comments aimed at Manchester United's hierarchy after their Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid.

It is also understood that there is no pressure on Wilcox internally regarding his position.

The implication that Martinez doesn't think his team-mates are good enough to compete has not gone down well with other players.

Martinez has been keen on a move away from Old Trafford for some time.

In the summer, he pushed for a move to Atletico Madrid, the side that beat United in the Champions League on Tuesday night, to follow his good friend and international team-mate, Cristian Romero, who left Spurs for Spain.

No suitable bid for Martinez came in for Manchester United to consider.

The 28-year-old made similar explosive comments about his bosses when at Ajax in 2022. Martinez, who again wanted a move away, called their sporting director Gerry Hamstra a "nobody".

Martinez remains a key part of Michael Carrick's squad and United's bosses know they have to handle this situation carefully.

Sports.title: Wardley: Davison could help AJ with 'inside knowledge' of Fury
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley suggested trainer Ben Davison could help Anthony Joshua with "some inside knowledge" going into his fight with Tyson Fury.

Trainer Davison has previously worked with Joshua and Fury, but he will be in Joshua's corner for their long-waited heavyweight showdown at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff on December 11.

Wardley, the former WBO heavyweight champion who also works with Davison, understands Joshua's reasoning.

"Your trainer, irrespective of working with people previously is a huge factor going into the fight," Wardley told Sky Sports News.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Wardley tells Sky Sports he was on the brink of victory over Dubois but became a 'victim of his own success'

"There will be some inside knowledge, however applicable that is and however it's used in the fight, maybe, maybe not. It always depends on the fighter you have in front of you.

"You play to their strengths, not to the opponent's weaknesses."

Fury called Davison a "traitor" but former world champion George Groves didn't consider that fair.

"Of course he's not. He's worked with almost all the heavyweights and I'd imagine Fury left Davison rather than the other way round. It's just more banter, not that the fight needs it," Groves told Sky Sports.

Joshua has recently worked with Oleksandr Usyk's training team before bringing Davison back to his corner on fight night, but Groves thinks Joshua has made the correct decision.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dubois says he would fight the winner of Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua

"When they're in the corner and he needs some advice maybe Ben Davison giving it to him feels a little bit more familiar than it does from, say, an Usyk Team or an American rent-a-coach or one of those guys," Groves said.

"You can find more established, on paper better coaches than Ben Davison but sometimes if crisis hits you want to have a familiar voice so that's why Ben Davison gets the call.

"It's probably the right move."

Should Fury-AJ be a world title fight?

Wardley can regain the WBO heavyweight title in his rematch with Daniel Dubois on Saturday.

Fury vs Joshua will also have a world title at stake, the WBA 'super' belt, and Wardley hopes he can earn a fight against the winner by defeating Dubois at The O2.

"It is a fight worthy of a world title. Where were they in the rankings, do they perfectly deserve it - that's more a question maybe for the WBA," Wardley said of Fury-Joshua.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joshua says he could KO Fury in a round. Watch back some of his explosive first round KOs!

"Does them two coming together deserve a world title on the line? It probably does. Does it add an extra incentive, an extra bauble for either one of them and for us as a public to speak about it and say if they win they're going to win a world title?

"And then does that mean they then carry on and start to taking on the likes of myself or [Filip] Hrgovic or [Agit] Kabayel or who knows?"

Sports.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
Sports.content:
Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season, given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence.

For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast.

But traducing the messenger will always be easier than hearing the message, even if Martínez’s views are widely shared within the United dressing room. If the fallout from the Manchester City legal case has demonstrated anything, it is English football’s ingrained reluctance to scrutinise the owners and executives who hold more influence over the sport than anybody else. Men in boots, not men in suits. Hey, watch the ball. It’s going to move!

All the same, it’s worth parsing exactly what Martínez was complaining about, because it’s a good deal more complex than it may appear on first viewing. Player calls out board – and specifically “technical director” Jason Wilcox – for failing to invest sufficiently in the squad over the summer. This was a summer in which United brought in three midfielders (Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba), a reserve goalkeeper (Karl Darlow), nobody up front and nobody in defence. So far, so simple.

But let’s begin to unpick the threads. Why did United not buy a defender in the summer, despite pursuing deals for Lewis Hall and Myles Lewis-Skelly? Because they were unable to sell a defender. There was no interest in Diogo Dalot or Noussair Mazraoui, nor in Harry Maguire, nor in Luke Shaw or Martínez, whose contracts are up next summer in any case. This is the product of recruitment decisions made and deals signed years ago. But why do United, one of the world’s most lucrative clubs, need to sell to buy in the first place?

Perhaps for the same reason they baulked at the asking price for Elliot Anderson and decided to sign the inconsistent Santos and the adequate but overpromoted Tielemans instead: this is a club in austerity measures, whose part-owner Jim Ratcliffe has been furiously cutting costs and raising ticket prices, determined to curb the years of excess that preceded him, where mediocre players were signed on ridiculous money, where failing coaches were paid to leave. But why would United, one of the most commercially successful clubs in footballing history, ever need to cut costs?

Perhaps as a result of the more than £1bn drained out of the club by the Glazers in their 21 years of ownership, not just in dividends but share sales and interest payments on the debt they undertook to buy the club, while neglecting the maintenance of Old Trafford and the training ground at Carrington. Whether he knows it or not, when Martínez is criticising the lack of investment he is in effect holding the Glazers accountable for more than two decades of avarice and mismanagement.

All of which lends a certain significance to Martínez’s intervention that goes beyond the churn of the weekly news cycle. Has any serving United player spoken out so frankly about the ruins of the Glazer ownership? Ole Gunnar Solskjær made a minor stand in early 2005, before they had arrived at the club. Cristiano Ronaldo threw some hand grenades over his shoulder a few days before he left for the second time in 2022. Countless others waited for the safety of retirement, when their disgruntlement could be monetised for personal gain, rather than used to stigmatise them, as Martínez will doubtless be stigmatised in the coming days.

View image in fullscreen A Manchester United supporter shows off a jumper protesting against the club’s owners and executives. Photograph: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images

Does any of this help United to win games in the short term? Almost certainly not. Martínez attempted to clarify his comments in a social media post on Wednesday night. He may still be dispatched to the bomb squad anyway, for the crime of pointing out that the emperor secured his throne almost entirely through the use of payment-in-kind loans.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Inevitably Michael Carrick too will be gone before long, away to the great Overlap podcast in the sky. A few months ago I wrote hopefully that Carrick might be the ideal man to cut through the noise and nonsense. I was wrong. The noise has beaten him; the nonsense always wins; any accumulated credit from last season has long since evaporated.

Of course it’s not Carrick’s fault that United haven’t signed a new defender in almost two years, that Bruno Fernandes is so clearly playing through discomfort, that Joshua Zirkzee is still somehow hanging around the place, that the ownership decided to embark on a purge of season-ticket holders in the summer, generating a huge wave of ill-feeling and apathy that can be felt at Old Trafford on matchdays: an entire fanbase trying to work out whether they actually still care about this.

But accountability is for the little people, and far easier to replace a coach on a modest 20-month contract than to oust Ineos or the Glazers, to replace Wilcox or Omar Berrada, even if we now know they partly built their reputations on the success of a club that has been found to have serially cheated. Bumper returns for the owners, price hikes for the fans, corners cut on the pitch; this is the story of the modern Manchester United, which by no coincidence is also the story of modern football.

Sports.title: European football leaders confident of finding candidate to stand against Infantino
Sports.content:
European football leaders are increasingly confident they will find a candidate to stand against Gianni Infantino in next year’s Fifa presidential election.

One European football association head told the Guardian they were “positive” that Infantino will face an opponent in March, a sentiment echoed by senior figures at Uefa and other national associations before Thursday’s crucial meeting of the Fifa council.

Uefa, Concacaf – the North and Central American and Caribbean confederation – and the Asian Football Confederation have made clear they will oppose Infantino’s re-election bid in the wake of the World Cup sell-off scandal, but have been unable to coalesce around a credible candidate before the 18 November deadline for nominations to be submitted to Fifa.

The respective presidents of the three continental confederations, Aleksander Ceferin, Victor Montagliani and Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim al-Khalifa, have ruled themselves out and suggestions that high-profile figures such as Arsène Wenger or Michele Kang could put themselves forward have been dismissed.

The former Portugal international Luis Figo, the first former player to call on Infantino to stand down in August, has also been mentioned, although he is also regarded as a potential Uefa president when Ceferin’s final term finishes in 2031.

Despite the seemingly limited pool of candidates, sources with knowledge of the anti-Infantino lobby’s plans are adamant they are making progress. One source said whoever emerges will leave it until close to the deadline to publicly declare their hand, to reduce the time for Fifa to scupper their nomination. The rebels believe the Fifa machine is being commandeered to support Infantino’s re-election campaign.

Infantino will be grilled by members of the 37-strong Fifa council on a range of subjects included the abandoned Fifa Forward Enterprise plan, the Fifa peace prize and the Folarin Balogun affair, when Fifa’s disciplinary committee overturned the US striker’s suspension during the World Cup.

In an attempt to preempt criticism of that decision, which followed an intervention from Donald Trump, the recipient for the inaugural Fifa peace prize, Infantino has proposed an amendment that would remove the disciplinary committee’s option to revoke one-match bans received for players shown a straight red card.
