Sports.title: Manchester City are suddenly box-office in age of charge-rage and mega defiance | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
Another day, another note of unreality; another vivid and brilliant spectacle that feels as though it has been whipped together out of meringue and burnt sugar. Time flies when the world is closing in. Two weeks on, this was Manchester City’s first home game since the verdict dropped, the irrefutable body of evidence was refuted, and English football entered its state of ongoing whiplash.

In the stadium this felt like watching someone dance while the world burns. This was a brilliant game pegged out around six goals, a collapse, a comeback, posts and bars struck, saved penalties, and a performance of state-of-the-art omni-football from this brilliantly high-grade PSG team.

Pep Guardiola was even present in the stands, looking oddly haunted beneath a flat cap. Looking in fact quite a lot like Vincenzo Pentangeli in The Godfather Part II, the mute Sicilian brother who turns up in the courtroom and has a congressional hearing dismissed just by glowering wordlessly. Well, it’s the best defence anyone’s come up with yet.

City’s players gave everything against superior opponents. The crowd roused itself from a state of sullen defiance to a state of angry defiance and occasionally even jubilant defiance. At times there was even a resurgence of that euphoric state of the glory years, the collective cognitive dissonance, hard white lights blotting out the sky, nothing out there beyond the spectacle. Take me to the place where you go, where nobody knows if it’s night or day.

There has been some talk in recent days about whether City’s games should be broadcast or even played at all. Is it all just empty, dystopian, an insult to sport? On the other hand, this is by far the most interesting City have ever been. It has been a cold project at times, frictionless football, the hand of a sovereign state at your back, victory without content.

View image in fullscreen Manchester City gave everything but PSG are a brilliantly high-grade team. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Well, not any more. In the age of charge-rage and mega-defiance City are suddenly total box office. No more denials. Just go full Nosferatu. Embrace the darkness. Smear and accuse. Say, yeah OK we did cheat but the real cheat is the rules. This is all deeply gripping main character stuff, performative villainy, like Milton’s Satan in Paradise Lost, who sees the rules, rejects them, and ends up stealing the whole show from boring old rules-obsessed God.

City had perfect opponents here in PSG, who are a kind of twin entity in all this, brothers by another mother. Oil state glove puppets. Twice punished for cheating the financial rules.

But then, nothing explains the world like football. Abu Dhabi versus Qatar in Manchester. Lawfare. Tribal populism. All of it played out against the background of an embattled British prime minister, vultures already picking away at his entrails. Andy Burnham always promised to offer something fresh and different. To be fair he could still be the first prime minister hounded from office because somebody really needed to overpay for Kalvin Phillips.

The Etihad was a febrile place before kick-off. There was smoke, fury, a crackle in the air, and a pointedly heartwarming club heritage video on the big screen, local people looking happy and real, legacy footage of skinny-legged Alfs and Herberts, men with comb-overs in brown overcoats. Then through to the stolen glory years, trophies lifted, last-day title pippings, with the final shouted caption: “The blues are in dreamland.” Yeah. That doesn’t quite sound how you think it does.

Mainly there was a chance here to boo everything and everyone. The PSG team was booed. The singing of the PSG fans was booed. The Champions League anthem was obliterated. A City Till I Die Tifo was hoisted because yes, death must come into it. The early songs were “City’s going down with a billion in the bank”, and the classic “Gary Neville is a wanker, is a wanker”. Whatever happened to not looking back in anger?

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Désiré Doué was sublime on the left, gliding about like a squirrel on a branch. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA

But then, this has always been a project defined by defiance, the raised fist, the punkish V-sign, even if this involves prostrating yourself for the benefit of an inherited billionaire monarchy. The banner that read “Sheikh Mansour, Manchester thanks you for 10 great years” is still there. It was always an odd sentiment. Why were you thanking him back then when the whole thing was self-funding, a sponsorship miracle, beloved of airlines and phone companies? It makes more sense now. Of course. He’s paying for it all.

PSG were brilliant here early on, Luis Enrique was up on his feet in rumpled black tracksuit bottoms and hoodie, handsomely ravaged, like a Jedi out for a jog. And by the time Vitinha made it 3-0 on 32 minutes the score could have been anything. The midfield was suffocating in and out of possession. Désiré Doué was sublime on the left, all fast-twitch spring and balance, like a squirrel on a branch.

And for long periods City’s fans fell silent. You can’t blame them. The sense of grievance may be misdirected, but it is undeniably real. If City’s fans are angry about being overlooked, conspired against, forced to kneel before some distant overlord, well, that’s because they are. Welcome to the world, welcome to east Manchester, welcome to the lighted empty boxes of New Islington, rental engines for an overseas state.

All that love, hunger, connections has been hijacked in the most tantalising way, sold back to you in the form of stolen glory. Please don’t put your life in the hands of a petro‑state propaganda machine, who’ll throw it all away. Here at least they had a brilliant game, players that gave everything, and spectacle if not victory.

Sports.title: My old teammate Miroslav Klose is bucking a trend in German coaching | Philipp Lahm
Sports.content:
You learn the most from the best. The Champions League winners are Paris Saint-Germain, and they could achieve a historic hat-trick this season. Since the tournament’s rebrand in 1992, they would be only the second club to accomplish this feat, after Real Madrid’s run from 2016 to 2018.

I see clear parallels between the two. For Madrid, nine players started in all three of their final victories. Similarly, PSG won their two finals with virtually identical lineups. The only change came during their title defence in Budapest, where Gianluigi Donnarumma no longer featured in goal, Luis Enrique having parted ways with the Italian European champion.

At its core, football has not changed. For two giants of the tournament’s predecessor, the European Cup – Ajax (1971 to 1973) and Bayern Munich (1974 to 1976) – seven players started all three finals. Had injuries not interfered, that number would have been higher. There is a similar pattern in Madrid’s five consecutive wins from 1956, with nine players appearing in at least three of those finals and three featuring in all five. Continuity plus selection: that is the eternal recipe for success.

Today’s elite managers have internalised this, as the numbers prove. We see remarkably similar patterns at PSG, Arsenal and Barcelona. In each case, a core of six to eight players establishes the team’s identity and anchors the XI in crucial matches. The next tier consists of the remaining three to five regular starters, who are pushed by four to six squad players. Thus, the backbone of a squad comprises about 16 players, with the rest providing depth.

Total playing time (roughly 5,000 minutes per season) is distributed as follows:

core players: about 70 to 85% each

remaining regular starters: 50 to 60% each

squad players: 40 to 45% each

fringe squad places: sharing the remaining maximum of 20%

Benchmarking also reveals there is no alternative to the standard operating system: ball-oriented defending. Managers also rigidly adhere to their formations, typically a 4-3-3 or 4-2-3-1. Substitutions are made like-for-like to preserve structural integrity.

Another encouraging trend is that all three clubs reserve a portion of their fringe squad places for at least three young talents, often products of their academies. To test their potential at the highest level, they are given consistent minutes. At Arsenal, 20-year-old Myles Lewis-Skelly seems to be establishing himself permanently.

View image in fullscreen Myles Lewis-Skelly’s progress has vindicated Arsenal’s faith in young talent. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

These principles are enforced over years and across all development levels by the current champions of France, England and Spain. This approach can also be observed at smaller clubs and, in a similar fashion, with national teams such as Morocco. It represents a universal blueprint for footballing success – one heavily influenced by the Spanish coaching philosophy, spearheaded by Pep Guardiola, Mikel Arteta and Luis Enrique.

The most significant deviations from this blueprint can be found in Germany. I see three pieces of evidence pointing to a unique German path. First, man-marking is experiencing a strange revival. Second, many Bundesliga clubs grant fewer opportunities to homegrown talent, despite paradoxically maintaining expensive academies. Third, a vast number of managers have no professional playing background.

These coaches frequently alter systems and formations, before and during matches. At times, they deploy players out of position. The most prominent example was Julian Nagelsmann, who as national coach hindered his side’s development through constant, fundamental changes.

Yet there are exceptions. One is Miroslav Klose. We shared the pitch in more than 80 international matches. He was a magnificent teammate, a true team player who understood his precise value to the group. He is a World Cup winner and was the tournament’s record goalscorer from 2014 until last summer. Naturally, someone with that background possesses a deep understanding of hierarchy, discipline and the tactical awareness of what makes a collective function.

Miro, now in his third season at Nürnberg and sitting in a promotion spot in the 2. Bundesliga, carries the DNA of a great manager. I recognise the methods that lead to success in his work. What sets him apart from many others is that he does not overcomplicate things. He does not tinker with his core system or formation. He identifies who meets the club’s demands and who does not, rarely altering his starting XI.

View image in fullscreen Julian Nagelsmann hindered his Germany team’s development through constant changes. Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters

Through these repetition effects, Miro has identified a core that provides stability. The winger Mohamed Zoma, who made his Italy debut last month, and the attacking midfielder Julian Justvan get about 90% of the playing time, while the central midfielder Finn Ole Becker secured about 80% before a recent injury. The defensive midfielder Adam Markhiev, a Finland international, is practically ever-present when fit. Miro had to rebuild his defence after summer transfers but seems to have quickly settled on his back four.

He also gives youth a chance, sticking by the academy graduates Tim Janisch and Eric Porstner even after mistakes. Since the turn of the year, the young striker Piet Scobel has featured every single week. Miro’s grasp of the club’s identity is also evident in his decision to appoint a local Franconian, the goalkeeper Jan Reichert, as the captain.

The manager’s position at Nürnberg is finally occupied in a way that allows something substantial to grow. Thanks to Miro, the club, stuck in the second tier since 2014 bar a single season, is again capitalising on the potential of their location. FCN have a grand history: only Bayern Munich have won more German league titles. The club legend Max Morlock scored Germany’s first goal in a World Cup final, in 1954.

The club also have immense potential. They benefit from a massive catchment area with virtually no local competition. The huge metropolitan region around Nuremberg, a city with 550,000 inhabitants, is economically robust, and the club boasts a 50,000-capacity stadium that is due for modernisation.

Above all, the club are deeply rooted in their community, supported by a vast and fiercely loyal fanbase. They remain a traditional, member-owned club. To the people here, “Der Club”, as they call it, truly means everything.

Philipp Lahm’s column was produced in partnership with Oliver Fritsch at the German online magazine Die Zeit.

Sports.title: Jackson and Barkley doubles sink feeble Fenerbahce in record Aston Villa win
Sports.content:
It may be a bit early for the pantomime season but the Holte End enjoyed acclaiming their heroes and villains as Aston Villa won at home for the first time this season with their biggest victory in European competition. Every touch for Mason Greenwood, playing his first game in England since January 2022, was booed, but even louder applause was reserved for Aston Villa’s rediscovered attacking prowess.

Johan Manzambi celebrated his 21st birthday by opening the scoring on his first Champions League appearance, before Nicolas Jackson took the game beyond Fenerbahce’s reach with two more goals before half-time to help banish any fears about playing in front of the demolished North Stand.

With Prince William cheering on from the stands, Ross Barkley made this a night to remember as he scored twice, the first goal from a penalty earned by Manzambi, and Tammy Abraham helped Villa score six in a game for the first time since beating Brighton in 2023. No team has won more games (15) in European competition since the start of last season.

Villa’s supposed hex about playing in front of the empty North Stand was put to bed as they scored three times at the end of the ground that is being redeveloped this winter. “Greenwood, Greenwood, what’s the score,” echoed around the three packed stands at Villa Park. Chants of a less salubrious nature were also given regular renditions. This was the former England forward’s first game in this country since he played in Manchester United’s 1-0 win against West Ham United in nearly five years ago.

View image in fullscreen Johan Manzambi scores his deflected goal for the opener. Photograph: Tim Keeton/EPA

Greenwood was charged in 2022 with attempted rape, controlling and coercive behaviour and assault occasioning actual bodily harm. The Crown Prosecution Service discontinued the case in February 2023 after key witnesses withdrew their involvement and new material came to light. The player had denied the charges.

He had played for Marseille in a friendly against Villa 14 months ago, when he allegedly spat at Amadou Onana. So it was no surprise when his name was booed as the teams were announced and at every subsequent involvement.

Far more palatable was the freedom with which Villa played. Jackson now has five goals for Unai Emery’s team since signing from Chelsea for £65m in the summer while Manzambi, a £59.5m capture from Freiburg, was a joy to watch in the No 10 role, combining deft touch with wiry physicality. “My first Champions League game and my first goal, on my birthday,” he said. “My family are here. That’s very nice for me.”

The Switzerland international composed himself to score after Mattéo Guendouzi had inadvertently headed on John McGinn’s cross following a short corner.

Zion Suzuki twice saved well from Vedat Muriqi but Villa created umpteen chances themselves. Jackson, collecting Boubacar Kamara’s pass, struck home cleanly from the edge of the penalty area just after the half-hour mark before repeating the trick six minutes before the interval. In between, Oguz Aydin shot against the Villa bar, but, truth be told, Villa’s 11th successive home win in European competitions was already safely banked.

Villa’s free-scoring spell is in stark contrast to their start to the season, when they only managed one goal in their opening four games. Now they have scored at least three times in four of their past six matches.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Should they beat Viking here next Wednesday, Villa would be well on their way to qualifying from the league stage with nine points from three games. “We are being ambitious,” Unai Emery, the Villa manager, said. “We want to be protagonists in the Champions League.”

View image in fullscreen Nicolas Jackson drills the ball between Nathan Aké’s legs to score Aston Villa’s third. Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/Reuters

Manzambi was tripped by Ismail Yuksek midway through the second half for the penalty from which Barkley made it 4-0, even if Jackson admitted he had fancied the chance to keep the match ball. “Yeah I wanted to take it but the most important thing is we win,” the striker told TNT Sports. “Hopefully next time I’ll get the hat-trick.”

The cheers that followed that goal were promptly matched by the jeers for Greenwood as he was substituted. The pantomime was over as a contest.

Barkley swiftly added a fifth with a deflected shot. But even before Abraham turned in Alysson’s cross for the sixth goal, some Villa minds were turning to Saturday evening’s trip to Newcastle United and the perennial autumnal challenge of resurrecting a difficult start to the league season. In Emery they trust.

Sports.title: Bradley Barcola’s clinical hat-trick inspires Liverpool to 6-3 rout of Lask
Sports.content:
Liverpool cleansed themselves from the stains of defeat by Manchester City at the earliest opportunity. A rampant display in Austria saw Bradley Barcola ignite his Liverpool account with the first hat-trick of his professional career and Andoni Iraola’s team devastate Lask’s big night in the Champions League. The major surprise was how the hosts managed to score three.

Iraola’s pre-match faith in the big-money signings Barcola and Florian Wirtz was repaid as the pair helped dismantle limited opponents. But it was not all about the money and the £123m signing from Paris Saint-Germain scoring the first goals of his Liverpool career. Lewis Koumas registered his first goal in the competition and replaced Steven Gerrard as the youngest player to score and assist in a Champions League game for Liverpool. A total of 26 shots equalled Liverpool’s record in a Champions League away game.

“I’m really happy for Bradley,” said the Liverpool head coach. “Yesterday you were asking me a lot about his numbers, and also Flo [Wirtz], and both of them played really well. They made a difference. Apart from the hat-trick Bradley was a threat one-v-one, helped us control the game and defended the pockets. It will do their confidence good for sure.”

The home end was full and in strong voice over an hour before kick-off as Lask supporters came to savour their club’s first home game in the Champions League proper. The Lask team proved to be much less impressive though, in fairness to the Austrian crowd, their support rarely wavered even as a rout unfolded before their eyes. Liverpool revelled in their superiority and the invitation to recover from Sunday’s first defeat of the season.

Iraola rested Virgil van Dijk, delaying the defender’s 200th game as Liverpool captain, and Alexis Mac Allister as he managed workloads ahead of Saturday’s visit to Brentford. A new-look central defence of Ronald Araújo and Jérémy Jacquet were given a physical test by the Lask strikers Samuel Adeniran and Krystof Danek but handled the host’s rudimental approach comfortably.

View image in fullscreen Bradley Barcola slides the ball into the bottom corner to score his second in the first half. Photograph: Dénes Erdős/AP

Liverpool were utterly dominant against an opponent that struggled to retain possession in all areas of the pitch. The breakthrough was inevitable but also a result of a mix-up in the Lask defence between Alemão and the goalkeeper, Lukas Jungwirth. From the second corner that followed their error, Araújo towered above his marker to head home Kostas Tsimikas’s delivery. It was the Uruguay international’s first Liverpool goal and the start of an onslaught.

Merely 96 seconds later it was 2-0 as Barcola also scored his first Liverpool goal. The summer recruit found himself under scrutiny ahead of the game, along with Wirtz, having gone six appearances for his new club without a goal or an assist. That issue was put to bed when Rio Ngumoha weaved in from the right and Koumas laid the ball back to the lurking winger. Barcola swept a first-time shot inside Jungwirth’s far post. Liverpool were enjoying themselves.

Wirtz soon found himself with a much-needed assist for Barcola’s second goal. The Germany international has looked more at home for Liverpool in the Champions League than Premier League and this was no exception. Wirtz picked out Barcola’s run into the Lask area and the winger rolled a cool finish beyond the exposed keeper.

Lask could have been seriously embarrassed before half-time. Koumas had a fine finish disallowed for offside and, following another neat exchange between Wirtz and Barcola, Ryan Gravenberch’s shot kissed the inside of the far post. Liverpool’s 19 attempts on goal were the most by an away side in the first half of a Champions League game since records began in 2003-04.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Liverpool’s Lewis Koumas jumps for joy after opening his Champions League account. Photograph: Michael Zemanek/Shutterstock

There would be no letup from Iraola’s team after the interval. Jeremie Frimpong morphed into an old-fashioned centre-forward to rise above Yvan Dibango and bury a textbook header into the bottom corner from Tsimikas’s cross. Koumas had a second goal disallowed for offside before Alisson’s clean sheet was ruined by the Lask substitute Robert Ljubicic sweeping home inside his near post. Barcola was presented with his hat-trick when Ngumoha released Frimpong and the full-back flashed a low cross through the Lask six-yard box. Barcola applied a simple finish at the back post.

Frimpong also supplied the assist for Koumas’s deserved goal, converted from close range after the home side were caught playing out from the back. The Lask substitute Florian Flecker brought a touch of respectability to the scoreline with two goals in four minutes, both set up by Dibango, but there was no disguising the emphatic manner of Liverpool’s victory nor the surge of confidence it should give to Barcola.

Sports.title: Champions League: Mourinho’s Real Madrid stage wild comeback on Roma return
Sports.content:
José Mourinho enjoyed a Roma reunion to remember as Real Madrid completed an astonishing comeback by scoring three late goals to claim a 4-3 away win in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Marten de Roon gave the hosts a deserved opener before Kylian Mbappé struck back on his 100th Champions League appearance to level the scores at the break. Two Donyell Malen strikes in the space of six minutes early in the second half seemed to take the game away from the 15-time European champions as Roma ran rampant.

But Madrid scored three goals in the final six minutes, all stemming from corners, to turn the game on its head as Carlos Espí, Endrick and the former Roma defender Antonio Rüdiger struck at a stunned Stadio Olimpico.

Mourinho was a popular figure as he led Roma to the Conference League title and Europa League final during two-and-a-half years in charge. The Portuguese coach was honoured with banners and chants by the home crowd in Roma’s first home Champions League match in more than seven years.

View image in fullscreen José Mourinho is given a hero’s welcome on his return to Roma. Photograph: Alessandra Tarantino/AP

The Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who featured in the win, was handed a four-match ban for pulling an opponent’s hair during Saturday’s league win over Villarreal. The decision was announced shortly before the game kicked off in Rome – a situation that left Mourinho furious with Spain’s football authorities.

“They do things shamelessly now,” Mourinho said. The cat is out of the bag now. Two hours before the match, a player must know he has a four-match suspension. Couldn’t they do it now? Couldn’t they do it tomorrow morning? Do we have to come by bus and almost arrive at the stadium when we find out?”

Fredrik Sjøvold’s 52nd-minute strike secured a 1-0 victory for Bodø/Glimt over Borussia Dortmund, extending the Norwegian side’s remarkable home record against Europe’s elite.

Bodø were a cut above the 2024 Champions League runners-up and took the lead through Sjøvold just after the break. Dortmund improved in the final half hour but were unable to strike back, despite a late chance for Felix Nmecha.

“There’s nothing we can complain about, we deserved to lose,” said the Dortmund coach, Niko Kovac. “We didn’t bring enough passion today – that’s something Bodø did much better. They took the lead and after that we woke up, but by then it was too late.”

View image in fullscreen Fredrik Sjøvold celebrates after scoring what proved to be the winner for Bodø/Glimt. Photograph: NTB/Reuters

Dortmund join Manchester City, Inter and Sporting as recent big-name scalps on the artificial turf of Bodø’s Aspmyra Stadium. Bodø’s run to the last 16 last season was underpinned by an excellent record at their 8,200-capacity home, officially the smallest venue in this year’s competition.

Nomadic Ukrainian champions Shakhtar Donetsk celebrated moving into their new Champions League “home” at Stamford Bridge by storming back to beat AEK Athens 3-1.

The Greek side took the lead in the 28th minute through Lovro Majer but Pedrinho levelled confidently from the penalty spot just six minutes later. With about 10 minutes of normal time to go, Vinicius Tobias found the net from a tight angle and the substitute Gleiker Mendoza made the game safe, smashing home after cutting in from the left.

Shakhtar, from the east of Ukraine, are using Chelsea’s ground as the base for their European fixtures this season, with the Londoners absent from continental competition.

View image in fullscreen Shakhtar Donetsk fans make themselves at home at Stamford Bridge. Photograph: Kirsty Wigglesworth/AP

Since the beginning of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the UK has provided refuge to 265,000 Ukrainians, according to the Ukrainian embassy in London. Fans from the expat population turned out in force on Wednesday, swelling the crowd to 29,000.

Isco scored the winner and Abde Ezzalzouli netted a contender for goal of the week as Real Betis defeated Porto 3-2 in a bad-tempered game in Seville.

Ezzalzouli struck the ball from the corner of the penalty area into the top corner at the far post after the break. Gabriel Veiga equalised with a fine free-kick and set off a kerfuffle between rival players with his celebration. Three players were booked.

The Porto substitute Samu Aghehowa – a Spain international – scored just two minutes after coming on, only for Cucho Hernández – another substitute – to equalise in the 74th. Isco got the winner late with a penalty.

Stuttgart continued their 100% record in this season’s league phase with a 3-0 win against Slovan Bratislava in Slovakia. Earlier, Anis Hadj Moussa scored twice as the Dutch leaders, Feyenoord, came from behind to beat visiting Como 3-2.

Sports.title: Championship roundup: Soucek doubles up as West Ham hit nine-man Lincoln for six
Sports.content:
West Ham returned to winning ways as they cruised to a 6-0 Championship victory against nine-man Lincoln at the ProAmpac Stadium.

The hosts had Tom Hamer sent off after just three minutes and Conor McGrandles followed him off the pitch 20 minutes later, with Konstantinos Mavropanos heading West Ham ahead on the stroke of half-time.

The second half was dominated by West Ham, with further goals coming from Edvin Austbø, Jarrod Bowen, Pablo and Tomas Soucek, who scored twice, as the beleaguered home side desperately tried to keep the score down.

“I credit Lincoln as even with one man down, they were in the game and still creating a lot of problems for us,” said the West Ham manager, Nuno Espírito Santo, after watching his club’s biggest away win for 103 years.

“I think we made mistakes in terms of trying to rush things,” Nuno added. “It changed after the second goal and we played much better, in terms of being patient, recycling the ball and being clinical.”

Southampton recorded their second hard-fought 1-0 win in the space of four days as they condemned their hosts, Norwich, to a fourth successive league defeat.

Tonda Eckert’s side followed up Sunday’s victory over their local rivals, Portsmouth, with their first away win of the campaign in the league, with Kuryu Matsuki scorijng what proved to be the winner early in the second half.

Southampton are now well-placed in the top half of the table after 10 games, despite starting the campaign with a four-point deduction, while Norwich remain too close to the bottom for comfort after another disappointing display.

“To be fair there have been some good performances away from home when we just needed to finish better, ” Eckert said. “Tonight we have put in another good performance and on this occasion, we have got our reward. I am very happy for the boys because they worked very hard out there.”

Ebou Adams scored an 89th-minute winner as Portsmouth recovered after giving away a 2-0 lead to beat 10-man Sheffield United 3-2 at Fratton Park.

The hosts had been in cruise control after Zak Swanson’s stunning blast into the top corner and Adrian Segecic’s tap-in either side of Hamza Choudhury’s dismissal for two bookings. But Japhet Tanganga and Tom Cannon levelled the score and the visitors were somehow hunting back-to-back victories for the first time this season.

View image in fullscreen Southampton manager Tonda Eckert celebrates with his players after their 1-0 win at Norwich. Photograph: Nigel French/PA

Adams had the last word when he jumped off the bench to convert with a minute to go to give Portsmouth their third win of the campaign. After the game, Sheffield United manager Chris Wilder criticised referee Oliver Langford for his decision to send Choudhury off.

“There were a number of decisions which were incredibly frustrating,” Wilder said. “That is three players that have been sent off in the last two games he [Langford] has refereed us. Where are the young and up-and-coming referees who would be refereeing in the Championship now, instead of the ones that are just surviving?

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“No doubt we will have another survivor ref on Saturday. Where is the quality? Where are the ones coming through?” Wilder added. It is a tough one for the players, but there is more frustration and anger towards somebody. We have to deal with it.”

The Portsmouth head coach, John Mousinho, was frustrated by his team’s display despite their late winner. “I am happy that we won the game but the nature and circumstances of it … we have a large amount to learn and a long way to come.

“There was a little bit of relief when the winner went in, but there was fury through the game and I still am furious,” he added. “I think the players are on the same page as me and that is why there was muted celebrations at the end.”

QPR continued their impressive early season form with a thumping 4-1 win at home to struggling Derby. Three of the goals came in the first half, with Alfie Lloyd scoring, Nicolas Madsen tucking away a penalty and Harvey Vale adding the third.

Paul Smyth made it four with a deflected effort midway through the second half before Lars-Jørgen Salvesen scored a late consolation goal for Derby. Rangers’ victory was marred by a potentially serious knee injury to defender Amadou Mbengue, who was carried off on a stretcher late on.

Derby have now gone six league games without a win but their head coach, John Eustace, remains optimistic despite increasing pressure. “It’s a long season. We’ve had some difficult moments and I’m confident we’ll come through it,” Eustace said. “I don’t think the players will need picking up. I think they’ll be angry and ready to go for the next game.”

Sports.title: EFL boss calls for refereeing overhaul in damning assessment of ‘survivors’
Sports.content:
Sheffield United manager Chris Wilder has called for a refereeing overhaul in the Championship in a long, post-match rant.

Wilder was left bemused by the sending off of Hamza Choudhury on Wednesday, going on to slam referee Oliver Langford.



2 Sheffield United boss Wilder has called for change to refereeing in the Championship after Choudhury was sent off Credit: Getty

Choudhury was shown a red card for picking up two yellows in the first half of the Blades' 3-2 defeat to Portsmouth, with his second coming just before the break in the 44th minute.

Pompey's Ryan Kavuma-McQueen touched the ball around the Bangladesh international, who clipped his opponent's legs and brought him down.

Wilder believed the decision from referee Langford was harsh, with fans appealing that Choudhury was simply run into.



But the Sheffield United midfielder was shown a second yellow card and given his marching orders, as his side went on to lose.

What did Wilder say about Championship referees?

The decision then sparked Wilder into a post-match rant, where he called for the pathway for younger officials to the second tier to be accelerated, labelling some existing referees 'survivors'.



"That's three players sent off in his [Langford's] last two games that he's refereed [for us]," the Blades manager began.

"The boy takes Mark McGuinness' head off in the middle of the park, Japh [Tanganga] gets sent off down at Charlton last year for a reckless challenge...



"I don't know, I just think where are the young referees, up-and-coming referees that should be in the Championship?

"Instead of the ones that just, for me, survive, keep surviving, keep surviving... so no doubt we'll have another survivor referee on Saturday.

"Where's the quality? Where are the ones coming through?"

2 Choudhury was sent off by Langford for two yellow cards before half time, leading to Wilder's rant on refereeing as a whole Credit: Getty

Wilder then continued his rant, adding: "I like Simon Hooper [Sheffield United's referee on Saturday] by the way...he came through the football league, into the Championship, into the Premier League.



"But where are the referees coming through now? Because there's a surviving group of referees, in my opinion, that are just doing that.

"I just don't know with Hamza...the chat was that he wasn't going to send him off and then all of a sudden, I get opposition players going over, gamesmanship is part of the game, but I've got to say it looked as if he wasn't going to send him off at the start and then he did."

How are Sheffield United doing this season?

Wilder will have been angry at Sheffield United going down to ten men as it ultimately led to his side losing again.

The Blades came from 2-0 down to level the game against Portsmouth at 2-2, even without Choudhury, but Ebou Adams scored an 89th minute winner for the hosts in the end.



The defeat meant Wilder's men have now lost three of their last four games, sitting 15th in the Championship table.

They've won just three of their opening 10 matches, drawing another three and losing four.

Next, Sheffield United take on Bristol City on Saturday before facing struggling Derby County on October 24.

Sports.title: Antonio Conte’s team tell Man United he is open to replacing Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Antonio Conte’s team tell Man United he is open to replacing Michael Carrick

Antonio Conte would be prepared to succeed Michael Carrick as Manchester United head coach, talkSPORT understands.

Carrick is under mounting pressure to turn United's fortunes around following a poor start to the season.

2 Carrick is struggling to build upon Man Utd's strong finish to the 2025/26 season Credit: Getty

The Manchester giants sit 13th in the Premier League having collected six points from the opening six games.

And United followed up a 1-1 draw with 19th-placed Tottenham Hotspur with a disappointing 2-0 loss at Atletico Madrid to extend their winless run to five matches.

And with a seemingly unhappy dressing room to contend with, Carrick may be shown the Old Trafford exit sooner rather than later.

Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler is known to be admired by the United hierarchy, while Julian Nagelsmann is another option.

But one possible contender for the job has already reached out to the club to express interest...

Conte ready to save Man Utd?

talkSPORT understands representatives of Conte have told United would be interested in taking over should Carrick face the axe.

The former Chelsea and Spurs boss guided Napoli to the 2024/25 Scudetto.

However, he left his role at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona helm earlier this year having finished second to Inter Milan.

And Conte has previously refused to rule out a Premier League return as rumours of Carrick's potential exit continue to swirl.

Lisandro Martinez saga

Carrick's most pressing task is to deal with a seemingly unhappy dressing room.

2 Martinez tore into the United decision makers following Tuesday's defeat to Atletico Madrid Credit: Getty

The most recent defeat in Spain prompted a furious response from centre-back Lisandro Martinez, who took aim at the club's board for failing to strengthen the squad over the summer.

talkSPORT understands the Argentina star has the backing of senior United players.

"It was really poor, really poor," Martinez told Amazon Prime shortly after the defeat to Atletico Madrid.

"I have to control myself a lot. But sometimes it's a reflection of our club at the moment. We did it last season and now we expect more from the top.

"To bring more players, to compete. Other teams bring in many more players. I expect more from everyone… 100 per cent I expected more from our technical director.

"I have to be honest and also the players have to do more but it's just important when you make a strong squad for this type of night.

"Last season we created a base to build an amazing team. It's annoying and disappointing to come here and I'm not seeing my team get an amazing result here."

On Carrick and whether or not he was backed enough, Martinez added: "I don't think so. He does his best. The team knows how you play, every detail and if you don't change the next season, it's a big problem.

"You start changing, changing, changing manager, but what about other areas.

"I can't say more. It's easy to say the players but also we have to see other areas."

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho in public disagreement with Real Madrid star in aftermath of Roma win
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho in public disagreement with Real Madrid star in aftermath of Roma win

Jose Mourinho was involved in a disagreement with Federico Valverde following Real Madrid's 4-3 win over Roma.

The Spanish giants came from 3-1 down to claim a memorable Champions League victory in Rome.



3 Rudiger scored Real Madrid's fourth in an incredible end to their Champions League win over Roma

Goals from Carlos Espi, Endrick and former Roma defender Antonio Rudiger in the space of seven second-half minutes capped a fine night at the Olimpico.

Espi and Endrick were both introduced after the break, with the young pair each enjoying an impressive cameo.

Midfielder Valverde has indicated that the substitutes played a key role in the comeback triumph and that the team only executed their gameplan once the changes were made.



What did Mourinho say?

Mourinho, though, was having none of it, saying as much in his post-match press conference.

"I don't entirely agree with [Federico] Valverde, because the opponent faced us with a different positioning from all their previous matches that we analysed," Mourinho said.



3 Valverde landed himself in hot water with the boss on Wednesday night

"They attacked us with three players down the right-hand side, with a player on the flank preventing us from pushing up to press Wesley."



The Los Blancos boss then explained the tweaks he made that instigated the turnaround in Italy.

"That's why I was talking a lot with [Aurelien] Tchouameni during the first half to make the necessary adjustments, and when the second half began I felt the team had become more stable," he continued.

"But we conceded a goal we should not have conceded because of what we did in midfield, then the opponent took advantage of the attacking transition and scored.

3 Mourinho's second-half tweaks and changes helped Real Madrid to an unlikely victory



"After that we showed an organised fighting spirit, and it was an emotional reaction within a tactical framework that helped us a great deal.

"I know very well how [Roma head coach Gian Piero] Gasperini's teams play because I spent many years in Italy, but he surprised us with his attacking plan down the right-hand side.

"Even so, there are no miracles in football, and it is difficult to maintain that intensity for all 90 minutes."

Valverde's previous

Valverde has previously found himself in the spotlight in Madrid having been involved in a number of training ground scuffles with teammate Tchouameni earlier this year.



Both players were involved in two bust ups earlier this year, the second of which landed the Uruguayan in hospital.

The midfield duo were slapped with €500,000 fines [£432k], which the club confirmed in a statement at the time.

Sports.title: Gareth Southgate drops bombshell update on future in management
Sports.content:
Former England manager Gareth Southgate has admitted he doesn't think he will return to management in the Premier League.

Southgate, who left his role with the Three Lions after losing in the final of Euro 2024, has not had a club role since 2006.

4 Southgate has admitted that he doesn't think he'll return to Premier League management after losing some of his passion for football Credit: Getty

He was linked to one of his former teams in Crystal Palace earlier this year, while he has been tipped to save Manchester United.

And with Michael Carrick under pressure, the Man United hotseat could end up being available in the coming weeks.

However, the 56-year-old is not planning on taking a new position in the Premier League, even after a couple of years without a job.

When asked if he would consider a return to managing in the Premier League, Southgate told the The Amol Rajan Connection: "I don't see a scenario where I do that.

"Towards the end of my time with England, I stopped enjoying, at the very least for a period, the wins keep you going.

"By the end, I didn't even enjoy the wins for any longer than a couple of minutes. So, I've hardly watched football.

"I went to the FA Cup final to see my team, Crystal Palace, win their first trophy. I've not been to a football ground since.

"So my sort of desire to be involved in football has changed."

What else has Southgate said on his future in football?

It seems Southgate has lost some of the passion for football management having spend time away from the game.

Following his departure from England after eight years as boss, he has not taken another managerial role.

4 Southgate is enjoying his life away from the game after spending eight years as England manager Credit: Getty

He has spent some time as a technical observer for UEFA since, as well as become a visiting lecturer at Harvard Business School.

But on the whole, Southgate is more than happy with his life away from football, enjoying his new experiences.

"I've loved the last 18 months of my life," the ex-Three Lions manager added.

"I've had 37 years where my sense of self depended on did I win or lose on Saturday.

"And actually I've loved having different experiences. I've met politicians, I've met people in the media industry, I have learned about leadership in all sorts of areas, I've travelled around the world learning things.

"I've just enjoyed playing a different film in my life."

4 The 56-year-old has not taken on a new management role since leaving England in 2024, opting for new experiences instead Credit: Getty

Southgate on Man City's charges

Despite his desire to work in football waining, Southgate has, of course, been dragged into the debate over Manchester City.

Man City were found guilty of 114 charges regarding financial breaches between 2009 and 2018 earlier this month, with the club then appealing and maintaining their innocence.

The club have dealt with huge backlash, with calls for them to be stripped of their titles or relegated, while the fans have players have had to deal with harsh treatment at Anfield on Sunday.

And Southgate has labelled the situation as 'unbelievably complex' for all parties involved, saying: "There'll be the tribal fans' response to punish Manchester City as much as we can, relegate them, fine them, do whatever you can.

"I've been in football boardrooms, I've been in meetings with UEFA, I've been in meetings with FIFA, I have been in all these spaces and I know how complicated all of this is.

"My underlying thought is none of this is good for football and there are no winners.

4 Southgate thinks there will be no winners from the ongoing situation regarding Man City's 114 guilty charges Credit: Getty

"Because if you're at the Premier League, for a very brief moment you might feel justified that all the flak you've had for this case taking so long, this is why it's taken so long and there's the verdict, and I'm sure there's an element of justification in that.

"Then there's this realisation of how do we deal with all of this because you know the possibility of all the different legal cases that emerge from this, how long this could still take, what's the right sort of punishment, how do you keep the whole game on track?

"That's unbelievably complex."

Sports.title: Top five greatest Premier League signings in history including surprise player who won nothing
Sports.content:
The Premier League has been the hub for some of the best transfers of all time over the years - but who has been the greatest?

In the latest edition of Max Scott's Mount Rushmore of Less series, he has attempted to whittle it down to just a few signings.

6 Max Scott has selected his five greatest ever Premier League signings because having only four on his Mount Rushmore just isn't enough Credit: Getty

And of course, continuing with the theme, Scott believes having just four on his Mount Rushmore isn't enough, so he has picked five of the greatest ever buys in the Premier League.

From impressive bargains to instant success and the beginning of a legacy, he has selected some huge names - and some surprises.

So, here are the top five Premier League signings in history...

Kompany was the epitomy of the leadership

"First up I think is a really underappreciated signing in the history of the Premier League," Scott began.

"That is, Vincent Kompany."

Kompany joined Manchester City in 2008 and went on to spend 11 years at the club, winning a whopping 12 trophies.

For eight of his years in Manchester he wore the captains armband, and he certainly set the standards for the club's glory.

"Signed from Hamburg for around £6-7million and went on to become, for me, the epitomy of the leadership of Pep Guardiola's incredible dominance in the Premier League.

"He scored two title-winning goals - the first the header in the Manchester derby and then that legendary strike against Leicester, elliciting the strangest noise from the gullet of Gary Neville.

"So, the fact that he has a statue of himself and as a player he has contributed to title-winning goals, and the fact that he was in City's starting 11 when they concededed 0.9 goals a game, for me, he's a magnificent leader and has to be in the top signings."

6 Kompany was Man City captain for eight years, winning four Premier League titles with the club across his 11-year spell Credit: Getty

Henry is 'the greatest signing in history'

Scott then continued: "Next is a player Arsenal signed for just £11m...and Arsene Wenger turned Thierry Henry into what I think is the greatest ever player to play in Premier League football.

"I don't even know where to begin in terms of his accolades. He was player of the year in Arsenal's Player of the Year during their famous Invincible title winning season.

"The season before, he became the first and only ever play to score 20 goals and get 20 assists, nobody has done it since.

"For me, this is evidence enough that Henry has to be in the Mount Rushmore or Less of great Premier League signings.

"Just the way he played, he might not have scored as many as Alan Shearer, he might not have scored them as quickly as Sergio Aguero, but he was a more complete player - graceful, powerful, clinical, anything you would want not just in a football player, but in an entertainment industry.

"Henry probably is THE greatest Premier League signing in history."

6 Scott has labelled Henry as the greatest ever signing in the Premier League after his incredible stats and success after joining Arsenal Credit: Getty

6 Signed for just £11m, Henry became the greatest ever Premier League player and went on to win more with Barcelona Credit: Getty

Harry Redknapp was bang on about Lampard

Ex-West Ham manager Harry Redknapp once sat next to a 16-year-old Frank Lampard in 1996 and said 'I'm telling you now, he will go right to the very top', in an iconic press conference moment.

And go to the top he did, with Scott saying: "You cannot deny that Harry Redknapp was absolutely bang on.

"Frank Lampard, signing from West Ham for £11m to Chelsea, did indeed go right to the very top.

"He won absolutely everything there is to win in 13 years at Chelsea, three Premier League titles, four FA Cups, the Champions League in 2021, and he only went and scored, in the Premier League alone, 177 goals and got 119 assists, as a midfielder.

"Lampard is the Mount Rushmore of great Premier League signings because he is the greatest ever goalscorer the Premier League has ever seen, you cannot deny that.

"He was the onle outfielder to spend more time on the pitch that Gareth Barry, that's saying a lot. He didn't just do it in bursts, there was longevity to his career."

6 Lampard was tipped to go to the 'very top' by Redknapp - and he did, becoming one of the greatest midfielders of all time at Chelsea Credit: Getty

Wherever Cantona went, success followed

"If you're younger the age of 30, then you may not appreciate this one as much - Eric Cantona is in my Mount Rushmore of Less of great Premier League signings," Scott said, picking his next transfer.

"Now, the stats themselves don't really scream one of the greatest ever signings, 64 goals for Man United in over 100 games.

"But the thing about Cantona, notwishstanding the fact he needs a bit of stick for the flying kick of a fan in the stands, everywhere he went, he won.

"Sir Alex Ferguson took him off Leeds for about a £1m, not that much money, one of the greatest bits of business from Ferguson.

"Cantona then went on to win the title after he joined Man United and in the four remaining seasons, won three titles and the one he didn't, he had the ban for booting the fan in the face."

The legendary Frenchman retired from football at 30, when he was still at the top, and that's also why Scott wants him in.

6 Coutinho was a star for Liverpool after signing for just £8.5m, but his eventual big-money exit led the club to title success under Klopp Credit: Getty

Coutinho the catalyst for Liverpool's success

Now, in Scott's Mount Rushmore of Less, he sometimes finds picking just four players tough, so he adds a fifth to the list.

And in this list of top signings, Philippe Coutinho takes a place despite his honours list at Anfield reading: League Cup runner-up and Europa League runner-up.

"Bare with me for a moment. Coutinho signed for £8.5m in a really strange time, it was the back end of the Steven Gerrard, Luis Suarez era where they nearly won the league and it was the beginning of the Mohamed Salah, Roberto Firmino, Sadio Mane playing in their prime under Jurgen Klopp.

"Coutinho was in the middle of that and he was an incredible football player. Now, he didn't win anything, but I think he kept that Liverpool dream alive. The owners at the time hung their hats on Coutinho being the start of something new.

"And he was, but in a really unexpected way, because when PSG come in and sign Neymar, Barcelona now need someone to replace him and sign Coutinho for £146m. That fills the back pockets of Liverpool, who at the time were bereft of a league title.

"They reinvest that money wisely, at the hands of Klopp, and they go on to become one of the most exciting Premier League sides that we've seen. They win the Champions League, the title...but for me, Coutinho is the catalyst for all of that to happen."

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca reveals Luis Enrique’s surprise post-match comment after PSG thriller
Sports.content:
Paris Saint-Germain manager Luis Enrique claimed his side was 'quite lucky' to beat Manchester City 4-2.

Enrique's surprising admission was revealed by City boss Enzo Maresca during his post-match interview with TNT Sports.

3 Maresca took charge of his first Champions League home game as Man City manager, but it ended in defeat Credit: Getty

PSG raced out to a three-goal lead inside the first 32 minutes courtesy of goals from Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Vitinha.

The early deficit marked the first time City shipped three goals in the opening half of a home game since November 2015, underlining the rarity of their defensive woes.

Although Erling Haaland netted twice in the second half, it mattered little as PSG romped to their eighth win over an English rival in Champions League action.

Despite the scoreline, which was aided by a string of errors from City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, Maresca felt his side 'deserved more'.

"I think we start quite good until the first goal and then we concede the second one after one minute," Maresca said.

"That created some bad feelings.

"Second half, we were much better and probably deserved something more.

"It was a bit strange, to be honest. Until the first goal, we started quite good, we were in the game, then we conceded the first and then the second one. We didn't lose half-time, we adjusted something. We created enough to deserve something more.

"We adjusted a bit when we were pressing. I think we lost a bit of the balance.

"Even with 3-0 in the first half, with the amount of chances we created in the second half, we deserved more. Luis said at the end of the game that they were quite lucky today.

3 Former Man City manager Pep Guardiola watched on from the sidelines as his old side were cut open Credit: AFP

"You have to be clinical but not lose the balance."

Maresca added he and his players 'are sorry' for the first half and will look to put it right on Saturday when City host Ipswich Town.

The loss to PSG dropped City down to 17th in the Champions League standings after two games.

As for the Parisians, they sit in first place having won both of their matches.

PSG have scored ten and conceded three, putting them top on goals scored ahead of eight other teams, including Barcelona, Aston Villa, Arsenal and Liverpool.

What did Enrique say publicly?

Enrique echoed his comments he made to Maresca in his full interview with TNT Sports.

He said: "It was very, very, very tough. I think credit to them because we started the match great and scored three goals and it was a big difference.

"But I don't love going in at half time with that difference because you think the match is done, and it's not done - you are in trouble.

"I think it was a very nice match. The way they play, it is amazing. The way Enzo Maresca plays is really nice and we like to play these kind of matches.

"I have to repeat, we were lucky because in the second half, we could have conceded more goals.

"Football is sometimes unfair, and you have to balance your performance because if you concede so many chances, it's hard to win.

"Today, we were lucky, and we need to improve that in the future."

3 Enrique was extremely complimentary of Maresca and Man City despite dishing out their first defeat of the season Credit: Getty

Story of the game

PSG hit the front after just 13 minutes through a clever move down the right.

Fabian Ruiz then collected and played a pass with the outside of his boot to Doue.

Doue cut inside and looked up as if he was going to pass before reversing a shot in at the near post, catching everyone by surprise.

It was 2-0 two minutes later as Doue and Dembele linked up beautifully with the former lifting a cross to the far post for the latter to head home.

The third came just after the half hour mark as Warren Zaire-Emery delicately flicked a ball into Vitinha's path, and he caressed it into the back of the net from just inside the box.

At half time, Maresca made a triple change as Iliman Ndiaye, Matheus Nunes and Ayyoub Bouaddi came on.

Ndiaye made an instant impact to set up Haaland as he cut in from the left and delivered a vicious cross that was glanced home by the big striker.

But with the momentum with the home side, Donnarumma made a howler.

Maghnes Akliouche turned and rifled in a shot from the edge of the box that the Italian palmed away but only backwards, and he couldn't prevent it dropping over the line.

City kept creating chance after chance and grabbed a second when Enzo Fernandez played Bouaddi in down the right-hand-side of the box.

Bouaddi then picked out Haaland, and he slotted home, and there was even time for a missed penalty after Nunes brought Nuno Mendes down in the area.

Former Man City man Ferran Torres stepped up and hit his effort straight at Donnarumma as PSG held on.

Next up for them is a home clash against Barcelona, which looks like a blockbuster, while City take on AEK Athens.
