Last year, the Associated Press news agency (AP) revealed that US tech giants had “quietly empowered Israel to track and kill many more alleged militants more quickly in Gaza and Lebanon through a sharp spike in artificial intelligence and computing services”.

The AP report went on to note that “the number of civilians killed has also soared, fueling fears that these tools are contributing to the deaths of innocent people”.

But while it might be news to the AP, that is unfortunately how a genocide works.

And as the US goes to war for AI dominance while the tech giants bank on a post-human world, one can’t help but feel that the toilet paper was a nice touch, indeed.

The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.

World.title: Iraq devalues dinar to ease cash crunch, leaving traders in limbo
World.content:
The government hopes a weaker dinar will help pay salaries, but traders face rising import costs and uncertainty.

Baghdad, Iraq – Sitting anxiously in his small office in Jameela market, one of Baghdad’s main wholesale markets, food trader Hamza al-Rudayni is waiting to see what the coming days will bring.

A decision by the Iraqi government to devalue the country’s currency, the dinar, against the US dollar has left traders like him facing sudden losses and uncertainty over the prices they should charge for their goods.

“I don’t know what to do,” al-Rudayni told Al Jazeera after the devaluation reduced the dollar value of his dinar holdings, leaving him with less money to purchase imported goods.

“All I know is I woke up a few days ago to discover that I had lost 25 million Iraqi dinars (roughly $16,500 at the new exchange rate) because of this decision, while larger merchants lost billions,” he said.

Al-Rudayni entered the wholesale trade market last year after losing his previous job at a private Iraqi bank that he says was sanctioned by the United States Treasury. He sold his car and used his savings to start trading with a larger merchant before recently launching his own business.

With exchange-rate fluctuations making prices unpredictable, al-Rudayni said he and many other traders have chosen to suspend buying and selling until the situation stabilises.

“Market activity has ground to a halt,” al-Rudayni said. “Traders buy goods in dollars but sell them in dinars, as regulations prohibit them from selling in dollars.”

That is the root of the problem for traders: A weaker dinar means they have to pay more in local currency for goods imported in dollars, while making it harder to determine the right price they should charge customers for goods they already have in stock.



Why devalue?

On October 7, the Iraqi government introduced a new official exchange rate against the US dollar, in an attempt to ease a financial crisis triggered by the US-Israeli war on Iran and the disruption of oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz.

Before the war, Iraq exported around 3.5 million barrels of oil per day through the Strait of Hormuz, accounting for 90 percent of Iraq’s government revenue.

The Central Bank of Iraq decision set the rate at 1,520 dinars per US dollar for cash sales to the public. It was previously set at 1,320 dinars per dollar.

Devaluing the Iraqi dinar by almost 15 percent against the dollar allows the government to receive more local currency for every dollar of oil revenue it converts, helping it cover public spending, including government employee salaries.

“It is my decision and I am responsible for it,” Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi said during a meeting with parliamentary leaders on Thursday.

“I was facing three challenging options to cover salaries and other mandatory expenditures,” al-Zaidi added. “The first is to cut salaries by 35 percent … the second is to pay the salaries every 45 days … while the third is to resort to foreign loans.”

Al-Zaidi, a former banker, also said that his government had inherited public debt exceeding 208 trillion Iraqi dinars ($139bn at the new rate) when it took office in May. He said the government needed approximately 10 trillion dinars ($6.7bn) each month to cover salaries and other essential expenditure.

A shortage of liquidity

The crisis in the Strait of Hormuz had caused a severe financial squeeze for the Iraqi government.

Although the situation has eased somewhat in recent weeks after Iraq’s oil exports partially recovered, they have yet to return to their pre-war levels.

Mudher Mohammed Salih, the Iraqi prime minister’s financial adviser, said in August that the Central Bank of Iraq’s foreign currency reserves had declined from $106bn to approximately $80bn.

To make up for the loss of revenue, the Iraqi government has also turned to borrowing from domestic banks to cover salaries and other expenses.

A Finance Ministry official told Al Jazeera that ensuring salaries were paid on time remained the government’s main priority, describing this issue as a matter of domestic economic stability.

“Our hands are tied regarding the revenue and how to maintain enough money to ensure that we can pay the salaries,” the official, who asked to remain anonymous because he was not authorised to speak publicly, said.



Economists have warned that while adjusting the exchange rate could ease some immediate fiscal pressures, it would not address the deeper weaknesses in Iraq’s economy.

“Nothing in economics is sacred, including the exchange rate,” said Nabil al-Marsoumi, professor of economics at Al Maaqal University in Basra. “It can be adjusted, but only after all other options have been exhausted.”

“In any case, the exchange rate shouldn’t be used as a cover-up for failures in the state’s economic and fiscal policies,” he added.

World.title: ‘Our works are next to each other’: Art bridges Gaza and West Bank
World.content:
Young Palestinian artists in Gaza and the occupied West Bank bring their work together in simultaneous exhibitions, despite Israeli restrictions that keep them apart.

Share ‘Our works are next to each other’: Art bridges Gaza and West Bank on social media

Bethlehem, occupied West Bank – Artists arrived with family and friends at the Bethlehem Peace Center, where a live feed connected them to a small gathering at an artist’s studio in Bureij refugee camp, in the central Gaza Strip.

The two exhibitions marked the opening of Anamel Falasteen, the first competition organised by Falasteen Collective, a cultural initiative launched in 2025 by Palestinian artists, filmmakers, designers and others working in arts and culture. The three-day twin exhibitions, held earlier this week, brought together young Palestinian artists whose work and opportunities to meet are separated by Israeli movement restrictions.

“In the competition, we have Palestinian artists from Jerusalem, historic Palestine, the Gaza Strip and the West Bank,” said Osama Nazzal, one of the judges, speaking in Bethlehem. “I don’t like these divisions. I want to say all of Palestine.”

From his studio at Gallery Paleta in Gaza’s Bureij refugee camp, amid Israel’s ongoing genocidal war on the Palestinian enclave, painter and juror Ghanem Al Den sent greetings on the live feed.

“Greetings and peace from soul to soul, from Gaza to our sister Palestinian cities across this beloved homeland,” he said.

“In this competition, many things that were lost came together. The most important thing is hope.”

After the speeches, visitors had the opportunity to take a closer look at the paintings, photographs and drawings that covered the walls. Visitors moved between them, stopping to look closer, point and talk about what they saw.



“Artists decided to come from Hebron, from Ramallah, from Jerusalem, from Jaffa, from Nablus, despite the risk,” said Mohamed Abusrour, one of the founding members of Falasteen Collective.

“They have a voice, they want to contribute, and they want to show the world that we still exist.”

Not all the works on display in Bethlehem were originals. Because of the blockade and movement restrictions, the organisers said there was no way to transport original artworks out of Gaza. Instead, they printed reproductions of the Gaza submissions and hung them alongside original pieces.

For one Bethlehem visitor, the curation was what stood out. She assumed some works exploring similar themes were by the same artist. They turned out to be by different artists, some in Gaza and others in the West Bank.

“I sat a bit longer with some paintings, and that brought tears to my eyes,” she said. “The livestream with the presence of everyone’s paintings was a portal to bringing everyone’s essence together.”

Young artists document loss and everyday life

The works on display reflected different ways of documenting Palestinian life, from the loss of family and home in Gaza to the traditions and everyday experiences artists want to preserve.

Abusrour said the idea for the competition came from listening to artist friends describe how they could not participate or express themselves freely. He said the aim was to give young Palestinians a platform to show their work at home and abroad “without any restriction”.

The competition was open to artists aged 15 to 30. About 170 applied, nearly 60 percent from Gaza, according to the organisers. A jury split between the West Bank and Gaza selected 120 works across three tracks: memory and place, land and return, and everyday heritage.

The jury met daily by video, working through power and internet cuts in Gaza.

“Despite the lack of resources, they decided to take part, and when they decided to take part, they decided to take part with strength,” Abusrour said of the artists in Gaza.

Among the works shown in Gaza was The Vine Bears Witness, by Arwa Mukhaimer, a 20-year-old university student. It shows the entrance to her family’s home, shaded by a grapevine. It was there, on March 30, 2024, that she received news of her father’s death. He had been unable to get medical treatment during Israel’s war on Gaza, she said. Five months later, she said, the house was destroyed.



“This painting is a memorial to what we lost, a double loss, of the father and of the place,” she told Al Jazeera.

Two days before he died, he told her: “My darling, may God be pleased with you.” She wrote those words into the painting.

When she was displaced as a result of the war, she said, “The first thing I thought about was my tools.” Art supplies are hard to find in Gaza, she said, and some materials never enter the Strip.

The challenges facing artists extend beyond access to materials. Gaza’s main art spaces, including the Eltiqa and Shababeek galleries, have been destroyed as a result of Israeli attacks in Gaza.

Mukhaimer said her painting “has hope and joy in it, but its meaning is painful and moving”.

In Bethlehem, Hanan Barghouthi, 24, a visual artist from Ramallah, also chose to paint joy, but from a different place. Her painting of a Palestinian wedding is filled with bright colours, traditional symbols, and movement.

“All the art has become about people expressing sadness, so I want to reflect happiness, because I like to be happy,” she said.

Movement restrictions divide Gaza and the West Bank

Bringing the two exhibitions together required organisers to work around the restrictions that keep Palestinians in the two territories apart. Artists in Gaza and the West Bank live under different conditions of Israeli occupation, but both face barriers to meeting, collaborating and exhibiting together.

Israel has imposed a land, sea and air blockade on the Gaza Strip since June 2007. In the occupied West Bank, the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) documented 925 obstacles restricting the movement of 3.4 million Palestinians, including in East Jerusalem, as of December 2025.

That separation is not accidental, said Rehab Nazzal, an artist and educator on the competition’s advisory committee.

“It’s a creation of the settler colonial project,” she said. “By suffocating the Palestinians with all the restrictions of movement, it intends to push the Palestinians out.”

Abusrour said spaces like the exhibition give young Palestinians a reason to stay and continue creating.

“You cannot live in a place, and be called steadfast, without having a reason to live as well,” he said.

Watching the Gaza artists on screen, Barghouthi said she felt “very sad” and asked herself, “Where are we and where are they?”

“I felt we were close to them, but at the same time far away,” she said. “But emotionally, I felt they were next to us, because our works are next to each other.”

World.title: Musk says US government may be behind slowdown of Ukraine drone speeds
World.content:
Elon Musk has suggested that the US government may be behind restrictions on the speed at which some of Ukraine's weapons can travel and stay connected to SpaceX's Starlink internet network.

Starlink is a vital tool allowing Kyiv to guide drones to Russian targets and also protect its own skies, but on Tuesday night Ukraine said unexpected new speed limits were disrupting its battlefield missions.

An adviser to President Volodymyr Zelensky said he believed the restrictions were not a coincidence and were related to the latest strains between Kyiv and Washington.

Musk said that Starshield, the military-grade sister service to Starlink, is controlled by the US government, and "any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately [the US president]".

Musk - writing on X - had been responding to pleas from Ukrainian officials to restore connectivity, including from Zelensky who told UK media: "I hope that it's a mistake, maybe [a] huge technical problem. I don't know, but we are asking to... switch [it] on."

Starlink, which is owned by Musk's SpaceX, restricted speed limits on Tuesday night to 100mph (160km/h), meaning any weapons that travelled faster than that lost connectivity to the network.

It had been partially restored by Wednesday evening, Ukraine's former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov said.

"Removing Starshield's speed limit entirely is now critical for Ukraine's defense," he wrote on X, thanking Elon Musk and asking for his "continued support".

About an hour later, Musk replied to that post, defending his company's involvement.

"Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS," he wrote.

Musk added that Starlink is for "civilian or defensive activities and cannot be used for offensive military action, as doing so would be inappropriate for a commercial company".

The US government has not commented.

In the early hours of Thursday, Russian strikes killed two people in the Dnipropetrovsk region, regional governor Oleksandr Hanzha said.

While both companies are owned by Musk's SpaceX, Starlink is a civilian service that uses satellites in low Earth orbit to provide internet access, particularly in remote areas, while Starshield is designed for government and military use.

The restrictions on Tuesday night came as Russia launched deadly attacks against Ukraine that killed several people in Kyiv, officials said, and hit communications and energy facilities used by Ukraine's military.

Zelensky said it was "one of the largest attacks" from Russia, and while "a significant part of the drones were shot down" there were "also hits".

At least 600,000 people across Ukraine were left without electricity, and residents said they received no warning of incoming drones before they hit.

"It is clear that this action cannot be a coincidence and is related to the current political situation," Zelensky's adviser Serhiy Beskrestnov wrote on Telegram on Wednesday morning.

World.title: Student protesters attack government buildings in Albania
World.content:
Thousands of students have taken to the streets in the Albanian capital of Tirana, attacking several government buildings on the second day of violent anti-government protests.

The demonstration began outside the ministry of education on Tuesday, as students called for better university conditions and job prospects.

Wednesday saw part of the education ministry's building set on fire, while the prime minister's office, finance and interior ministry, and several surrounding businesses were also attacked.

Albania's Deputy Prime Minister âAlbana KoÃ§iu has called for "calmness, self-restraint and maturity" and said "Albania does not need to burn to change".

World.title: Retired US generals call on Pentagon to cancel 'barbaric' execution livestream
World.content:
A group of 72 retired US generals, admirals, and other high-ranking military officers are pressing the US government to cancel plans to livestream an execution by firing squad.

"We ask the President, our Congressional representatives, and our fellow citizens to act to prevent this barbaric abuse of authority," they wrote in a letter where they also argued the livestream would turn the mass killer into a "martyr".

Last week, the Pentagon announced it would publicly show the 3 December execution of Nidal Hasan, an Army psychiatrist who shot dead 13 unarmed US soldiers at the Fort Hood military base.

Lawmakers from both parties, as well as religious leaders, have criticised the plan.

Last week President Donald Trump said he "absolutely" approved of the livestream plan, but some administration officials are now leaning against it, according to CBS News, the BBC's US media partner. CBS reported that Trump had not yet made a final decision on the livestream as of Tuesday.

In the open letter released on Wednesday, the former military leaders - which included 45 generals, 12 admirals and several former judge advocates general - said they did not oppose the death penalty being carried out.

But they argued a public execution would violate the US Constitution's protections against cruel and unusual punishment and turn what should be a "solemn and grave punishment" into "a carnival for the enjoyment of voyeurs and spectators".

"This type of exploitative broadcasting - that debases human dignity- will taint the honor of the military that employs it, and a nation that allows it," they also wrote.

"It will be used by our nation's enemies to stoke hatred, harm American soldiers and citizens in the future, and will ensure that Hasan becomes a martyr for attacking and killing his fellow soldiers."

The letter's signatories came from throughout the military and included a handful of officers who retired during Trump's first term. Some also had served during the Iraq and Afghanistan wars.

Hasan said in court that he carried out the shooting at Fort Hood, the deadliest ever non-combat attack on an American base, believing he was protecting Muslims and the Taliban in Afghanistan from the US military. Hasan was shot during the attack and now uses a wheelchair.

Retired Maj Gen Tony Taguba, who led the Army's investigation into reported prisoner abuses at Abu Ghraib in Iraq, and retired Air Force Coll Moe Davis, a prosecutor at the Guatanamo Bay detention centre who called waterboarding torture, signed the letter.

So did Charles Bolden, a US Marine Corps Major General who became the head of Nasa, and retired Lt Gen Claudia Kennedy, the first woman to become a three-star general in the Army.

World.title: White House defends new press secretary amid questions about her legal credentials
World.content:
The White House is defending its new press secretary, Katie Zacharia, as she faces scrutiny over her legal credentials.

President Donald Trump described Zacharia as an attorney when announcing her appointment last week. She has referred to herself as a lawyer.

But when she was asked on Tuesday by a reporter in which state she had passed the bar exam required to be an attorney in the US, she said standing alongside the president: "When I moved to China."

She does not appear to be registered to the bar in any state where she has lived. White House communications director Steven Cheung said Zacharia is "uniquely qualified and whip smart to help inform the American people".

Responding to questions about her credentials, Zacharia said in a statement this week: "I practised international transaction law, with all the appropriate credentials."

On Wednesday, a watchdog group, Campaign for Accountability, filed a complaint with the California State Bar Association.

It is seeking an investigation into whether Zacharia "repeatedly held herself out to the public as entitled to practise law without a licence to do so, conduct California law treats as a crime".

The 42-year-old political strategist graduated from law school at Pepperdine University in California in 2011, the university confirmed.

A law degree is not a licence to practise law in the US.

The new White House press secretary told the New York Times on Wednesday that when she first began appearing on cable news, she had asked Pepperdine how she should identify herself.

She said she was advised by the university president that she could call herself a lawyer, but not an attorney.

The new press secretary also told the paper that when she answered China to a question about her bar exam, it was a misunderstanding. She had mistakenly thought, above the din of Marine One, the reporter had asked: "Where were you after law school?"

Zacharia took the bar exam in California after graduating from law school but did not pass, according to the Wall Street Journal. California's bar exam is widely regarded as one of the hardest in the US to pass.

A person with direct knowledge of the matter told the outlet that Zacharia took the exam around the same time that she was planning a wedding and preparing to move to China with her husband-to-be.

World.title: 'Nowhere to escape' - Indonesians share footage of orange haze blanketing towns
World.content:
A thick orange smog has descended on the Indonesian city of Palangka Raya.

Witnesses captured videos of the haze washing over the Kalimantan region not far from where wildfires continue to burn.

The ISPU air pollution index exceeded 1,200, according to data from the national environment ministry, four times higher than the "hazardous" level of 300 on Wednesday.

Toxic smog is choking millions across Indonesia, Singapore and Malaysia, with authorities partly blaming the agricultural clearing method known as "slash and burn" for compounding the intense haze.

Read more on this story here.

World.title: At the Brooklyn novelty shop in 'surreal' row with Kelly Clarkson over mechanical bird
World.content:
On a rainy Wednesday afternoon, a novelty toy and games store in a quiet part of New York City was seeing much busier foot traffic than usual.

Inside, the shop was packed with cameramen and customers, while passersby in this Brooklyn neighbourhood of Cobble Hill looked inside, asking: "Where's the bird?"

Art of Play has found itself at the centre of a social media storm since the weekend when Grammy-winning musician Kelly Clarkson complained online that the boutique store would not let her buy a singing and dancing mechanical bird that was perched on the wall.

The Since U Been Gone singer claimed she was "looked at as if I couldn't afford" the bird - which she said had a price tag of $15,000 (Â£11,000).

"Y'all should go check out Art of Play in Brooklyn if you enjoy being treated like Julia Roberts' character in Pretty Woman," she said, referring to a scene from the 1990 romantic comedy film where Roberts' character is treated poorly by staff at a shop, who imply she cannot afford various items.

In a follow-up post on social media, Clarkson said the store had told her the bird cost $15,000 and that they could find her something else "comparable".

Art of Play has defended how it treated the star on social media, saying the wooden bird - which is called Molly - is permanently attached to the wall and is not for sale.

It said that during Clarkson's five-minute visit on Saturday, an employee suggested to her that she could buy an identical bird for $15,000.

They also said they had offered her a different singing bird for $2,000 from a clock-making shop in Germany, which she could have purchased that day.

"Imagine our surprise when our small local business was suddenly attacked by eight million people who have never visited our store," Art of Play said.

"It's been a surreal experience to be the focus of such widespread outrage after just one mention by a celebrity."

World.title: Sally Rooney books withdrawn in UK over Palestine Action support
World.content:
Normal People author Sally Rooney has said her novels will no longer be supplied to booksellers in the UK as a result of her support for Palestine Action.

The Irish novelist said last year she intended to carry on using her royalties to support the group, which is a proscribed terrorist organisation in the UK.

In a statement to BBC News, Rooney said further publication of her work could constitute a "serious criminal offence", so she had agreed with her publisher Faber not to continue supplying her books to UK retailers.

"I have made every effort to be honest with the public about my beliefs and intentions, and I am wholly prepared to accept the consequences," she said.

Ebook editions have already been removed from sale in the UK, although many book shops still have existing stock of physical copies.

Waterstones confirmed to the BBC that Faber had advised there were no restrictions on booksellers keeping their current copies on the shelves.

Rooney has sold more than six million books globally, including 2.3 million in the UK, according to NielsenIQ BookData.

Normal People was published in 2018 and turned into a hit TV series two years later, effectively launching the acting careers of Paul Mescal and Daisy Edgar-Jones.

Rooney's other novels are Intermezzo, Conversations With Friends and Beautiful World, Where Are You.

Publisher Faber told BBC News: "Current legislation in the UK has led to circumstances where Faber cannot pass on UK earnings to Sally Rooney for her work.

"To sell a writer's work and not be able to pass on earnings is an unconscionable situation for a publisher.

"As such, and in full agreement with Sally, we have taken the decision that we can no longer supply her works in the UK in any format."

Faber added: "We remain the proud publisher of her remarkable body of work, which we will continue to sell in other territories."

World.title: Anthropic flags revenue surge to investors ahead of stock market debut
World.content:
Artificial intelligence (AI) giant Anthropic saw its revenue surge by 45% to $16.8bn (Â£12.7bn) in the three months to the end of September, the BBC understands.

The figures were revealed by the Claude-developer in a briefing for prospective investors on Wednesday as it lays the groundwork for a stock market listing, which is expected to take place before the end of the year.

It comes as some tech stocks, including firms that make the chips and other hardware that power data centres, have fallen in recent days over concerns about the hundreds of billions of dollars being spent on AI infrastructure.

An Anthropic spokesperson declined to comment.

Anthropic's revenue has risen in successive quarters this year, from $4.7bn in the first three months to $11.6bn the following period.

The company also reportedly told investors during the event at its headquarters in San Francisco that it had made a profit for the second quarter in a row.

Its revenue figures, along with those of rival OpenAI, offer an important gauge of the AI industry's growth and ability to finance the infrastructure needed to develop the technology.

Stocks in some US technology companies dropped on Wednesday over concerns around investments in AI.

Shares in chip makers - including AMD, Nvidia and Intel - fell sharply.

In Asia, shares in Japanese tech investment firm Softbank were down by more than 9% on Thursday. South Korean semiconductor giants also dropped, with Samsung falling by 9.5% and SK Hynix 11% lower.

Tech-heavy indexes in the region were also down. Trading on South Korea's Kospi and Kosdaq was temporarily halted after falling by more than 8%, while Japan's Nikkei 225 lost close to 5%.

World.title: Military Plane Crash: Igbokoda communities petition Tinubu
World.content:
Communities in Igbokoda, Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State, have petitioned President Bola Tinubu over environmental pollution occasioned by the crash of a Nigeria Air force plane in the area on 5 October.

The petition, which was signed by the Olu of Igbokoda, Afolabi Odidiomo, on behalf of the communities, was sent to the president through the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation.

The Chief of Air Staff, Nigerian Air Force, the Ministers of Defence and Environment, the Director-General, NESREA, Director-General, NEMA and the Governor of Ondo State were copied.

The petition comes after over one week of search and rescue operations, which have failed to extract the bodies of all 25 people who were killed, from the swamp into which the plane plunged.

It also comes the same day the Ondo State Government directed its Ministries of Environment and Health to commence the fumigation of the water and the supply of clean water to the community as an immediate response to the suspected pollution of the water due to the crash.

The NAF ATR-42 aircraft

The agencies are also expected to provide nose masks and other health kits to protect the residents from any hazards that may arise from the crash.

The communities noted that the petition was not intended to prejudge the outcome of ongoing investogations or to attribute liability, but was made in the public interest and on behalf of residents who may have been affected by the crash and its aftermath.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

They said beyond the immediate consequences of the accident, there are grave questions about the recovery of the aircraft and any human remains, the possible release of aviation fuel or other hazardous substances, and the effect on the surrounding waters, aquatic life and people whose livelihoods depend on them.

“Reports concerning submerged wreckage and possible fuel leakage have heightened these concerns. The actual extent of any contamination must be determined through proper investigation and scientific testing rather than assumption,” the petition read in part.

“Our people should not be left to speculate about the safety of their waters or bear the consequences of any damage arising from an incident involving a federal government aircraft.

“The possibility that aviation fuel, lubricants or other substances may have entered the surrounding waters requires urgent attention.

“We therefore request an environmental assessment by competent and suitably qualified personnel, with the participation of the relevant federal and state authorities, to include:

a. Collection and laboratory analysis of water and sediment samples from the crash site and potentially affected locations.

b. Examination of the surrounding aquatic environment for evidence of contamination.

c. Assessment of any effect on fish, other aquatic organisms and fishing grounds.

d. Identification of any continuing source of contamination, including leakage from submerged wreckage.

e. Determination of whether the affected waters are safe for fishing, domestic use or other activities.

f. Recommendations for containment, clean-up and restoration to a safe condition.

“The findings, including test results, should be made available to the affected communities, subject to any lawful restrictions for genuine operational or security reasons.”

The communities also demanded that until relevant tests are completed, residents should receive practical guidance on precautions in relation to potentially affected waters and aquatic products.

“We request that the relevant health and environmental agencies:

a. Assess any immediate or potential health risks arising from the incident.

b. Advise residents on the use of water and consumption of fish or aquatic products from affected areas.

c. Provide medical assessment and appropriate treatment for any person suspected of exposure-related illness.

d. Establish a channel for residents to report suspected health effects and obtain reliable information.

e. Arrange further monitoring where a continuing risk is identified,” the petition said.

On the recovery of the aircraft human remains, the petitiion requested an update on the recovery operation, including the condition and location of any remaining wreckage and steps being taken to recover any outstanding human remains, with due regard to safety, environmental protection and preservation of evidence.

“Any human remains yet to be recovered should receive urgent and respectful attention,” the petition stated.

The petitioners noted that Igbokoda residents depend on the waters in the area for their livelihood and requested an assessment of the actual economic consequences, such as identifying fishing grounds and economic activities affected by the crash or safety restrictions; determine persons whose activities have been interrupted or impaired; ascertain any verified loss of equipment, stock, income or property attributable to the incident and determine additional expenditure reasonably incurred as a result of the incident.

They further requested that if contamination is established, the relevant authorities should among other things, contain and remove any identified source of pollution; recover or safely secure wreckage to prevent further harm; clean up affected locations using appropriate methods; restore affected areas as far as reasonably practicable and monitor water quality after initial clean-up.

In demanding for compensation, the petitioners asked for a transparent, fair and accessible claims process for persons who can demonstrate loss or injury attributable to the incident, covering damage to property and equipment, loss of income, reasonable expenses, personal injury and other established losses recognised by law.

Summarising their demands, the communities said, “We respectfully request that the federal government, acting through appropriate institutions and in coordination with Ondo State Government –

“i. Acknowledge this petition and designate the office to coordinate the response.

ii. Provide an update on the recovery of wreckage and human remains.

iii. Arrange an independent environmental assessment of the crash site and surrounding waters.

iv. Investigate fuel leakage or other contamination and contain any hazard.

v. Collect and analyse environmental samples and make findings available.

vi. Issue appropriate public health advice.

vii. Provide medical assessment and assistance to affected persons.

viii. Implement a clean-up and remediation plan if contamination is found.

ix. Establish follow-up monitoring.

x. Assess effects on local livelihoods.

xi. Establish a fair and accessible compensation claims process.

xii. Consider interim assistance for proven immediate hardship.

xiii. Appoint a liaison officer for Igbokoda and affected communities.

xiv. Provide periodic updates and a clear timetable.

xv. Ensure proper inter-agency coordination.

We respectfully request a substantive written response within thirty (30) days from receipt, including steps already taken, agency responsible for each outstanding task, measures for immediate risks, and a timetable. We recognise full investigation and remediation may take longer than 30 days.”

World.title: Ray Ekpu investigative journalism prize opens 2026 entries, increases prize money to N1.75m
World.content:
The Ray Ekpu Prize for Investigative Journalism has opened entries for its 2026 edition, offering a total of N1.75 million to investigative journalists of Akwa Ibom origin, as two new sponsors join the initiative established five years ago to promote accountability journalism.

The Ray Ekpu Prize Committee in a Facebook post on Thursday said entries opened on 5 October and will close on 23 October.

The competition is open to members of the Nigeria Union of Journalists of Akwa Ibom origin who practise in Nigeria.

The 2026 edition is sponsored by the Inoyo Toro Foundation, the Ibom Heritage Preservation Foundation and Umoh Joshua. The latest sponsorship arrangement increases the total prize money from N1 million to N1.75 million.

The overall winner will receive N1 million, while the first and second runners-up will receive N500,000 and N250,000, respectively.

How Inoyo established the prize

The prize was announced in July 2021 by Udom Inoyo, a lawyer and former senior executive of ExxonMobil in Nigeria, as part of efforts to recognise outstanding investigative journalism and encourage journalists to hold public officials accountable.

The Inoyo Toro Foundation formally instituted the award in September 2021, naming it after Ray Ekpu, the veteran Nigerian journalist and co-founder of Newswatch magazine.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The inaugural award through 2023 carried a prize of N500,000 for the winner. However, in 2024 when Thompson & Grace Investment Ltd joined in sponsoring the award, the prize was expanded to accommodate a first runner-up (N300,000) and a second runner-up (N200,000).

At the time, Mr Inoyo described the initiative as a contribution to improving journalism in Akwa Ibom State and Nigeria. He said the award was intended to reward quality, factual investigative reporting and encourage journalists to uphold the profession’s watchdog role.

Mr Inoyo, who retired from ExxonMobil after more than three decades of service, rose to become vice-chairman of the company’s Nigerian affiliates. He studied political science and law at the University of Calabar and was called to the Nigerian Bar in 1988.

He established the Inoyo Toro Foundation in 2007 to promote education and human-capital development, including the recognition of teachers and the mentoring of students in Akwa Ibom.

Through the foundation, he has continued to support the journalism award, which has expanded its prize money over the years. The addition of the Ibom Heritage Preservation Foundation and Mr Joshua as joint sponsors for the 2026 edition brings further financial support to the initiative.

The award honours Mr Ekpu, whose career in journalism includes his role in establishing Newswatch in 1985 alongside Dele Giwa, Dan Agbese and Yakubu Mohammed. The magazine became a prominent platform for investigative reporting and political journalism in Nigeria.

PREMIUM TIMES journalists among past honourees

Ekemini Simon, a PREMIUM TIMES reporter, is a four-time winner of the Ray Ekpu Prize, having won the award before joining the newspaper.

Mr Simon was also a runner-up in 2024 edition in which Cletus Ukpong, the regional editor of PREMIUM TIMES, won the prize. Saviour Imukudo, another PREMIUM TIMES journalist, was a runner-up in the 2025 edition.

The journalists’ records reflect the award’s recognition of investigative reporting that check public institutions, exposes wrongdoing and contributes to public accountability.

Eligibility, judging criteria

According to the committee, eligible reports must have been published or broadcast between 21 October 2025 and 20 October 2026. Entries may come from print, online, radio and television journalism.

Applicants must provide evidence of publication or broadcast, including verifiable details of the date, time and media organisation. Television entries must include a video recording of the broadcast.

Entries will be assessed against six criteria: depth of investigation, conformity with the ideals of journalistic excellence, style and language of presentation, contribution to good governance in public office, impact on the fight against corruption and impunity, and contribution to national unity and ethnic cohesion.

The committee said the depth of investigation and journalistic excellence carry 20 points each. Style and language account for 15 points, while the remaining three criteria carry 15 points each.

Interested journalists can apply through rayekpuprize.org by selecting “Apply Now”, creating an account, completing their profiles and submitting their entries.

The committee said the winners would be announced at a public event later this year.

World.title: Gunmen kill traditional ruler in Plateau
World.content:
Gunmen have killed Jatau Samkwar, the Mishkaham Bokkos, at his residence in Daffo, Bokkos Local Government Area of Plateau State.

The traditional ruler was reportedly attacked on Monday night, 12 October, amid security concerns in the area.

The Mwaghavul Traditional Council, Bokkos branch, announced the killing, identifying the attackers as Fulani militias.

However, the identities of the perpetrators have not been independently established.

According to reports, the attackers invaded the monarch’s residence and shot him in the legs.

He was initially taken to a hospital in Daffo before being referred to another medical facility, where he reportedly died.

Kefas Mallai, chairman of the Community Peace Observers in Bokkos, confirmed the incident and expressed concern over the recurring attacks in the area.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Mallai also disclosed that the traditional ruler’s son had reportedly been abducted but regained his freedom on Sunday, a day before the attack on his father.

As of the time of filing this report, the Mwaghavul Chiefdom and the Mwaghavul Development Association had yet to issue official statements on the attack.

Efforts to obtain comments from the Plateau State Police Command spokesperson, Alfred Alabo, were unsuccessful, as his telephone lines were unreachable as of the time of filing this report.

The killing comes amid security challenges in Bokkos and other parts of Plateau State, where communities have experienced recurring attacks, killings and abductions.

In a related incident, three people travelling on a motorcycle along a road linking communities in the area were reportedly attacked. Two of them were killed, while the third sustained injuries.

The latest killing has raised fresh concerns about the safety of residents and traditional institutions in Plateau State, particularly in communities that have experienced repeated security threats.

World.title: Injury Update: Super Eagles striker Umar Sadiq nears Valencia return
World.content:
Super Eagles striker Umar Sadiq has offered an encouraging update on his recovery from injury, revealing that he could return to team training with Valencia soon, provided he comes through his latest medical assessment without complications.

The Nigerian forward has been sidelined since sustaining the injury in September, shortly before Valencia’s meeting with FC Barcelona, bringing his promising start to the campaign to a temporary halt.

Sadiq had opened his goalscoring account for the season against Deportivo La Coruña before the setback forced him out of action. He has subsequently missed five league fixtures against Barcelona, Sevilla, Alavés, Real Sociedad and Racing Santander.

However, the 29-year-old is hopeful of rejoining his teammates after saying he is nearing the final stages of his recovery.

Speaking to the media during the club’s meet-and-greet event, Sadiq disclosed that he was scheduled to undergo further tests on Thursday to determine whether he could resume training.

“Yes, I think I’m almost back. Just a few more steps before I rejoin the team,” Sadiq was quoted as saying by AS.

“Tomorrow (Thursday) I have to have some tests done and, if everything goes as planned, I think it will be very soon.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The update will boost Valencia, who will be eager to have the Nigerian striker available again as they look to improve their fortunes this season. His return would also allow the forward to work under new manager Javier Aguirre for the first time since the coach’s arrival.

Sadiq backs Aguirre as Valencia target improvement

Sadiq also spoke positively about the atmosphere within the Valencia dressing room, expressing his support for Aguirre and the manager’s efforts to create a positive environment around the squad.

The striker said the players were approaching their work one step at a time while staying committed to helping the club achieve its objectives.

“We’re doing well. We’re trying to bring a lot of positivity, as you saw in the last match,” he added.

“We’re taking it one step at a time, and we all support the new coach. Yes, I’ve spoken to him.

“He told me to get well soon and that he’s waiting for me, because he knows what I can contribute to the team.”

Aguirre’s message appears to have reassured Sadiq about the role he could play once he returns to full fitness. The coach’s eagerness to welcome him back also suggests that the forward remains part of Valencia’s plans as they seek greater consistency.

Having missed the opening fixtures of Aguirre’s tenure, Sadiq will be keen to make up for lost time and demonstrate his value when he is cleared to return.

The Nigerian’s immediate priority, however, will be completing his recovery without rushing back before he is ready. Thursday’s tests should provide a clearer indication of his progress and the possibility of a return to training.

The Goal is to take Valencia where it deserves to be — Sadiq

Despite his absence, Sadiq insists the club’s collective ambition remains clear: to help Valencia reach the level their history and stature demand.

The striker stressed that the objective goes beyond individual contributions, emphasising that every squad member shares responsibility for improving the club’s position.

“The goal is to take Valencia to where it deserves to be. That’s not just my goal, but the goal of all the players,” he concluded.

Sadiq will now hope his recovery proceeds as planned, allowing him to return to the pitch and begin working under Aguirre. After making a positive start to the campaign before his injury, the Super Eagles forward has an opportunity to regain momentum and establish himself in the new manager’s plans.

For Valencia, his return would provide another attacking option as the club pursues its ambitions. For Sadiq, the next step is clear: pass his medical checks, return to training and turn his optimism into a timely comeback.

World.title: Plateau motorists pay ₦1,420 for petrol at NNPC stations as other outlets charge ₦1,492
World.content:
Motorists in Jos, Plateau State, are paying between ₦1,420 and ₦1,492 per litre of petrol, a market survey by this newspaper has shown, amid a federal government intervention aimed at cushioning the impact of rising fuel prices.

PREMIUM TIMES’ checks at filling stations across the Plateau State capital on Wednesday, 14 October, showed that outlets operated by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) sold petrol at ₦1,420 per litre, while other filling stations charged between ₦1,472 and ₦1,492.

The findings come days after the federal government announced a temporary arrangement under which NNPCL Retail would forgo its retail profit margin and sell petrol at cost for an initial 30-day period.

The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, announced the measures on 8 October during a briefing in Abuja on rising fuel prices and the government’s response to increasing energy costs.

The government subsequently issued a statement confirming the arrangement.

Under the initiative, NNPCL Retail agreed to forgo its retail profit margin and sell petrol at cost for 30 days, with priority given to public transport operators.

The government said the measure was intended to provide temporary relief to households and businesses affected by rising fuel prices.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

At the same briefing, Mr Oyedele said the government was negotiating a ceiling of ₦1,350 per litre on petrol’s landing or ex-gantry cost under a proposed price-modulation mechanism.

The proposed ceiling was not a fixed nationwide pump price. Rather, it was intended to help moderate the impact of fluctuations in international crude oil prices and exchange rates on petrol costs.

The distinction is important in assessing the prices recorded in Plateau, where NNPCL outlets surveyed sold petrol at ₦1,420 per litre.

At other filling stations surveyed, motorists paid ₦52 to ₦72 more per litre than at NNPCL outlets.

However, some motorists who spoke to this newspaper said they preferred purchasing petrol from other outlets, citing concerns about the accuracy of dispensing pumps at some NNPCL stations.

They alleged that some pumps did not dispense the quantity of petrol indicated on their meters, raising concerns about whether customers received the full quantity for which they paid.

The allegations could not be independently verified as of the time of filing this report.

Independent testing by the relevant authorities would be required to establish whether the pumps dispense accurate quantities.

The price differences also have financial implications for motorists and commercial transport operators who depend heavily on petrol.

A motorist buying 40 litres at ₦1,492 per litre would pay ₦59,680, compared with ₦56,800 at ₦1,420 per litre. The difference amounts to ₦2,880 for the same quantity of fuel.

For commercial drivers who purchase petrol frequently, such differences can increase operating costs and put additional pressure on transport fares and household spending.

The findings highlight the importance of transparent retail pricing and effective consumer protection as the federal government implements measures to moderate the impact of rising fuel costs.

As of the time of filing this report, NNPCL’s response to the price differences and the allegations concerning its dispensing pumps had not been obtained.

World.title: Katsina health professionals declare 7-day warning strike
World.content:
The Assembly of Healthcare Professionals has declared a seven-day warning strike over the state government’s failure to address its demands for improved allowances and salary adjustments fully.

The assembly’s chairman, Ibrahim Balange, announced the decision on Wednesday, saying the strike would begin at midnight on 14 October.

The unions under the assembly include the Medical and Health Workers Union of Nigeria (MHWUN), the National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives (NANNM), and the National Union of Allied Health Professionals (NUAHP).

Mr Balange said the assembly issued a seven-day strike notice to the government on 7 October, but the expiration of the notice did not yield satisfactory resolution of the outstanding issues.

He said the struggle for improved allowances began in 2024, when the state government indicated its intention to review the benefits of healthcare professionals in line with what is obtained in the federal government service.

According to him, the workers were shortchanged during the implementation of the minimum wage, prompting them to complain that the salary table approved for their members differed from what they were being paid.

He said a committee was later established to investigate the matter and made recommendations in March 2025, but the government had not yet implemented them.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Balange explained that the workers were later engaged by the Office of Public Service Reform, which offered them 10 per cent of the difference between their salaries and those of their counterparts in federal institutions.

He said the assembly rejected the offer and issued a three-week ultimatum to the government, which was later extended by one week following further engagements.

According to him, the workers suspended plans to commence a strike on 7 September after some stakeholders intervened and promised to address their concerns.

He, however, said the assembly was later informed that the governor had approved a 15 per cent increment, only five percentage points higher than the previous offer.

Mr Balange expressed dissatisfaction that the assembly was not involved in preparing the salary adjustment table or determining the increment before the decision was communicated to it.

He said the assembly demanded full implementation of the allowances and salary structure applicable to healthcare professionals in the federal government service, but had indicated its willingness to accept 75 per cent as a compromise.

“Some of our members have not even agreed to 75 per cent, but we have to look at the matter holistically and consider how to move forward,” he said.

Mr Balange warned that the disparity in remuneration could undermine the state’s healthcare system, noting that Katsina had previously been regarded as one of the states with relatively attractive healthcare employment conditions.

He said the assembly remained open to negotiations with the government but insisted on improving the allowances to ensure fairness and retain healthcare professionals in the state.

The chairman said the assembly would reconvene after the seven-day warning strike to review the outcome and decide on next steps.

He warned that failure to reach an agreement with the government could lead to an ultimatum for an indefinite strike, adding that the industrial action was being undertaken in accordance with labour laws.

Mr Balange apologised to the government and the public for any inconvenience the strike might cause, while reaffirming the assembly’s commitment to protecting its members’ welfare and professional interests. (NAN)

World.title: 2027: Tinubu’s grip on Nigeria worse than Abacha – Dele Momodu
World.content:
Veteran journalist and African Democratic Congress (ADC) chieftain, Dele Momodu, has described President Bola Tinubu’s growing political influence as worse than what Nigeria experienced under the late military ruler, Sani Abacha.

Mr Momodu, who is the Deputy Director-General of the ADC’s 2027 Presidential Campaign Council, made the remarks on Wednesday evening during an interview on Arise TV’s Prime Time.

This came hours after Mr Tinubu inaugurated the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council for the 2027 election.

The ADC chieftain criticised the inclusion of opposition politicians, including Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke, Anambra State Governor Chukwuma Soludo and Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, in the APC campaign structure.

He likened the development to the political consolidation witnessed during the Abacha era.

“Today, Tinubu has virtually taken over everything: the executive, the legislature, the judiciary. Almost everything under Tinubu is worse than what we fought against,” Mr Momodu said.

He was responding to concerns that Nigeria could be moving towards a one-party dominant system ahead of the 2027 election.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Former vice-president and ADC’s presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, also criticised the expanded campaign council, describing it as a “crowded confession of Tinubu’s fear”. Atiku accused the president of using political alliances to shield his administration from criticism over economic hardship and insecurity.

Opposition figures in APC council

Mr Tinubu inaugurated his presidential campaign council in Abuja on Wednesday as political parties intensify preparations for the 16 January 2027 presidential election.

The council includes several serving politicians outside the APC, notably Mr Adeleke, Mr Soludo and Mr Wike, who have been assigned roles relating to the president’s campaign in their respective areas.

Mr Momodu said the participation of opposition politicians does not necessarily translate into support for the president among voters in their states.

He questioned governors’ ability to transfer their personal political support to Mr Tinubu.

“Osun people… supported Ademola Adeleke because he performed, but that support is not unconditional,” he said.

Opposition vote

The ADC chieftain also dismissed suggestions that the presence of Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi and Mr Tinubu in the 2027 race would necessarily divide the opposition vote in a manner that benefits the incumbent.

The three politicians are among the 18 presidential candidates on INEC’s final list for the January election. Mr Tinubu is contesting on the APC platform, Mr Abubakar on the ADC platform and Mr Obi on the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) platform.

Mr Momodu further argued that the ADC candidate remains a formidable opposition contender.

He said Atiku’s experience as a former vice president and his political reach across the northern states would make him competitive in the election.

INEC allegation

Mr Momodu also alleged that Mr Tinubu had “proliferated INEC with people from Yoruba land”, suggesting that the appointments could affect confidence in the commission’s neutrality.

INEC has published the final list of 18 presidential candidates for the election scheduled for January 2027, with the commission also continuing preparations under the revised electoral timetable.

Mr Momodu said opposition parties are working behind the scenes to counter what he described as the ruling party’s growing political influence.

“We are not going to come in public and say this, but we know what to do to make sure that he does not get that second term. And we also know that some of the people pretending to be supporting him today, and I’m not trying to trivialise this thing. I know some of them; they are praying fervently that they will not have to go through this thing where governors become like houseboys,” he said.

World.title: Court convicts 19 in Kebbi over terrorism, illegal firearms, cable vandalism
World.content:
The Federal High Court in Birnin Kebbi has convicted 19 people of offences involving terrorism, unlawful possession of firearms and electricity cable vandalism, following investigations and prosecutions that lasted 17 months.

The Kebbi State Police Command disclosed the convictions in a statement its spokesperson, Bashir Usman, issued on Wednesday.

The court, presided over by Justice Emmanuel Gakko, sentenced two men, Aliyu Hadari and Umar Uzzi, to 15 years’ imprisonment on each of three counts involving terrorism, providing logistical support to an armed terrorist group and conspiracy to commit terrorism.

The offences were prosecuted under the Terrorism (Prevention and Prohibition) Act, 2022.

The police said the two men were arrested along Yauri Road while travelling in a vehicle acquired to transport kidnapped victims to a forest hideout.

The court also ordered the forfeiture of the vehicle and a Bajaj motorcycle to the federal government after finding that they were connected to the offences.

The police did not indicate whether the prison terms would run concurrently or consecutively.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Eleven convicted over illegal firearms

The court also convicted 11 people of unlawful possession of firearms, with prison sentences ranging from two to six years.

Among them was Ripin Liu, a Chinese national arrested with a locally made Beretta pistol. He was sentenced to six years’ imprisonment with an option of a fine.

Mohammed Ibrahim, also known as Banki, received four years’ imprisonment without an option of a fine, while Abubakar Siddi was sentenced to three years without an option of a fine.

Four others, Mohammed Bako, Bello Dantiye, Aliyu Dandaula and Abubakar Usman, received three-year prison sentences each, also without the option of a fine.

Buba Umaru, who was arrested in Bagudo Local Government Area after allegedly crossing from a neighbouring country with a locally fabricated pistol, was sentenced to three years’ imprisonment.

John Zweme received two years and six months’ imprisonment with an option of a fine, while Aliyu Bako and Sani Alaramma were each sentenced to two years, also with an option of a fine.

The police recovered 11 firearms during the investigations, including locally fabricated pistols and dane guns.

The statement did not disclose the amounts of the fines imposed as alternatives to imprisonment.

Six jailed for cable theft

Six other people were convicted of vandalising and stealing electricity cables in Sakaba Local Government Area.

They are Sani Tanko, Ibrahim Hamza, Samson Sunday, Abdulrahman Isah, Adamu Musa and Masudu.

The police said the theft disrupted electricity supply to communities in the area.

The convicts received prison sentences ranging from three to eight years, although the command did not specify their individual terms.

The convictions followed police operations across Yauri, Bagudo, Sakaba and other parts of Kebbi State.

The Commissioner of Police, Umar Hadejia, commended the investigators and prosecuting counsel for pursuing the cases over 17 months.

He also praised the trial judge and said the command would continue operations against terrorism, illegal firearms possession and vandalism of public infrastructure.

Mr Hadejia appealed to residents to report suspicious movements and activities, promising that the police would act on credible information.

World.title: Martinez blames ‘anger’ for dig at Man Utd hierarchy
World.content:
Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez said “anger and frustration” at defeat to Atletico Madrid led to his swipe at the club’s board for a lack of investment in the transfer market.

The English giants lost 2-0 in Spain on Tuesday in the Champions League. They are also off to their worst start to a Premier League season for 40 years.

Martinez took aim at technical director Jason Wilcox, saying he “100 percent” expected more investment in the squad during the transfer window after United finished third in the Premier League last season to return to Europe’s top competition.

United signed three midfielders — Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos — for around £150 million ($198 million), but their spending fell far short of some of their Premier League rivals.

“After the match, I spoke out of anger and frustration at not getting the result we all wanted,” Martinez posted on social media.

The Argentine international’s comments were backed by some fans, but Martinez has been criticised for his own part in United’s poor start to the season.

He scored an own goal in a 1-1 draw at bottom-of-the-table Fulham last month and was outmuscled by Dominic Solanke as 10-man Tottenham salvaged a point at Old Trafford last weekend.

“When I talk about wanting more, I’m talking about the ambition we must all have as part of this club. To keep growing, to become stronger and to have everything we need to compete at the highest level.

“These are standards we must all hold ourselves to, starting with me.

“I believe in my team-mates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward. I’m convinced that the way forward is to keep working together, with ambition and commitment.”

The pressure is rising on United boss Michael Carrick just months after he was handed the job on a permanent basis.

Carrick’s men travel to historic rivals Leeds on Sunday before another Champions League trip, to Italian side Como, on Wednesday.

AFP

World.title: ‘Local champion’  -  Donald Duke replies Gov Diri over Lagos-Calabar coastal road
World.content:
Presidential candidate of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Donald Duke, has described Bayelsa State Governor Douye Diri as a “local champion” following the governor’s criticism of his position on the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway.

Duke, a former governor of Cross River State, responded to Diri during an interview on Arise Television’s The Morning Show on Thursday, insisting that the coastal road project was not feasible because of its cost and the terrain it would traverse.

Diri had expressed disappointment with Duke’s earlier claim that constructing the highway through Bayelsa would be impracticable because of the state’s swampy terrain.

The Bayelsa governor, through his Chief Press Secretary, Daniel Alabrah, argued that Duke was out of touch with developments in the state, where his administration had built roads and bridges across swamps and mangroves.

“Clearly, he is not abreast of current developments in road construction and infrastructure development in our state,” Diri said.

Responding, the PRP candidate dismissed Diri’s defence of the project, saying the governor was viewing the matter from a state-level perspective rather than considering the wider implications for Nigeria.

“And the governor of Bayelsa, if he did say so, I don’t know the fellow, but if he did say so, I think he’s just being a local champion,” Duke said.

He added that his regional origin did not prevent him from assessing the project from a national perspective.

“I’m from the South-South. I’m a Nigerian. South-South just happens to be where I originated from. But I’m looking at the totality of Nigeria,” he said.

Duke maintained that Nigeria lacked the financial capacity to undertake the project, arguing that the government was already borrowing to fund infrastructure development.

“It’s just not feasible. We don’t have the kind of money to do it. We’re literally borrowing to even stretch Epe stretch. We’re borrowing. We can’t do it,” he said.

Duke also questioned the decision to divert a section of the road to the East-West Road, asking whether the existing highway had been considered from the start of the project.

“Now, they have said that they’re going to divert the road onto the East-West Highway. Weren’t they aware of the East-West Highway from get-go?” he asked.

World.title: Man,​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍​‍⁠‌​‌‍​‌​ 40, dies in attack on Accord supporters in Ibadan – Police
World.content:
The Police Command in Oyo State has confirmed the death of one Azeez Tajudeen, 40, following Wednesday’s attack on supporters of the Accord governorship candidate, Alhaji Oriyomi Hamzat, in Ibadan.

The command’s spokesperson, DSP Olayinka Ayanlade, confirmed the death in a statement issued on Thursday in Ibadan.

He said the incident happened around the Molete area of Ibadan during a procession organised to welcome Hamzat back home from the United Kingdom.

According to him, a complainant reported to the police that the group was attacked by suspected hoodlums shortly after leaving Molete while proceeding toward Agidigbo office on Iwo Road.

“During the attack, one Azeez Tajudeen, aged 40, a native of Oke Amu in Itesiwaju Local Government Area of Oyo State, sustained a severe injury to his right eye.

“He was immediately rushed for medical attention and subsequently taken to State Hospital, Ring Road, Ibadan, where he was examined and confirmed dead.

“His remains have since been deposited at the hospital’s morgue,” Ayanlade said.

The police spokesperson said the state Commissioner of Police, Abimbola Olugbenga, had directed that the case be transferred to the Command Monitoring Unit for investigation.

Ayanlade urged political aspirants, party leaders, and event organisers to formally notify the command at least 48 hours before any planned gathering takes place.

He said this would enable adequate security arrangements, prevent breaches of public peace, and safeguard participants and other members of the public. (NAN)

World.title: Netanyahu’s main rival vows to defeat Hamas within 18 months if elected PM
World.content:
Photo: Oded Balilty/AP

Israeli opposition politician Gadi Eisenkot, Prime Miniter Benjamin Netanyahu’s main rival in upcoming elections, vowed Thursday to defeat Hamas in Gaza if he becomes prime minister following the October 27 vote.

“Today I give a public commitment: from the moment I enter the Prime Minister’s Office, within 18 months Hamas will no longer rule the Gaza Strip,” the leader of the centre-right Yashar party said at a press conference near the war-ravaged Palestinian territory.

He said he would achieve this either by implementing US President Donald Trump’s ceasefire plan for Gaza, which provides for the gradual disarmament of Hamas and a transfer of power, or through “creative operations” by Israel’s military aimed at destroying the Palestinian movement’s military wing.

World.title: UCH resident doctors suspend warning strike
World.content:
University College Hospital, UCH

The Association of Resident Doctors (ARD), University College Hospital (UCH), Ibadan, has suspended its three-day warning strike and directed members to resume duty on Thursday.

The association announced the suspension in a memo issued to members and made available to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in Ibadan on Thursday.

The association’s president, Dr Uthman Adedeji and general secretary, Dr Mary Awodiji, jointly signed the memo.

“Sequel to the resolutions of the Emergency General Meeting (EGM), held on Thursday, Oct. 8, members are hereby informed that the 3-day warning strike has been completed.

“Consequently, work resumes today, Thursday, Oct. 15, by 8.00 a.m.,” the memo said.

It enjoined all members to promptly resume at their respective duty posts, adding that congress would receive updates on stipulated timelines in the coming days.

NAN recalls that ARD-UCH embarked on the three-day warning strike on Monday over persistent electricity crisis and chronic water shortage at the College of Medicine axis of the hospital.

The association is demanding immediate restoration of electricity to the area, urgent repair of all faulty circuit breakers as backups, and uninterrupted electricity supply to every part of the hospital.

It also issued a seven-day ultimatum to UCH management from Oct. 12 to Oct. 19, after which it said it might proceed with an indefinite strike should the demands remain unmet. (NAN)

World.title: Meet Albanian who may be world’s oldest woman at 117
World.content:
The 117-year-old Qamile Marra holds a black and white photograph from her youth during an interview with AFP in the garden of her home in the village of Ferras, near Kucove, some 80 kilometres from the capital Tirana on October 3, 2026. At 117, Qamile Marra’s priority isn’t proving she’s the world’s oldest woman, or even convincing Albanian pension authorities she’s not dead. For the woman who was born under Ottoman rule, turned 36 a fortnight before the end of World War II and outlived Albania’s communist dictatorship, her focus remains firmly on enjoying life. (Photo by Adnan Beci / AFP)

At 117, Qamile Marra is not particularly concerned with proving she may be the world’s oldest woman — or even persuading Albanian pension officials that she is not dead.

For a woman born under Ottoman rule, who turned 36 a fortnight before the end of World War II and outlived Albania’s communist dictatorship, her focus remains firmly on enjoying life.

“Life is beautiful, like Mount Tomorr in bloom,” she told AFP with a smile, referring to one of Albania’s loftiest peaks as she sat outside her home in Ferras, about 100 kilometres (60 miles) south of the capital.

Surrounded by fruit trees, Marra has spent almost her entire life in the village, growing her own food and tending livestock.

“You live as long as God has decreed,” she said, her deeply wrinkled face framed by a traditional white headscarf.

According to her birthdate as listed on several official documents — August 19, 1909 — Marra would be two days older than Britain’s Ethel Caterham, recognised by Guinness World Records as the world’s oldest living woman.

Definitively proving the age of “supercentenarians” can be difficult.

Many of the people famous for living the longest are from places where shoddy recordkeeping and suspected pension fraud are rampant, according to a study that won the 2024 Ig Nobel prize, which awards offbeat scientific research.

But Marra has extensive records that appear to confirm her age.

Her relatives have contacted Guinness and hold a birth certificate issued in 1945, a passport issued in 1978 and a recent identity card, all showing the same date of birth.

Her age even surprised local authorities, who stopped her pension when she turned 100, according to her 80-year-old son Hysen.

“They didn’t believe my mother was still alive,” he said, recalling how he had to show proof, including witness statements, to resume the meagre payments.

Earlier this month, the government issued her a special state pension to mark her age.

– What’s the secret? –

Perhaps the answer lies in Marra’s habits and lifestyle.

She rises early to sweep the yard, water her flowers and feed the chickens before settling down with her favourite coffee.

She still enjoys regular walks through her carefully tended orchard with her son, who lives with her, stopping to pick ripe pomegranates along the way.

She also slips basil leaves in her pockets to “enjoy the aroma”.

Whatever the secret, her son says she has never even visited a doctor.

“She is in good health and has never taken any medication.”

– Five generations –

Marra’s husband died 36 years ago, but she still smiles when talking about their decades together — an arranged marriage, but a loving one.

“Otherwise, how could I have had seven children with him?” she said.

She has now seen five generations of her family grow up around her.

Tears welled up as she remembered the family and friends she had lost. But her face brightened when a niece called to chat.

“I’ve watched them get engaged, marry and build their own homes and lives,” she said.

“When I see people coming and going in the house, I am so happy.”

From her own youth, she has kept a single photograph: a near-century-old picture of a young woman wearing a white scarf just like the one she had on.

“I was 18!” she said.

AFP

World.title: Referees must protect players like me, Yamal, Álvarez – Vini Jr
World.content:
Real Madrid’s Brazilian forward #07 Vinicius Junior (C) is restrained by teammates as he argues with referee Isidro Escuderos after receiving a red card during the Spanish league football match between Real Madrid CF and Villarreal CF at the Santiago Bernabeu Stadium in Madrid on October 10, 2026. (Photo by Oscar DEL POZO / AFP)

Real Madrid forward Vinícius Jr has called on referees to give greater protection to attacking players, naming himself, Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal and Atlético Madrid’s Julián Álvarez among those he believes need better treatment on the pitch.

The Brazilian forward broke his silence after he was handed a four-match ban on Wednesday y after being sent off during Saturday’s 1-0 La Liga win over Villarreal for pulling the hair of an opponent.

Speaking to Spanish newspaper Marca, the Brazilian said, “I think the punishment came at a bad time. They had the whole day to announce the decision, but I found out about it when I arrived at the stadium. The rule is new, and La Liga officials always come to explain the new amendments to us, but they did not explain this particular rule to us.”

He added: “I have never committed a violent act against another player. I get kicked a lot, and yet I feel that referees show me cards very easily.”

The 25-year-old also stressed the need for referees to protect players capable of influencing matches, citing Yamal and Álvarez alongside himself.

“The fans have to boo me because I’m here to score goals against their teams, but I don’t understand the referees, because I’ve seen a statistic that says I get 500 fouls for five red cards and I don’t know how many yellow cards, and the yellow cards are always for Vini. I don’t understand. We have to defend the players who do things differently, like Lamine at Barcelona or Julián at Atlético,” he said.

Reflecting on his career at Real Madrid, Vinícius recalled joining the Spanish club at 18 and facing doubts about his ability to score goals.

“Remember, I arrived at 18 years old and many people laughed at me. They said I can’t score, then I had more than 100 goals for Madrid,” he said.

World.title: Musk calls on Zelensky to ‘go’ as Ukraine leader
World.content:
Ukraine President, Zelensky

Tech billionaire Elon Musk called on Wednesday for Volodymyr Zelensky to “go” as Ukraine’s president, as Kyiv raised doubts over US support for the war-torn country.

Ukraine accused the United States this week of helping Russia by failing to warn it of incoming missile strikes and hobbling Kyiv’s military response through changes to Musk’s satellite system which it uses for communications.

“And so the slaughter continues,” Musk wrote on X. “Time for Zelensky to go.”

Zelensky had called on Musk to restore Starlink, which was designed by the mogul’s SpaceX company and which Kyiv says has been slowed down.

Musk said any disruption was the responsibility of the US government.

He drew a distinction between Starshield, which Ukraine relies on for battlefield communications and which he said was controlled by the US government, and the Starlink civilian satellite system, which Ukraine also deploys but is not allowed to use for offensive operations.

The row comes after Zelensky replied in the affirmative when asked if he felt “betrayed” after US President Donald Trump announced a diesel-supply deal with heavily sanctioned Moscow.

A senior official in Kyiv also said that the United States had in recent days threatened to stop providing intelligence about Russian missile launches that Ukraine uses to thwart attacks — which Trump has denied.

Trump, facing key midterm elections next month in which soaring fuel prices are a major issue, has blamed Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries for the squeeze on supplies and increase in prices at the pump.

World.title: RMB Nigeria Asset Management Wins Excellence Award
World.content:
RMB Nigeria Asset Management Limited has been honoured with the Excellence in Investment Management award at the 2026 Banks and Other Financial Institutions (BAFI) Awards, celebrating the firm’s exceptional performance and dedication to delivering superior investment solutions.

This prestigious category win recognises RMB Nigeria Asset Management’s rigorous investment expertise, disciplined risk management, and steadfast commitment to generating sustainable, long-term value for its clients.

Commenting on the recognition, Chief Executive Officer of RMB Nigeria Asset Management Limited, Kike Mesubi, said:

“This recognition reflects our commitment to disciplined investment management, informed decision-making and a clear understanding of our clients’ objectives. In a market shaped by changing economic conditions, our focus remains on applying rigorous analysis and sound risk management to deliver investment solutions aligned with our clients’ needs and long-term goals.

We are proud of this recognition and remain committed to creating lasting value for the clients that place their trust in us.”

Operating in a dynamic financial landscape, the firm offers a diverse suite of tailored investment solutions spanning money market, fixed income, bespoke solutions, access to offshore investments and alternative investment solutions. These solutions are designed to align with the return and risk objectives and financial objectives of individual, corporate and institutional investors.

This recognition reflects the firm’s focus on combining macroeconomic insight, investment expertise and a client-centric approach to navigating evolving market conditions and changing investor behavior.

World.title: The Clear Corridor to Oke Mosan: How Ogun’s Political Calculus Shifted After the INEC Ballot Shake-Up
World.content:
By Kunle Somorin

History, as the venerable English historian Thomas Carlyle once postulated, is ultimately shaped by the interplay of persistent preparation and the sudden, unyielding turns of fate.
