World.title: Estonia would allow criminal proceeds to be confiscated without a conviction
World.content:
Estonia plans to work with other European Union countries to amend legislation to allow assets obtained through criminal activity to be confiscated even without a criminal conviction.

It was about six years ago that the Supreme Court ruled to permanently terminate criminal proceedings against Edgar Savisaar who had been accused of corruption. The court found that Savisaar was so seriously ill that even if convicted, he would be unable to serve a sentence.

Similarly, no one was convicted in the lengthy Port of Tallinn corruption trial. In that case, the court ruled that the alleged corruption offenses had passed the statute of limitations.

Under a plan agreed upon by European Union member states, it would in the future be possible to confiscate assets belonging to individuals or companies even without a criminal conviction, provided a court determines that the assets are of criminal origin.

This would be possible, for example, if a suspect becomes seriously ill, evades proceedings or the statute of limitations on the offense has expired.

So far, only a small proportion of criminal proceeds have been successfully confiscated, both in Estonia and across Europe more broadly. In large-scale fraud cases, for example, it may be possible to clearly establish that assets were obtained illegally, while proving the precise role of each participant is more difficult.

"If these assets were obtained through criminal activity, terminating the proceedings would essentially mean that the criminal proceeds would remain in the hands of those who committed the offenses, allowing them to profit from their crimes. The process involves proving where the assets came from and establishing that they are of criminal origin, meaning they were obtained as a result of a crime. Once that has been proven, the assets can be confiscated," explained Andreas Kangur, head of the Penal Law and Procedure Division at the Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs.

The European Convention on Human Rights states that everyone charged with a criminal offense is presumed innocent until proven guilty according to law. The same principle is enshrined in Estonia's Constitution.

Kangur also emphasized that confiscating criminal assets in this way must not involve labeling someone a criminal, even implicitly.

"The European Court of Human Rights has ruled on such cases and found that, as long as someone is not explicitly labeled a criminal, confiscation without a criminal conviction does not violate the presumption of innocence under the European Convention on Human Rights," Kangur said.

Chief State Prosecutor Alar Lehesmets said that confiscating assets without a criminal conviction is far from unprecedented.

Alar Lehesmets. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

"Many European countries have had such measures in place for a long time, including the Netherlands, Belgium and France. Sweden has had a similar provision for several years. Estonia is by no means breaking new ground here. On the contrary, we are actually lagging behind and are only now taking steps to combat crime that more progressive countries have already taken," Lehesmets said.

Estonia is therefore moving in step with other European Union member states in adopting the so-called asset recovery and confiscation directive. In fact, Estonia is already running behind schedule, as member states agreed to adopt the legislation by the end of November.

"Drafting this legislation has not been easy for us. Some of the measures that, as I understand it, have become fairly widely accepted in many European countries still seem quite radical to us," Kangur said.

World.title: Ministry of Culture drops plan to slash county library funding
World.content:
Minister of Culture Heidy Purga told Kuku Radio that a previously planned cut in state funding for public libraries next year has now been scrapped.

Purga said the decision was the result of negotiations between the ministry and libraries. She noted that public libraries form an important cultural and community network in Estonia.

"We at the Ministry of Culture have found the funding needed to maintain the subsidy and next year we will be able to provide it at the same level," Purga said. She added that this would not involve cutting anyone else's operating subsidies.

Purga said that, in addition to subsidies for acquiring library materials, the Ministry of Culture also supports the development of public library collections and services through other measures. "The library accelerator program, which is aimed at libraries in various local municipalities, has gotten off to a very good start," she said.

Last week, Ministry of Culture library adviser Ülle Talihärm told ERR that €1.77 million had been earmarked for public library acquisitions in 2027, compared with €1.87 million last year. "The decrease is linked to the 10 percent budget cut spread across multiple years in the state budget," Talihärm said.

World.title: Photos: Ülle Madise meets Alexander Stubb in Helsinki on 2nd foreign trip
World.content:
This was Madise's second official foreign trip since being sworn in at the start of the week.

She said a stronger Europe strengthens NATO, and welcomed Finland's move to halt issuing tourist visas to Russian citizens.

"Finland is Estonia's close friend and a reliable ally. Our security depends on allies we can trust, and on being worthy of their trust ourselves," Madise said. She noted there is something in the bond between Estonia and Finland that both peoples understand the same way, given their two languages are closely related.

"We know what that word means. It is a wonderful word in both Finnish and Estonian," she said.

On European security, Madise stressed that a stronger Europe strengthens NATO.

"Europe must take greater responsibility for its own defense and turn investments into means of defending people. This also helps keep the United States engaged. A strong political will and readiness to respond to hybrid threats are also needed," Madise said.

She welcomed Finland's initiative to stop issuing tourist visas to Russian citizens entirely, and stressed the need to prevent Russian fighters from entering the Schengen area.

She agreed with Stubb that international law primarily protects small and medium-sized countries. "A rules- and obligations-based international order is ultimately beneficial to most countries and to every person," she went on.

Madise reiterated that Estonia stands firmly with Ukraine. "Ukrainians have the right to live freely in their own country, and that right is defended by the UN Charter and the Helsinki Final Act. We do not recognize borders changed by force. A just and lasting peace must allow people to rebuild their lives without fear of losing their homes again."

The Estonian president stressed that it is Ukraine that gets to decide its own future, and that Europe must be at the table when its security is at stake. She also reaffirmed Estonia's support for Ukraine's progress towards the EU and an open path to NATO membership.

Madise's first official foreign visit as head of state took place on Tuesday, when she met Latvian President Edgars Rinkēvičs in Riga.

World.title: Tallinn French Lyceum struggling with leaky sports hall roof
World.content:
The Tallinn French Lyceum's sports hall began leaking even before it opened, but the leak has now become so severe that the school has suspended use of the building for several days.

The Tallinn French Lyceum's sports hall was officially opened in October 2018. Principal Peter Pedak told ERR that the building had actually begun leaking even before it opened.

"Water has never come in as heavily as it is now, but there have been leaks before," Pedak acknowledged.

According to Pedak, the current, more serious leak is likely caused by a blockage in the rainwater drainage system. However, a camera inspection scheduled for Wednesday should help determine whether that is the case. The school closed the sports hall on Tuesday and Wednesday to investigate the problem.

The principal noted that the sports hall's roof also serves as a walkable surface and is partially covered by a flower bed.

"We are not entirely sure how well it is waterproofed," Pedak admitted. "In short, we first need to establish what is causing the leaks and then draw up a plan with the school's governing authority, the Tallinn Education Department. We have been in close contact with them on this issue and I hope that, now that the situation has become truly critical, we can get the building repaired more quickly."

However, leaks are not the relatively new sports hall's only problem, as there are also cracks in its ceiling. Asked whether these were construction defects, Pedak said that was a more complicated issue. He explained that the cracks are located above the panels and are generally not considered to pose an immediate danger.

The school does not have funding in its budget for major construction work. While the lyceum is commissioning the camera inspection itself, any major repairs, should they prove necessary, would be the responsibility of the Education Department. What happens next will depend on the inspection results. Once the causes of the rainwater entering the building have been identified, a repair plan can be drawn up and the costs estimated.

The principal hopes the building can continue to be used in the near future. The current closure for a few days will not disrupt physical education classes, as these are being held outdoors anyway until the fall break.

Tallinn Education Department spokesperson Sille Tiitsmaa said the sports hall's current problem is water accumulating on the roof and leaking into the building. She said this was caused by a blocked drainage system that prevents rainwater from draining off the roof quickly enough.

Tiitsmaa confirmed that the Education Department has been in close contact with the school and has supported its efforts to resolve the problem.

"At present, there is no reason to plan more extensive renovations of the sports hall or a roof replacement as the problem is caused by a blockage in the drainage system, which is currently being addressed," Tiitsmaa added.

World.title: Iraq discusses $250 million Kempinski hotel project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s National Investment Commission (NIC) is exploring a $250 million luxury hotel complex to be operated by worldwide hospitality giant Kempinski, after talks with a team headed by Iraqi businessman and banking investor Jawad Al-Kassab.

According to a statement released by the NIC, Chairman Adel Dakhil Mohammed al-Yasiri met with Al-Kassab and his investment partners to discuss potential in Iraq’s hospitality industry.

The preliminary concept is for the development of a hotel and residential complex on roughly 20 to 30 dunams of land, including hotel rooms, private villas, serviced residential units, and conference and event facilities.

The site has not been specified, and the project is still in the negotiation stage, with no development timeline or formal investment agreement declared.

Al-Kassab has vast expertise in international property development and hotel investment. He is the founder and chairman of Jawad Al Kassab International Holding Group, which has assets in the Middle East, Europe, and North America.

His portfolio includes the Kempinski Hotel Ishtar Dead Sea and Kempinski Hotel Aqaba in Jordan, as well as assets in Saudi Arabia, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Arab Emirates.

Within Iraq, Al-Kassab has participated in the Al-Kawthar residential development in Babil governorate, demonstrating his long-standing involvement in the country’s housing and building industries.

Aside from real estate and hospitality, Al-Kassab is also involved in Iraq’s financial industry as Chairman of the Board of Directors of Arab Bank Iraq, linking his investing operations to the growth of the country’s private banking sector.

The bank commenced operations as a private Iraqi shareholding business in 2025, following the receipt of its final banking license in 2024.

It has set up a headquarters in Baghdad’s Jadriyah area and announced intentions to grow its branch network and digital banking services.

If the Kempinski development goes forward, it will be another significant hospitality investment in Al-Kassab’s Iraq portfolio.

The NIC said that it was ready to assist and facilitate the project’s processes, as Iraq wants private investment in tourism, hotels, and supporting infrastructure.

World.title: Iraq, Qatar sign business cooperation agreement at Doha forum, plan joint business council
World.content:
Doha (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi and Qatari business executives convened in Doha on October 7 for the Qatar-Iraq Business Forum, where the chambers of commerce from both nations inked an agreement to boost trade and investment relations and form a joint business council.

The meeting, organized by Qatar Chamber, brought together members from the Federation of Iraqi Chambers of Commerce (FICC), government officials, and private-sector executives to examine investment potential in Iraq and ways to strengthen bilateral economic collaboration.

The two chambers signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to enhance institutional collaboration and facilitate commercial partnerships between Iraqi and Qatari enterprises.

The anticipated formation of the Iraq-Qatar Business Council is a key component of the agreement, with the goal of linking firms, discovering investment possibilities, and facilitating joint ventures.

The Iraqi delegation, headed by FICC President Amer Khalaf Alawi, comprised delegates from the International Chamber of Commerce in Iraq (ICC Iraq).

Chairman Mohsin Al-Hamid and Secretary General Ahmed Al-Yasiri represented the ICC Iraq delegation.

Other attendees were the Iraqi Prime Minister’s advisor on the Development Road and Railroads, the director general of the Ministry of Trade’s Private Sector Development Department, Iraqi business executives, and Iraq’s Ambassador to Qatar, Mohammed Jaafar Al-Sadr.

The forum included talks on bilateral commerce and Iraq’s Development Road project, which is a proposed transportation and logistics corridor that would link the Gulf with Turkish and European markets via Iraq.

The forum indicates a rising interest in improving Iraq-Qatar economic ties, especially as Baghdad attempts to attract Gulf investment, diversify its economy, and increase private sector activity.

The planned Iraq-Qatar Business Council might help transform conversations into long-term business partnerships.

World.title: Iraq’s SOMO begins settling outstanding oil payments to Gulf Keystone at international prices
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Gulf Keystone Petroleum announced on Thursday that Iraq’s State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) has begun compensating international oil companies operating in Iraq’s Kurdistan Region for outstanding oil export payments, taking a significant step toward resolving financial disputes affecting the region’s oil industry.

The London-listed business said the first cargo of extra crude oil, known as top-up barrels, was recently lifted after SOMO allocated them under the temporary tripartite export agreements comprising Baghdad, Erbil, and foreign oil companies.

Top-up barrels are extra amounts of crude oil delivered as compensation instead of direct cash payments. They enable oil corporations to recover the difference between the income previously earned for their exports and the amounts to which they are entitled under global market pricing.

In Gulf Keystone’s situation, the first allocation is designed to align oil export sales in the fourth quarter of 2025 with worldwide prices and begin to reduce the company’s outstanding receivables.

The move is a significant step toward completing payment agreements between the Iraqi Federal Government, the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG), and foreign oil corporations, whose financial conflicts have hampered northern Iraq crude exports and investment plans.

Gulf Keystone CEO Jon Harris welcomed the decision, citing the commencement of the compensation process as an important milestone for both the company and Iraq’s oil sector.

“The commencement of the top-up payments is a significant positive milestone,” Harris said.

He said that obtaining the company’s entire production-sharing contract entitlement at international rates was in line with Iraq’s modified federal budget legislation and current contracts.

Harris also praised Baghdad and Erbil’s commitment, saying it improved the investment prospects for Iraq’s oil industry.

Gulf Keystone added that it will continue to pursue collection of its remaining outstanding top-up receivables, since the first allocation does not constitute complete settlement of the sums owing.

The business expects the new payment system to spur more investment in the Shaikan oilfield in Iraq’s Kurdistan Region, where it hopes to develop significant oil reserves and resources.

The declaration provides an initial precedent for paying producers with more crude allocations; however, Gulf Keystone did not specify the amount of the first cargo or the entire remaining balance.

World.title: Why is Shell facing lawsuits over climate disasters in Brazil and the Philippines?
World.content:
Washington – A typhoon in the Philippines and flooding in Brazil. Twice in less than a year, British energy giant Shell has been the target of a new type of lawsuit seeking to make polluters pay part of the cost of specific extreme weather events.

“We chose Shell because it’s an emblematic company. It meets all the criteria,” Thales Miola, a lawyer for the Brazilian NGO Instituto Preservar, told AFP.

On Friday, the organization and federal prosecutors jointly filed a lawsuit against Shell’s subsidiary in South America’s largest country.

They are seeking the equivalent of $108 million in compensation for catastrophic flooding in southern Brazil in 2024. The disaster killed nearly 200 people, displaced half a million and caused widespread destruction.

Until now, the only lawsuits filed over the disaster had targeted public authorities.

Shell is not Brazil’s biggest oil company — that distinction belongs to state-owned Petrobras — but it has operated there for decades, and its contribution to global warming is well-documented and “a huge amount for a single company,” Miola said.

According to estimates by the think tank Carbon Majors cited in the lawsuit, Shell holds responsibility for 2.02 percent of global carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuel and cement-making.

Much of those emissions come from burning the hydrocarbons the company produces and sells. Shell’s share is more than three times that of Petrobras.

At the heart of the legal argument is an attribution study published in a journal belonging to the Nature group, which estimates that climate change intensified the extreme rainfall in 2024 by 12 percent.

The plaintiffs want Shell to pay for that additional intensity in proportion to its contribution to global emissions: two percent of the 12 percent increase.

“In Brazil, it is the first time that we use attribution science against a carbon major company,” Miola said. “Choosing Shell does not exempt the other companies from being prosecuted in the near future.”

– Super typhoon –

In the Philippines, too, the plaintiffs want Shell to pay for its history and its size.

In December 2021, Typhoon Rai, known locally as Odette, devastated several islands. More than 400 people died and hundreds of thousands lost their homes. It was one of the worst disasters in the country’s history.

Four years later, in 2025, around 100 survivors, supported by NGOs, filed a lawsuit against Shell in the United Kingdom, where the company is based.

The lawyers base their case on the company’s “historic carbon emissions” and the link between those emissions and global warming, which climate scientists have shown intensifies cyclones.

– Aggravating factor –

The plaintiffs cite an additional aggravating factor: Shell’s “history of misinformation regarding the causes and impacts of climate change,” said Greg Lascelles, a lawyer at Hausfeld, the firm handling the lawsuit in London.

“There’s a lot of evidence about Shell knowing as early as in the 1960s” that fossil fuels contributed to global warming, said Madeleine Lynch, a campaigner on the “Odette case.”

The lawsuit argues that this establishes negligence under Philippine law.

The Brazilian lawsuit also cites Shell’s past record, including an internal company report from 1986 that acknowledged fossil fuels’ role in increasing greenhouse gas emissions and global warming.

Shell has not responded to the Brazilian lawsuit. However, in December, following the Philippine lawsuit, the company said “the suggestion that Shell had unique knowledge about climate change is simply not true.”

– ‘Test cases’ –

Claims seeking compensation from major companies for specific climate-related damage — sometimes in countries where those companies are not even based — are only just beginning to emerge.

Swiss cement maker Holcim is being sued by residents of an Indonesian island being eroded by rising sea levels. Pakistani farmers are suing two companies in Germany, including a cement manufacturer.

“The cases we’re seeing in the world are test cases, to see whether it is a viable legal strategy,” said Noah Walker-Crawford, a researcher at the Grantham Research Institute on Climate Change and the Environment at the London School of Economics.

“If these cases are successful,” he said, “We could expect to see a lot more of these cases against more companies as well.”

World.title: Iraq to continue economic, financial reforms
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Finance Minister Faleh Sari reaffirmed on Wednesday Iraq’s commitment to continuing economic and financial reforms, diversifying revenue sources, and strengthening the role of the private sector.

According to Sari, these measures aim to bolster economic stability and enhance the country’s capacity to deal with regional challenges.

The Iraqi minister’s remarks took place during his speech at the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group, held in Bangkok, Thailand, according to a statement released by the Finance Ministry.

Sari emphasized that the government is addressing the economic consequences of the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz by reprioritizing expenditures, increasing non-oil revenues, and maintaining the state’s essential obligations while pursuing structural reforms.

According to Sari, overcoming current challenges requires a transition toward a more diversified and sustainable economy.

“Iraq Vision 2050” represents a strategic plan for reducing dependency on oil, broadening production, empowering the private sector, and achieving inclusive and sustainable economic growth, according to Sari.

The minister noted that the reform package includes enhancing public financial management, automating customs and tax operations, boosting the business and investment climate, upgrading the banking sector, and increasing electronic payment systems.

According to Sari, the partnership with the IMF and the World Bank Group supports the economic and financial reform program.

The minister highlighted the value of leveraging the technical and institutional expertise provided by these institutions to strengthen the sustainability of public finances and facilitate the implementation of Iraq’s development priorities.

World.title: UNDP chief sounds alarm on growing poverty after Iran war shock
World.content:
Bangkok – Millions could be thrown into poverty by surging energy costs, the impact of an intense El Nino phenomenon and higher interest rates, with vulnerable countries being pushed to the brink by repeated crises, the UN’s development chief told AFP.

Global fuel prices have soared since the United States launched its war on Iran in late February, with Tehran’s retaliations against Washington’s Gulf allies curtailing major oil and natural gas supplies.

Fiscal deficits and debt-to-GDP ratios around the world have ballooned since the 2008 global financial crisis, with governments firefighting against a series of shocks including the pandemic and wars in Ukraine and the Middle East.

Speaking on the sidelines of the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, UN Development Programme (UNDP) head Alexander de Croo said many developing countries had responded to the current spike in energy prices with blanket subsidies, but a succession of crises had left them with limited resources to keep that up.

“You have to repair your roof while at the same time your home is on fire,” he told AFP, adding governments in the developing world did not have time to rebuild buffers or resolve previous shocks before being hit by new crises.

The IMF warned this week that while global growth had held up in the face of the energy crisis, that resilience was highly dependent on the boom in AI technology investments, and poorer countries not exposed to that were still struggling.

IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva had warned that “winter is coming” — an allusion to popular fantasy book series “Game of Thrones” — implying that a cataclysm was around the corner if the world did not prepare for it.

And De Croo added: “Some countries have a well-insulated house with money in the bank. Other countries have a house without a roof and no money in the bank.

“We’re stumbling from one crisis into the other, and what countries need is some space, and some time, and access to financing.”

Not getting the response right could be devastating. The UNDP warned in a new report that about 130 million people were at risk of being pushed into poverty this year if energy and food price increases were fully passed on without subsidies.

People in South and East Asia and sub-Saharan Africa are at particular risk, the agency said.

– ‘Difficult to manage’ –

With advanced economies seeing bond yields surge — owing to elevated inflation expectations, surging debt ratios and AI capital-raising activities — global borrowing costs have been rising.

That in turn, de Croo warned, had tightened space for developing countries to access the capital they needed to combat the shocks, with rising interest rates feeding into increasing debt payments.

According to UNDP, the median developing country now spends about 9.5 percent of government revenue on interest payments — the highest in a quarter of a century, and more than three times that in high-income countries.

“It starts to be a difficult situation to manage, and it takes away all their margin for policy,” de Croo said.

The former Belgian prime minister said he would spend the week in Bangkok — where world economic policy leaders have gathered since Monday — pushing for advanced economies and multilateral agencies to invest in economic growth, resilience and job creation in the developing world.

He also said recent stark cuts in international aid were having an impact on those countries.

The UNDP warned there was potentially more pain to come, with this year’s El Nino climate phenomenon forecast to be the strongest on record.

That is expected to have widespread effects including flooding, droughts and other extreme events that are estimated to peak in early 2027.

De Croo also said private capital needed to step in to help fight some of the worst consequences of climate change.

“We see that the impact of climate has an economic cost. Avoiding that cost has a business case,” he said.

World.title: Tech stock lead rout after US inflation fuels rate hike bets
World.content:
Hong Kong – Asian stocks plunged Thursday as tech firms suffered another painful rout after forecast-topping US inflation data fuelled expectations the Federal Reserve will have to ramp interest rates higher.

Seoul and Tokyo again bore the brunt of the selling as traders bailed out of once-imperious chipmakers, though the selling was heavy across the region, tracking sharp losses on Wall Street.

Markets, already struggling with concerns about the outlook for the AI investment boom, were stung after data showed the US consumer price index hit 3.7 percent in September, sharply up from the previous month and more than the 3.6 percent forecast.

The reading is the highest in five months and was largely driven by the surge in energy costs caused by the more than seven-month Iran war, which saw Tehran effectively choke off the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global crude passed.

Gasoline costs accounted for more than half of the monthly CPI jump, surging 9.1 percent in September.

The figures will put pressure on the Fed to hike rates at least once more, following September’s lift, with the bank’s decision due on October 28, a week before the US midterm elections.

Bets on a second successive hike rose after the release. There is now a 37.1 percent chance officials will announce a 25-basis-point increase this month, according to CME Group’s FedWatch tool. The probability was around 22 percent before the data.

“This CPI report is a headache for the Fed, which had been indicating a willingness to pause this month,” said Neil Wilson at Saxo Markets, referring to several board members who had suggested they favoured a go-slow approach to assess last month’s lift.

“Markets too had all but priced out a hike later this month but repriced for the Fed to move a bit quicker after US inflation came in a little hotter than expected.”

– December lift ‘fully priced’ –

Pepperstone’s Chris Weston wrote: “Further evidence of right-tail inflation risk in the US has reinforced the higher-for-longer rates narrative, with sellers emerging across risk assets and interest rate-sensitive equities coming under renewed pressure.

“The breadth of price pressures across the CPI basket has been particularly concerning, challenging a market desperately in need of evidence of disinflation.”

He said “a December hike is now effectively fully priced”, adding that there was also a 66 percent probability of a January lift.

Tech firms — which rely on borrowing to fund their huge AI investments — led the losses Thursday, tracking their counterparts in New York.

Seoul’s Kospi dived more than seven percent, with SK hynix sinking more than 10 percent and Samsung more than nine percent.

And in Tokyo the Nikkei 225 shed more than four percent as Kioxia also dived more than 10 percent and Advantest plunged 12 percent. Tech investment titan SoftBank lost 9.5 percent.

Taipei lost almost three percent as market-heavyweight TSMC gave up around two percent.

The selling came after many tech firms had clawed back some of the huge losses sustained in a summer rout that came on the back of worries about elevated valuations and questions over when firms would see returns on their colossal investments.

Hong Kong, Shanghai, Singapore, Wellington, Manila and Jakarta were also deep in negative territory.

US government borrowing costs surged on the news, with 10-year Treasuries hitting fresh 24-year highs, though they later retreated on investor demand owing to their attractive yields above 5.3 percent.

The dollar gave back most of the gains sparked by bets on higher interest rates, while the yen was also helped by comments from Japan’s finance minister warning Tokyo was ready to step in with support.

World.title: Behind AI’s carbon footprint, a potential climate tool
World.content:
Paris – Artificial intelligence has become a lightning rod in climate debates over concerns about the growing carbon footprint of the data centres powering the technology.

The issue will be in the spotlight at the COP31 climate summit in Turkey next month, with the hosts saying they will push for “climate-responsible AI”.

But the discussion over the technology’s environmental impact — along with fears that it could pose an existential threat to humanity — has overshadowed its potential as a tool to combat climate change.

AI is being deployed in a broad range of applications, from improving weather forecasts to monitoring industrial emissions and optimising renewable energy.

Many of these applications are less energy-hungry than general-purpose language models such as OpenAI’s ChatGPT or Anthropic’s Claude, according to experts.

“Data centres have come in as a challenge… There are genuine concerns about what all of this could mean for the energy system, for the energy sector, for climate,” Siddharth Singh, an AI expert at the International Energy Agency (IEA), told AFP.

“At the same time, because (AI) is a tool, it’s an opportunity. It really comes down to how it is deployed,” Singh said.

– Renewables efficiency –

AI is already being used to make electricity grids more efficient in complex energy systems, helping operators manage the variability of solar and wind power.

The technology can produce localised forecasts of cloud cover, sunlight and wind, allowing companies to predict renewable output more accurately.

Singh said it can help limit the amount of “curtailment” — the practice of reducing certain types of electricity because the grid cannot handle it.

If deployed across the economy, from transport to industry and buildings, the technology could save 13.5 exajoules of energy by 2035, equivalent to Indonesia’s annual energy demand, according to the IEA.

Emissions reductions can be made, for example, by using AI to schedule a washing machine to run when solar electricity is abundant, Singh said.

WattTime, an environmental tech nonprofit, helps companies time their electric vehicles, phones or other devices to periods when the energy is coming from cleaner power sources.

“One of the things AI is very good at is forecasting,” WattTime co-founder Gavin McCormick said.

– Weather forecasting revolution –

AI is transforming weather forecasting by producing high-quality projections much faster, said Florian Pappenberger, director-general of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF).

“AI has really revolutionised weather forecasting in the sense that you can actually now predict weather much faster, with a really high skill and with a high performance,” Pappenberger told AFP.

He said AI forecasting is still grounded in physics-based models, while allowing the ECMWF to achieve in two years what would traditionally have taken 10 years to accomplish.

It is also much cheaper than traditional methods, enabling the ECMWF to produce more forecasts.

The technology can also improve early warning systems.

A Google system can forecast river floods up to seven days in advance in over 150 countries, according to the US tech giant.

Rather than replacing humans, Pappenberger said, “I think (AI) is more like giving us superpowers to be even better or do things even better than we ever did before.”

– Spotting emissions –

Satellites and AI are also used to spot greenhouse gas emissions from individual facilities such as oil and gas sites, mines or landfills.

An initiative co-founded by McCormick, Climate TRACE, harnesses the technology to track emissions around the planet and build an inventory of the pollutants.

“Climate TRACE is 20 years more advanced because of AI,” McCormick said.

“We have been able to provide emissions inventories to every city and a lot of them now can make a climate action plan,” he said. “Without AI this would not have been possible.”

– Oil AI –

But while AI could boost the efficiency and use of renewables, the technology has long been used by oil and gas companies to sift through geological data, identify underground reservoirs and streamline fossil fuel production.

“AI can also have a detrimental impact on climate change from that angle,” said Maria Joao Sousa, executive director of Climate Change AI, a nonprofit promoting the use of AI for climate action.

“AI will never be a silver bullet,” she said. “Technology itself will never be the solution alone.”

World.title: 'All for one man': CJP's Dipke targets Centre for sweeping curbs to stamp out anti-CEC protests
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (

) activist Abhijeet Dipke on Thursday accused the government of detaining protesters and even opposition leaders that include former chief ministers, just to save âone manâ, chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Addressing the media, Dipke said students, organisations, and the youth protesting for the past 10-15 days were being âdragged awayâ, while opposition leaders were detained too.

âFor the past 10-15 days, studentsâ organisations and the youth of Delhi have been out on the streets, being dragged away. When the Opposition joined them, they were detained too, including the leader of the opposition and former chief ministers like Mamata Banerjee, Arvind Kejriwal and Pinarayi Vijayan,â Dipke said.

âAll this for whom? For one man, Gyanesh Kumar,â he added.

Dipke further alleged that Railways services were suspended after the October 10 call, saying this was possibly the first time such a step had been taken in the countryâs history.

âThat wasnât enough, so they shut the Metro and closed stations across Delhi. For whom? Gyanesh Kumar. Still not satisfied, they brought in forces from Jammu and Kashmir,â he said.

Meanwhile, All India Students' Association leader and activist, Neha Bora, expressed solidarity with the media and criticised the authorities over the detention and alleged harassment of journalists.





Speaking at the press conference, Bora said journalists were detained for hours and even beaten, despite having their press cards.

âWe saw how cameras were snatched from journalists and they were told that they would not get the camera if they cover this,â she said.

World.title: Supreme Court issues notice on SIR petition, seeks records of EC decision-making
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday issued notice to the

(ECI), chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi on a petition filed by Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders alleging large-scale voter deletions and irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and justice Joymalya Bagchi sought responses from the poll panel and the other respondents, and tagged the plea with matters already pending before the court concerning SIR.

The petitioners have sought scrutiny of the ECIâs decision-making during the revision exercise, alleging that decisions were taken without adequate collective deliberation and that eligible voters were excluded without sufficient safeguards.

The plea seeks disclosure of official records, including files, minutes, notings and objections recorded by election commissioners, as well as access logs relating to the ECINET and ERONET electoral-roll databases.

The INDIA bloc leaders have also sought an independent audit of voter deletions, publication of booth-wise lists of deleted electors with reasons for their removal, and an effective mechanism to restore names deleted erroneously.





They have raised concerns over alleged changes to Form 6, which is used to enrol new voters, and sought safeguards against deletion without notice and an opportunity to be heard.

The petition does not seek to reopen the question of whether the ECI has the authority to conduct SIR, but challenges aspects of how the exercise has been implemented and the decisions taken in its course.

During the hearing, the CJI also expressed concern over the conduct of one of the petitioners during the INDIA blocâs October 12 march to the Supreme Court.

The march, led by Rahul, was organised to protest alleged electoral irregularities and demand Kumarâs resignation.

After lawyers raised objections to the procession, Surya Kant said nobody could âbrowbeatâ the judiciary. He added, âWe are not sitting in an ivory tower, we are aware of things.â

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The court clarified that issuing notice on the SIR petition did not amount to condoning the conduct of the political leaders during the march.

The CJI said the court wanted to question one of the petitioners about his conduct at the next hearing.

The march followed the CJIâs decision to decline a meeting sought by Gandhi and Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge to submit a memorandum on the SIR process and the functioning of the ECI. The CJI had said the issues were already pending before the court and advised the leaders to seek relief through judicial proceedings.

World.title: 'Growing concern over anti-India hate in US': MEA demands probe into Hindu temple attack plot
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Thursday voiced concern and demanded a probe over an alleged plot to target a Hindu temple in the US, saying the incident has heightened Indiaâs concerns over the "growing racist hostility and anti-India hate" in the United States.

Also Read |

The MEAâs remarks came after US law enforcement agencies arrested a 19-year-old man, identified as Alexandros Paporakis, following an investigation into threats of a potential mass shooting at a Hindu temple in Aurora, Illinois.

âWe are deeply concerned by reports of an alleged plot to carry out a mass shooting targeting a Hindu temple in the Aurora region of Illinois. The reported anti-Hindu and racist nature of the alleged plot, including references to violence against people of Indian origin, is particularly disturbing,â the MEA said in a statement.

âThis incident adds to growing concerns over racist hostility and anti-India hate in the US. There is a need for greater vigilance, zero tolerance for hate-motivated violence, and decisive action to ensure the safety and security of the Indian community,â it added.

The MEA further stated that India expected US authorities to thoroughly investigate the matter, bring those responsible to justice and take the necessary steps to prevent similar incidents in the future.





The alleged attack plot

According to the Palatine Police Department, which probed the alleged plot and arrested Paporakis, the investigation began on October 11, when it received information from the Mount Prospect Police Department about a possible mass shooting. The tip came from an individual who reported receiving âconcerningâ electronic messages from Paporakis.

Also Read |

Investigators found that Paporakis had shared a document outlining an alleged plan to carry out a mass shooting at the temple.

He had also circulated images of a rifle, rifle magazines, body armour and other tactical equipment.

Police arrested the suspect as he was leaving his home. A subsequent search of the residence yielded a rifle, several loaded rifle magazines, hundreds of additional rounds of ammunition, tactical equipment and other items linked to the investigation.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Among the recovered items was a tactical vest fitted with body armour and a patch displaying imagery associated with white supremacist extremism.

Detectives also examined electronic communications and a document attributed to Paporakis titled âWhy I Fought: A.K.A.: (Aurora Shooterâs Manifesto).â According to the police department, the document contained white supremacist and extremist views, including references to violence against people of South Asian heritage, particularly those of Indian descent.

Investigators believe Paporakis may have been planning an attack on October 11, potentially targeting a Hindu place of worship in the Aurora area. Following the probe, police contacted places of worship of the Hindu community within their jurisdiction to alert them to the reported threat.

World.title: 'Serious allegations': SC hears pleas on sexual harassment of women journalists, attacks on children among protest-related petitions
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

on Thursday directed the police not to take any coercive action against a woman journalist whose complaint alleging molestation is pending consideration before the court.

The apex court also directed all law enforcement agencies to preserve and submit CCTV footage of protest-related incidents after various counsels sought the material.

The direction came as the court heard pleas concerning the October 10 protests in Delhi, including allegations of harassment and manhandling of women journalists.

The bench, led by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant, said the allegations of harassment of women journalists were serious and sought the personal presence of a senior Delhi Police officer to explain the matter.

The court had earlier said it was aware of the allegations and had asked police officers present in court to inquire into them.

Senior advocate Indira Jaisingh, appearing in a plea alleging sexual harassment of women journalists during the protests, said she was willing to submit the names of the women concerned to the court in a sealed cover. She said the matter required sensitivity and needed to be dealt with appropriately.





Jaisingh said she was representing a woman who had been âvery badlyâ treated by a police officer. She alleged that the person accused of the assault had subsequently approached the

and filed a counter-atrocities complaint, with those proceedings now being heard there.

She said she would submit two reports to the Supreme Court in sealed covers, one containing the names of the alleged victims of harassment and the other listing persons recommended to head a committee to investigate the allegations.

The bench suggested that the committee should comprise predominantly former women judges and former IPS officers. Jaisingh sought a blanket direction in the matter, while Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre, said the issue should be considered after the police submitted its report. Jaisingh countered that people had the right to work as independent journalists.

Mehta said the definition of a journalist had become broad, with some people working as freelancers and others as âreel makersâ.

âWe donât know whoâs who, but no lady should be subjected to Harrasmentâ, he submitted, adding that the protection should extend to female police personnel as well.

The hearing also concerns petitions seeking contempt action against authorities for disobeying the Supreme Courtâs October 11 order, which had effectively lifted a âcomplete banâ affecting Delhi Metro and railway services and other civic services during the protests.

The court had granted the Centre an extension until Thursday to respond to these pleas, as well as a batch of petitions challenging alleged police detentions.

The petitions also raise allegations of attacks and assaults on children and peaceful protesters by certain goons, who were allegedly garlanded by supporters after being granted bail just a day after their arrest.

Mehta said the apologies tendered by the authorities before the court were in keeping with the procedure followed in contempt proceedings.

He also objected to media reports carrying headlines stating that the authorities had apologised for violating court orders.

The court responded, âWe are not taking cognisance of unconditional and unqualified apologies. Because of your submission, it will become qualified,â.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The proceedings are part of the courtâs consideration of four sets of matters linked directly or indirectly to the October 10 protests.

An FIR has been registered against Delhi Police ACP Vivek Bhagat following a complaint by a woman journalist accusing him of sexual harassment in connection with the October 3 incident. The allegations and claims in the FIR remain subject to investigation and judicial determination.

The FIR invokes Sections 221, 356(2) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with Sections 3(1)(p), 3(1)(q), 3(1)(r) and 3(1)(s) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. The Delhi High Court is scheduled to hear a plea seeking interim protection from arrest on Friday.

World.title: SC seeks Centre, Delhi Police response to plea challenging Jantar Mantar’s de-notification as protest site

on Monday sought responses from the Centre, Delhi government and

World.title: 'Consistently sides with those who exploit women': BJP targets Congress over Akoijam's dismissal from JNU
World.content:
NEW DELHI: BJP on Thursday attacked Congress over dismissal of its Inner Manipur MP, Angomcha Bimol Akoijam from Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) following an internal inquiry into sexual harassment allegations by female students.

Addressing reporters, BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj accused the Congress leadership of remaining silent on the issue and alleged that the party was siding with those accused of exploiting women.

âIt is highly unfortunate that the Congress party consistently sides with those who exploit women. When Bimal Akoijam, a sitting MP from the Congress party, sexually harassed 11 female students, JNUâs internal committee found that the complaints filed by these students against him were truthful and substantiated by facts.

Consequently, on October 9, 2026, Bimal Akoijam was dismissed from his position at JNU,â the BJP MP said.

âYet, there is an absolutely deafening silence from Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi, Kharge ji, and Sonia Gandhi... Today, under the guidance and leadership of our Mahila Morcha National President and fellow MP, Rupkumari Choudhary, we met with the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, Om Birla.... We appealed to the President, Droupadi Murmu.





Yesterday, a delegation met with the Chairperson of the National Commission for Women (NCW), Vijaya Rahatkar, and today, we submitted a memorandum to Om Birla.

We had a very productive discussion...â she added.

Earlier on Wednesday, Delhi Police has served a notice to Akoijam, asking him to join an investigation into the allegations. The notice comes days after police registered an FIR following a complaint forwarded by JNUâs chief security officer for necessary legal action, news agency PTI reported.

The documents submitted to the police included the universityâs dismissal order, the internal committeeâs inquiry report and its assessment of the allegations.

The FIR invokes provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) relating to sexual harassment and words, gestures or acts intended to insult a womanâs modesty. Police documents refer to an incident on May 6 and an unspecified period before that date.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Akoijam, a professor at JNUâs Centre for the Study of Social Systems under the School of Social Sciences, was dismissed with immediate effect on October 9 following an internal inquiry.

According to reports, several female students filed sexual harassment complaints against Akoijam in May. The allegations included claims that he invited students to his campus residence under the pretext of meetings or gatherings and attempted to sexually harass them. Some students also alleged that he made inappropriate remarks in class.

Akoijam has denied the allegations, describing the complaints as politically motivated. He has also challenged the universityâs account of the inquiry process.

World.title: Over 150 more 'Aam Aadmi Clinics' opened in Punjab: CM Bhagwant Mann
World.content:
Punjab chief minister

on Wednesday dedicated 154 new 'Aam Aadmi Clinics' to the people, taking the total to 1,244 in the state.

Mann asserted that his government's priority is to deliver quality healthcare, education and employment rather than indulge in "politics of slogans".

Addressing a public gathering at village Harkhowal in Chabbewal here, he highlighted over 6.48 crore OPD visits at the Clinics and healthcare coverage worth up to Rs 10 lakh for 54.20 lakh families, while warning that a change of government could put public welfare initiatives, including free bus travel for women and monthly financial assistance, at risk.

Assembly elections in Punjab are scheduled to be held early next year.

Launching a sharp attack on AAP rivals, Mann said that they want to shut down Aam Aadmi Clinics, the Mukh Mantri Sehat Yojna, Rs 1,000 monthly assistance for women and free bus travel, as they cannot digest the people-centric initiatives being implemented by his government.

Highlighting that the Mukh Mantri Sehat Yojna covers 54.20 lakh families and nearly 8 lakh beneficiaries have received treatment, he reiterated that his government's priorities are people's healthcare, children's education and youth employment, not slogan-driven politics.





Mann said today, 154 new Aam Aadmi Clinics have been dedicated to the people of Punjab.

With this, the total number of these Clinics in Punjab has reached 1,244.

He alleged that successive governments which ruled Punjab only looted the state.

Hitting out at rival parties, Mann said, "they may resort to any number of malicious tactics to defame us, but as long as I have the love and trust of the people, I have nothing to fear from them".

"The historic mandate given by the people of Punjab has placed a tremendous responsibility on our shoulders, and we are fulfilling our promises through concrete action. The difference between the previous governments and our government is clear.

"Earlier, power was treated as a means to benefit some families and select individuals, but today, governance revolves around the common people, their aspirations and their welfare.

The winds of development are blowing across Punjab, and no conspiracy by the opposition can stop this transformation," he said.

Launching a sharp attack on the opposition, he said that parties which had governed Punjab for decades were now struggling with internal divisions, a lack of credible leadership and an inability to present a constructive vision for the state.

Taking a dig at the Shiromani Akali Dal, Mann said, "The Akali Dal once claimed that it would govern Punjab for 25 years, but today it is struggling to maintain its political relevance..."

Criticising the Congress, he said, "Congress leaders are unable to present a united front even on matters concerning Punjab's future. Those who ruled Punjab for years and failed to fulfil the aspirations of its people are now unable to tolerate the work being done by AAP government.

They are joining hands against us because they have no credible agenda for Punjab, but the people of the state continue to stand firmly with us."

Mann said that the people of Punjab had rejected the politics of corruption, nepotism and personal enrichment and were now demanding accountable governance and tangible results.

"The previous Akali governments failed to protect Punjab's youth from the drug menace, while the sacrilege incidents inflicted a severe blow on the party's credibility among the people. The opposition must understand that people have rejected the politics of corruption, nepotism and personal enrichment.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

I appeal to the people to remain vigilant against attempts to mislead them. The trust and blessings of the people are our greatest political strength," he said.

Meanwhile, of the 154 more Aam Aadmi Clinics dedicated to the people of Punjab on Wednesday include 36 in Amritsar, 26 in Patiala, 17 in Ludhiana, 12 in Gurdaspur, 11 in Jalandhar and 10 in SAS Nagar (Mohali).

Mann reiterated that the expansion of Aam Aadmi Clinics, free medicines and diagnostic tests, and the Mukh Mantri Sehat Yojna were part of the state government's broader commitment to ensuring accessible and affordable healthcare for the people of Punjab.

World.title: 'Nobody can browbeat judiciary': SC issues notice to Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav and others over October 12 march

on Thursday issued notices to

, Samajwadi Party chief

and other protestors over their October 12 march to the apex court to protest alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

World.title: Anbumani seeks 30% Deepavali bonus for public sector workers
World.content:
Pattali Makkal Katchi (PMK) president Anbumani Ramadoss on Thursday (October 15, 2026) urged the Tamil Nadu government to immediately announce and disburse a 30% Deepavali bonus to workers in all State public sector undertakings, including temporary and outsourced employees.

In a statement, he said the government was yet to announce the bonus despite Deepavali falling on November 8. He said the maximum bonus had remained at 20% since 2004, with workers receiving between ₹7,000 and ₹16,800 based on a prescribed wage ceiling.

Arguing the amount was inadequate amid rising living costs, he urged the government to provide the same bonus rate to workers across all public sector undertakings, irrespective of their financial position or whether employees were permanent, temporary, or outsourced.

Citing the Union government’s announcement of a bonus equivalent to 78 days’ wages for railway employees, he said Tamil Nadu should not delay its decision further.

World.content: What does it take for a man to become a god? In North Keralam, Theyyam artistes undergo hours of rituals, makeup and transformation to embody deities. World.title: Liquor being consumed illegally in hotels on Shivamogga–Tirthahalli Road
World.content:
A team of Excise Department officials of Karnataka inspected hotels and dhabas in Shivamogga taluk and registered seven cases for allegedly allowing the illegal consumption of liquor.

On October 14, the team checked hotels on either side of the Shivamogga–Tirthahalli Road at Gajanur, Sakrebailu, and Mandagadde. They found hotel owners allowing customers to consume liquor while having food.

Deputy Commissioner of Excise K.S. Murali, who led the team, warned hotel-owners of legal action if they violate the law. Cases were booked under Sections 15(A) and 32(3) of the Karnataka Excise Act, 1986, for allowing consumption of liquor in unlicenced public places.

Cases were booked against Fish Land, Fish Hotel, Vanashree Hotel, Hotel Sakrebailu, Bhavani Hotel, Chinnu Hotel, and Tunga Hotel.

Mr. Murali said hotels and dhabas should not allow the consumption of liquor on their premises. Those who violate the law will face penal action, he said.

Officers of the Shivamogga and Sagar sub-divisions were part of the raids. They included Deputy Superintendents of Excise Noushad Ahmed Khan and Sheela Dharajkar.

World.title: Who is ACP Vivek Bhagat? Delhi cop accused of sexual harassment during protests
World.content:
Amid protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, an Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) is caught in the eye of a storm on the charges of sexual assault against women. Vivek Bhagat, presently posted as Sub-Divisional Police Officer (SDPO) in Connaught Place, has come under intense scrutiny after three women journalists accused the cop of sexually assaulting them during the recent CEC protests in Delhi.

Who is Vivek Bhagat

Vivek Bhagat, posted as SDPO in Connaught Place police station, is a 2018-batch IPS officer. Mr. Bhagat was among 12 DANIPS (Delhi, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Daman and Diu and Dadra and Nagar Haveli (Police) Service officers) assigned as the current duty charge of additional DCP.

After the sexual assault allegations were raised, the Delhi Police said three complaints have been received and have been transferred to the Crime Branch for inquiry on October 4.

Amid the row, the accused official, an Assistant Commissioner of Police rank officer, was promoted to the rank of Additional Deputy Commissioner of police on Monday (October 5) in an order signed by the Deputy Secretary (Home) Ramesh Kumar. ACP Bhagat subsequently requested that he not be given the current duty charge until a full enquiry into the allegations of harassment of women journalists was completed.

Several media reports also suggest that Mr. Bhagat was deployed for crowd control measures during the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protests in July, demanding the resignation of former education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

Women journalists’ allegations against Bhagat

On October 3, three women journalists alleged sexual harassment by police personnel, while they were reporting a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in Jantar Mantar. The trio demanded the Delhi Police to transfer their complaints to Crime Branch for an impartial enquiry, as per a PTI report.

In response, the New Delhi district police said it received complaints following the alleged incidents during the protest, when police personnel were deployed to maintain law and order. “The Crime Branch will examine the allegations and record statements of the complainants and other persons concerned as part of the enquiry”, the officer said.

A woman journalist told PTI that she and others subsequently went to a police station to lodge a complaint, but no FIR was filed.

“Police personnel were detaining protesters, and there were no women police personnel present at the spot. I asked ACP Vivek Bhagat of the Delhi Police about the absence of women police personnel, following which he sexually assaulted me and pushed me back,” she alleged.

Expressing ‘shock and dismay’ over the police’s treatment of women journalists covering the protests, the Press Club of India urged the Delhi Police to act on the complaint immediately.

“Behaviour of this kind cannot be normalised in a democracy. Journalists must be allowed to work freely, without fear, and document those who gather to raise various issues. That this is not being allowed even at the heart of the national capital does not bode well for the trajectory of media freedom in India,” it said in a statement.

“The Delhi Police must immediately act on the female journalist’s complaint and ensure that it gives media persons the space to do their jobs without having to face aggression and threats,” it added.

Bhagat’s request to keep the order on hold

Following the allegations, Mr. Bhagat has written to Delhi Police Chief, asking to keep the order concerning him on hold until the completion of the enquiry.

In a letter addressed to Commissioner of Police Anurag Kumar on Wednesday (October 7, 2026), he wrote, “However, considering the enquiry pending against me in the Crime Branch Delhi Police regarding allegations against me by a YouTuber, I hereby give my consent to keep this order concerning only me on hold”.

The government also clarified that the proposal to confer the additional duty charge on the 12 officers, including Mr. Bhagat was initiated on August 25, “much before the present set of events”, and the orders were issued after due approval on October 5.

Following the crime branch enquiry, the government subsequently said the earlier order would be modified and reissued for assignment of the charge to the remaining 11 officers.

World.title: Vizianagaram seeks shift of Mayor poll to October 29 over Sirimanotsavam
World.content:
The Vizianagaram District Collector and Superintendent of Police have asked the State Election Commission (SEC) to move polling in the Vizianagaram Municipal Corporation from October 28 to October 29 because of the Pydithalli Ammavari Sirimanu Utsavam.

Polling in the corporation is scheduled for October 28 along with 99 other urban local bodies, for which the election notification was issued on October 14.

In a letter to the SEC, Collector S. Ramsundar Reddy and SP A.R. Damodar sought the change so that the elections could be conducted free from the burden of the festival on October 27, which draws a huge number of devotees from across Andhra Pradesh and some parts of the neighbouring States, according to an official release.

The Sirimanotsavam of Goddess Pydithalli Ammavaru is preceded by the Vizianagaram Utsavam on October 25 and 26. The corporation will elect its Mayor and 62 corporators. As many as 2,23,050 voters are to cast their votes at 229 polling booths in the city, of which the police have identified 81 as very sensitive.

On Wednesday, Mr. Ramsundar Reddy had told The Hindu that the district administration had sufficient experience in handling important programmes simultaneously. Officials had been directed to cancel leave and make staff work on holidays if necessary.

World.title: Applications open for Kanavu Aerial Workshop for women photographers in Tamil Nadu
World.content:
Chennai Photo Biennale Foundation’s Kanavu Fellowship and Kala Collective, in partnership with Chennai Drone Academy, invite applications for the Kanavu Aerial Workshop. The 10-day residential programme is set to take place in Chennai in February next year and is open to women photographers aged 18 and above from across Tamil Nadu.

The programme brings technical training and visual storytelling together. The first six days will focus on drone flying and training towards DGCA Remote Pilot Certification. The remaining four days will focus on aerial photography and videography, allowing participants to develop their own images and videos for their portfolios.

The workshop offers women photographers an opportunity to expand their practice and learn skills they can bring to future creative and professional work. Preference will be given to previous Kanavu Fellowship participants, Kala Collective members, and applicants from low-income or marginalised backgrounds.

The fee is ₹30,000 and includes training, hostel accommodation and DGCA certification. Participants can pay in two instalments. Fully funded places are available for those who cannot afford the fee. Applicants may also choose to contribute ₹60,000, covering their own participation and supporting a scholarship place for another woman.

The workshop will take place at Chennai Drone Academy in Edapalayam, Chennai. Hostel accommodation and vegetarian meals will be provided for participants staying on campus. Final dates will be confirmed by mid-December based on selected applicants’ availability.

Applications close on 30 November 2026. For details, WhatsApp 9940046599, visit them on Instagram @chennaiphotobiennale

World.title: Women’s seats in Kadapa, Pulivendula draw leaders’ spouses, Jagan’s aunt into the fray
World.content:
The posts of Kadapa Municipal Corporation Mayor and Pulivendula municipality Chairperson are reserved for Women (General), bringing women to the fore in these urban local bodies.

Considered the fortress of the Congress in the past and the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) later, the two seats were held by YSR family loyalists in the past.

The YSRCP has fielded Y.S. Prameelamma, wife of Y.S. Manohar Reddy and aunt of former Chief Minister and Pulivendula MLA Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy, as its candidate for Chairperson of Pulivendula.

The choice is considered a tested and safe bet for the YSRCP. The TDP-led alliance has criticised it, saying the family-based party could not look beyond traditional options to benefit loyalists.

The TDP has fielded Thugutla Geetha Kumari, spouse of party loyalist Thugutla Madhu.

The TDP is on a high after winning the Pulivendula ZPTC seat last year. Its candidate, Mareddy Latha Reddy, is the wife of party strongman B.Tech Ravi alias Mareddy Ravindranath Reddy. TDP MLC Bhumireddy Ramagopal Reddy, who also hails from Pulivendula, is keen on winning the seat too.

YSRCP MP Y.S. Avinash Reddy has begun campaigning for the party candidate to retain the seat, which is the family’s home ground.

The deployment of bouncers around Mr. Avinash Reddy has become a point of ridicule for TDP leaders. Mr. Ravi mocked the YSRCP leader for considering “safety first” for “having failed to bring in development” to the constituency despite the family holding fort for over four decades.

NDA undecided on Kadapa

For the Kadapa Municipal Corporation, which is held by the YSRCP, the party has chosen Bandi Deepthi, spouse of former Deputy Mayor Bandi Nityananda Reddy.

Party workers celebrated when the party’s district president P. Ravindranath Reddy, Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy’s maternal uncle, announced her candidature.

But the NDA is yet to decide on its candidate because the TDP and the Jana Sena Party (JSP) are both said to be claiming the seat.

It is learnt that the JSP is staking a claim to the Mayor’s seat of either the Tirupati or Kadapa corporation, so the decision on this seat will depend on the outcome of the more seriously contested Tirupati seat.

World.title: ‘Jailer 2’ movie review: Rajinikanth’s flourishes elevate Nelson’s rousing herogasm
World.content:
Over the last two decades, numerous filmmakers have attempted to make the defining superstar film. While 2010s films, like Petta, celebrated Rajinikanth in all his glory, the demands of the pan-Indian cinema market and a more action-weary, fidgety audience in the post-streaming era have reshaped what makes a quintessential Rajini film in the 2020s. Director Nelson’s 2023 hit Jailer understood that formula (even if it was far from perfect) so intrinsically that it wouldn’t be far-fetched to call this style of mass masala filmmaking a definitive sub-genre tailored for its larger-than-life superstar.

The allure of the first Jailer film might seem straightforward at first — it had a Baashha-esque no-frills plotline peppered with fan service and cameos from stars across the Indian film industry. But what truly worked in its favour was how on-brand it was for Nelson; other than banking on the dark humour he is known for (and Breaking Bad-inspired ideas), Jailer was a pitch-perfect union of Nelson’s penchant for underplaying the protagonist and modern-day Rajinism, which requires sober storytelling and verisimilitude. All shenanigans transpire only around the titular Jailer, Tiger Muthuvel Pandian. While Rajini thrives in narratively earned moments of heroism, the villains and secondary characters do much of the heavy lifting, both in narrative and in mass elevation.

In Jailer 2, Nelson almost perfects this masala cinema formula. The prescription once again has invisible snipers punctuating the screen on cue like a well-placed Anirudh Ravichander motif, crowds of henchmen getting reduced to a pool of flesh and blood in minutes, and amidst all of that, Tiger Muthuvel Pandian going about his life as if he isn’t the man who is already plotting Plan Z. And Nelson doesn’t wish to hide that he’s working with the template — the sequel begins with a carbon-copy scene that kickstarted the first film. Dhileep (Suraj Venjramoodu), furious that he is unable to find the man who murdered his friend Varman (Vinayakan; the character died at the end of Jailer), tortures and kills his own men for their incompetence. Of course, a bigger whale, Bodhi Kalpak (SJ Suryah), is breathing down Dhileep’s neck to get the job done.

Meanwhile, our man-with-a-past lives a quiet life in a hillside town with his wife (Ramya Krishnan), their grandson Rithvik and their daughter-in-law (Mirnaa Menon). A chance encounter with a local municipality officer cascades into trouble, which is when you realise that Dhileep wasn’t the one searching for Jailer; Jailer had been fishing for the statue-smuggling syndicate all along.

Jailer 2 (Tamil) Director: Nelson Cast: Rajinikanth, SJ Suryah, Vidya Balan, Shivarajkumar Runtime: 165 minutes Storyline: A retired jailer is forced to confront his violent past when a new threat puts his still-grieving family in danger

Nelson takes pleasure in making the plot revolve around Rajini. In a spectacular scene set on a bridge, Muthuvel shows what he could do with just a slight move of his glasses. But theatre halls are bound to erupt when this tiger roars — like in a rousing scene inside a tea shop in which Nelson goes the traditional route to unleash ‘saviour Rajini.’

Now, Rajini doing Rajini should hardly surprise one, and Jailer 2 fabulously comes into its own in the interstices between these moments. An in-form Nelson works humour with such precision and conviction that you almost wish these characters (most of whom are played by Nelson regulars) appeared more often. In the first Jailer film, Yogi Babu’s Vimal played the innocent stooge who fell for Muthuvel’s ‘family man’ act and, when he realised what was happening, was already into the thick of it. Vimal’s counterpart in the sequel is Namo Narayana’s Moorthy, and every scene with him leaves you in splits. In fact, the scenes featuring Moorthy, Vimal and Bjorn Surrao’s character might single-handedly carry Jailer 2 over the mark.

Humour is one thing, but Nelson seems to have retained and improved aspects that were effective in the first film. Beyond all of its sensational beats, Jailer was also a unique family drama about a man who is forced to kill his own son. And Jailer 2 takes off from this emotional core and weaves a strong sentimental arc that anchors the storyline — especially in the second half, where the film follows its larger ambitions. At the very beginning, we see Muthuvel and his family still recovering from Arjun’s death, with the latter’s wife seeming to be the most affected. Protecting the family — who are already vulnerable — becomes Muthuvel’s paramount concern. But Muthuvel (interestingly, the audience too) seems to have forgotten a key detail from the first film that hits home, and nothing prepares you for this moment when it arrives.

This is also why Jailer 2 doesn’t seem like a cash grab banking on its predecessor’s glory; it’s a proper sequel written with intent. If not for plot points, many little pleasures — like a character taking a tissue at a specific moment or one in which a weapon hidden under a vehicle’s seat is used — find great callbacks in the sequel.

ALSO READ: Rajinikanth’s ‘Jailer 2’ special pan-India appearances: Who is the pick of the lot?

Similarly, Shivarajkumar, whose cameo in Jailer single-handedly boosted its theatrical run, finds more narrative purpose in the sequel. Jailer finally resembles a fictional world where these superstars are simply friends. Speaking of cameos and world-building, Mohanlal and Jackie Shroff, unfortunately, get even less screen space this time, but one special cameo in the second half by a former co-star of Rajinikanth guarantees a herogasm. Vidya Balan’s Kantha Kalpa doesn’t make much of an impression, though the character shows future promise.

And one can only call Jailer 2 an almost perfect version of the formula, except for a few niggles. The film could have done without the two item dance sequences; the first one (‘Ala Bolelo’) hinders the film’s momentum, and the song, too, feels like a sore spot in Anirudh’s otherwise satisfying album. Post-intermission blues plague the sequel as well; a scene set at a birthday party in Goa looks effective on paper but loses steam in execution.

But all these complaints hardly spoil what is otherwise a smooth, entertaining film. And watching an ensemble of stars play ball for a 75-year-young superstar is simply superb — as the dialogue goes, “frame-ah paarunga ji.” After 172 films, Rajinikanth owning the frames is old news, but watching the increasingly frail, ageing star give his all in every scene — and still with his signature swag and style — is surely inspiring (Neelambari’s dialogue comes to mind). But, as has been the case with Rajini films of late, Jailer 2 also reminds you that the superstar can no longer fight, dance, and move like before. This film, for instance, doesn’t feature him dancing at all, and one wonders if this is the Rajinikanth — one who has to underplay his strengths — we might see for the rest of his career.

Jailer 2 ends with a hint at a possible third film. Whether the Jailer template could sustain one more film, we can’t say yet. After all, before the first Jailer film, audiences had written off Nelson as a one-trick pony. But Jailer 2, especially, is proof of a serious filmmaker at the helm, who is also, incidentally, the funniest. Spotting this talent and trusting him to direct such a massive project — not once but twice — is another move only Rajini can make. In thalaivar we believe.

Jailer 2 is currently running in theatres

World.title: Teacher, 32 students killed in Peshawar school roof collapse
World.content:
PESHAWAR: At least 33 people, including 32 students and a female teacher, were killed when a school roof collapsed in the provincial capital’s Afridi Abad area on Thursday.

Lady Reading Hospital (LRH) spokesperson Muhammad Asim told Dawn that the death toll had risen to 33 from an earlier figure of 28. The deceased included 32 students aged between seven and 14 and a female teacher, he said.

A total of 20 injured children were also brought to the hospital, most of whom have since been discharged. Three children who sustained serious head injuries remained under treatment, he added.

Speaking to Geo News, Peshawar Deputy Commissioner Afaq Wazir confirmed that the rescue operation launched after the collapse had concluded.

“Rescue teams have cleared all the debris, and no more injured children are at the scene,” he said.

Residents gather during a search operation after a roof collapsed at a school in Peshawar on October 15. —AFP

Following the incident, an emergency was declared at the hospital, said the LRH spokesperson in an earlier statement.

Peshawar DC earlier told Dawn that the roof of Al-Khair School had collapsed, trapping students beneath the debris. According to a statement issued by his office, students were present in their classrooms when the incident occurred.

A rescue official told AFP that the ceiling came down on the students after the roof of a higher floor collapsed, crumpling the two storeys. Peshawar Capital City Police Officer (CCPO) Dr Mian Saeed Ahmed said the building’s structure was weak.

“Its roof was overweight with construction on a weak structure that caused the collapse,” AFP quoted him as saying.

Speaking to Dawn, Samiullah, a parent who rushed to the site after hearing about the incident, said he had rescued three girls, all under the age of eight.

“I received a call from home at around 8:50am and reached the site about 10 minutes later, at around 9am. We have six children studying at the school,” he said.

“When I saw the building, I thought my son, who was in a ground-floor classroom beneath the collapsed first floor, had also died. However, he had left the classroom to drink water,” he added.

KP governor orders audit

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi expressed grief over the deaths in the school roof collapse and sought a detailed report on the incident. He also directed the authorities to determine the cause of the collapse.

“The loss of precious lives of innocent children is an extremely painful tragedy,” he said, according to a statement, extending his heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families.
